articleTitle: DL-YOLOv8: Improved YOLOv8 for Cable Sheath Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the task of cable sheath defect detection, traditional detection methods face challenges of low detection accuracy due to multi-scale transformations of damaged targets and susceptibility to background interference. To address this issue, this paper proposed DL- YOLOv8, an algorithm specifically designed for cable sheath defect detection. Firstly, since cable sheath defects exhibit distinct edge features, a Gradient Attention (GA) module is constructed to focus the model's attention on the damaged target areas. Secondly, a new loss function, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta_{-}\text{IoU}$</tex>, is designed to optimize the model's localization performance for elongated damaged targets by using a parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> to assign different sensitivities to the length and width penalty terms in the E IoU loss function. On our self-built dataset, compared to the original YOLOv8 model, DL- YOLOv8 improves the performance metrics AP50 and AP75 for cable sheath defect detection by 4.7% and 11.8%, respectively. The improved algorithm demonstrates higher accuracy and better localization, making it more suitable for the task of cable sheath defect detection.

articleTitle: Difference in Inductance Between Integer Slot and Fractional Slot THMF-PC-PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to investigate the difference in inductance parameters of the third-harmonic-magnetic-field-based pole-change permanent magnet synchronous motors (THMF-PC-PMSMs) with different winding types, this paper analyzes these parameters before and after the change of pole. Initially, this paper introduces the theory of THMF-PC-PMSMs with field-weakening and speed regulation, and then calculates the magnetic potential of the THMF-PV-PMSMs before and after the change of pole. Under ideal conditions, this paper analyzes the inductance parameters of both integer-slot centralized winding and typical fractional-slot centralized winding. A 10-pole, 12-slot is selected as a typical fractional-slot centralized winding to be discussed. Comparative analysis reveals that the inductance change in the 10-pole 12-slot is more significant than in the integer-slot after the pole change.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Risk Assessment and Strategy Analysis of Overhead Transmission Lines Based on Analytic Hierarchy Process
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To address the uncertainty and destructive potential of natural disasters, the risk assessment of overhead transmission lines is crucial. To comprehensively quantify the operational risks of overhead transmission lines under natural disaster conditions, a comprehensive model for quantifying risks has been developed. This model considers probabilities of risk occurrence, impacts of risk consequences, and severity levels of hazards caused by various natural disasters. Subsequently, the analytic hierarchy process was employed to calculate risk weights for overhead transmission lines under multiple natural disaster scenarios, establishing a corresponding hierarchical structure of risk weights. This method enables the evaluation of overhead line risks under various natural disaster conditions, confirming the feasibility of the approach. It effectively and reasonably assesses the impact levels of different natural disasters on overhead transmission lines, providing a comprehensive and systematic analysis of operational risks.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Direct-hanging Cascaded Energy Storage Converter Based on Power-current Control
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: A direct-hanging cascaded energy storage converter based on power-current double-loop control is studid in this paper, including the design of the energy storage converter and the power-current double-loop control strategy. The design parameters are determined and optimized through comprehensive analysis of Matlab/Simulink simulations. Furthermore, a low-voltage direct-mounted stage Fed converter system platform is constructed and tested, a good agreement is observed between the simulations and measurements, effectively validates the design of the direct-hanging cascaded energy storage system based on power-current double loop control, and its effectiveness in control and adjustment of the active and reactive powers in real time.

articleTitle: Electricity Price Prediction Method with Multi- Time-Segmented Models Based on Load Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the context of spot trading in the electricity market, accurate electricity price forecasting is crucial for market participants to formulate optimal trading strategies. Electricity price fluctuations are driven by supply and demand dynamics, and price behaviors exhibit distinct volatility characteristics across different load segments. This paper proposes a load factor-based multi-model forecasting approach that segments the day into specific time periods to enhance the accuracy and reliability of day-ahead multi-step price predictions. Firstly, the relationship between day-ahead electricity prices and bidding space is analyzed from the perspective of power producers' bidding strategies, anchored in the electricity price formation mechanism. Secondly, leveraging price autocorrelation analysis and load factor indicators, various time segmentation methods are proposed and applied to the dataset. Finally, using actual data from Guangdong province, the proposed method is compared with traditional time series forecasting methods under different time segmentation strategies. The study demonstrates that the load-segmented multi-model forecasting approach significantly improves the accuracy and reliability of electricity price predictions while providing robust economic interpretability.

articleTitle: Theoretical Modeling and Experimental Verification of AC Resistance in Large Cross-Section XLPE Single-Core Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In recent years, the electric power industry has experienced rapid development, driving continuous expansion in the scale of power systems. In these systems, large-section conductors are responsible for crucial functions such as transmitting current, grounding protection, and busbar connections. Due to the skin effect, the alternating current (AC) resistance of large-section high-voltage cable conductors is significantly higher than their direct current (DC) resistance. This not only reduces the current-carrying capacity of the cables but also increases line losses, making accurate measurement of the AC resistance of large-section conductors critical. Most existing studies consider the AC resistance of cables under fundamental wave conditions; however, the widespread use of nonlinear loads has significantly increased the harmonic content in transmission lines. The impact of harmonics on additional losses in large-section cables is substantial and cannot be ignored. The calculation formulas in the IEC-60287 standard are only applicable to solid copper rods with cross-sections up to 1600 mm 2, and the current and voltage phasor measurement method it employs cannot directly calculate the AC resistance of large-section conductors under non-sinusoidal conditions, introducing certain errors. This paper first constructs a finite element simulation model for a 630 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> large-section cable conductor and calculates its AC resistance through simulation. Subsequently, an experimental testing platform for the AC resistance of large-section cable conductors was established, and the active power method based on electrical measurement was used to calculate the AC resistance. The experimental results, which are highly consistent with the simulation data, confirm the validity of the model, providing an important reference for measuring the AC resistance of large-section cables under harmonic conditions.

articleTitle: Switching Excitation Controller for Transient Stability of Multi-Machine Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper proposes a switching excitation controller to enhance the transient stability of multi-machine power systems. The switching excitation controller (SEC) consists of a conventional excitation controller (CEC), a bang-bang excitation controller (BEC), and a state-dependent switching strategy. Moreover, the SEC switches between the CEC and the BEC based on the switching strategy. The BEC is designed as a second-order bang-bang funnel controller, which can quickly switch the excitation voltage between the upper and lower limit values. To verify the performance of the proposed controller, simulation studies are undertaken in a 10-generator 24- bus power system, which includes the case of a three-phase-to-ground fault. The results reveal that the SEC can achieve the goal of transient stability enhancement.

articleTitle: RTU Upfrequency Reconstruction Based on Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to solve the frequency compatibility problem between some node phasor measurement unit (PMU) data and remote terminal unit (RTU) measurement data, a RTU upfrequency reconstruction method based on SRResN et deep learning network was proposed. First, the time series data is converted into electrical data images. Secondly, we propose a data image super resolution residual network (SRResNet) model and use the data image to train the SRResN et model. Finally, the SRResNet model based on training reconstructs RTU low frequency data into high frequency data to realize data fusion. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the simulation analysis of the load disturbance on the IEEE39-node system.

articleTitle: Effects of Heat and Moisture Transfer on Stray Current Distribution in Soils with Different Salt Contents
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to study the variation of stray current in urban rail transit with soil heat and moisture transfer, and analyze the influence of soil moisture content and temperature on stray current density at different depths, an experimental platform for stray current distribution in urban rail transit was built. The temperature and water content of soil at different depths were tested, and the variation of soil temperature and water content at different depths was analyzed. The results showed that the temperature and water content changed significantly in shallow soil. At the same time, the stray current density values at different depths were tested. The results showed that the stray current density decreased with the increase of depth in both single salt and mixed salt soils. The current density values of Cl<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup> containing single salt and mixed salt soils were significantly higher than those of SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-</sup> and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2-</sup> containing soils. The conclusions of the study can provide some theoretical guidance for the safe operation and maintenance management of urban rail transit.

articleTitle: Stability of Inverters Under Droop Control in Lossy AC Microgrids with Inductive-Resistive Load
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper analyzes the steady-state condition of frequency synchronization of inverters under droop control in a lossy AC microgrid with inductive-resistive loads. Firstly, the active power control equation of inverters with load impedance under droop control is established, and then the irrationality of the kuramoto model is illustrated. Secondly, stability condition for the frequency synchronization of inverters under droop control in lossy AC microgrids with inductive-resistive loads is derived. Finally, the proposed condition in this paper are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Distributed Collaborative Control of Reconfigurable Battery Energy Storage Based on Consensus Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To enhance the high-reliability operation capability of reconfigurable battery energy storage systems, a distributed cooperative control method of reconfigurable battery energy storage based on consensus algorithms is proposed in this paper, which can improve the frequency and power characteristics of the system. Firstly, the mathematical model of virtual synchronous generator(VSG) control, the structure of reconfigurable battery energy storage system, and the parallel VSG distributed architecture are introduced; Secondly, combined with the mathematical model of VSG control, the overall scheme of frequency recovery and power output reasonable distribution of VSG parallel system is designed; Then, according to the structural characteristics of reconfigurable battery energy storage, a battery pack reconfiguration strategy is proposed, which can meet the power output demand through the free combination of battery packs; Finally, a simulation model is built in Matlab/Simulink environment, and the simulation results verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation Study on Buoy Structure for an Oscillating Buoy Wave Energy Generation Device
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Wave energy, as an environmentally friendly and sustainable energy source, possessed substantial development potential and held significant application value in the domain of new energy technologies. To enhance the capture efficiency of wave energy, a novel oscillating buoy-type wave energy generation device was designed. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) method was applied to numerically simulate the hydrodynamic performance of the wave energy generation device, providing a theoretical foundation for optimizing the design of wave energy generation devices. Firstly, the paper investigated the impact of buoy shape on its hydrodynamic characteristics. The result indicated that buoy with a circular bottom adapted better to harsh sea conditions than those with a conical bottom. Secondly, a hole was made at the center of the circular oscillating buoy, and the CFD software Star-CCM+ was used to numerically simulate the hydrodynamic performance of the buoy with openings. This paper considered different aperture sizes of the buoy under two sets of different conditions, including 200mm, 400mm, 600mm and 800mm. Based on the numerical simulation results, through statistical analysis, the oscillating force and oscillating motion amplitude data of the oscillating buoys with different apertures were obtained, covering the maximum, minimum, variance, and mean deviation values for each aperture size of the buoys. Thirdly, taking a buoy with an aperture radius of 600mm as an example, the corresponding maximum PTO damping coefficient was calculated, and the average power were derived. Through statistical analysis of the hydrodynamic performance and power calculation of an oscillating buoy, the following conclusions could be drawn: Under the same operating conditions, choosing a circular-bottom buoy could improve its stability and adaptability in harsh sea conditions. The oscillating buoy with a 200mm aperture exhibited the largest maximum oscillating force, while the buoy with an 800mm aperture demonstrated the smallest maximum oscillating force. As the aperture size increased, the oscillating force and amplitude generally exhibited a fluctuating decrease. By taking a buoy with a 600mm aperture as an example, the calculated maximum PTO damping coefficient and the corresponding average power indicated that the choice of aperture size in buoy design significantly impacted energy capture efficiency and power output.

articleTitle: Decoupling Control with Kalman Filter for Quad-Active-Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Conventional decoupling control can effectively manage voltage regulation in quad-active-bridge (QAB) converter, however, the equivalent inductance in QAB converter will perturbate due to changing operation frequency and environmental temperature, which inevitably impacts the voltage control performance of conventional decoupling control. To address this issue, this article proposes a decoupling matrix-based PI method integrated with Kalman filter to eliminate the parametric effect on voltage control. The feasibility and benefits of the proposed control method is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: A Commutation Torque Ripple Suppression Strategy for Brushless DC Motor Based on an Improved Zeta Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid advancement in the field of automation, the control precision requirements for brushless DC motors in electromechanical equipment are continuously increasing. To address the issue of commutation torque ripple in current brushless DC motors, this paper proposes a suppression strategy by integrating an improved Zeta converter into the brushless DC motor driver. During the commutation process, the improved Zeta converter operates in boost mode, adjusting the DC bus voltage to match four times the back electromotive force amplitude. This effectively reduces commutation torque fluctuations. During non-commutation periods, the connection of a capacitor in the circuit structure of the Zeta converter to the DC bus results in the input voltage of the three-phase bridge being higher than the DC power supply voltage, which helps reduce the required rating of the DC power supply. Comparative simulation analysis verifies that this method effectively suppresses commutation torque ripple in the brushless DC motor and significantly enhances the performance of the motor driver.

articleTitle: PMSM Control Strategy Based on SVDGHCKF
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the study of sensorless control strategies for PMSM, this paper proposes a generalized higher-order cubature Kal-man filtering algorithm based on singular value decomposition, to address the limitations of the traditional CKF observer's low observation accuracy and filter divergence. The algorithm tries to improve the PMSM's control performance. First, this work establishes an accurate mathematical model of the PMSM as a research foundation. The classic CKF algorithm's observation accuracy is then greatly improved by introducing the fifth-order spherical radial volume criterion, which raises the observation ac-curacy to the fifth-order level. Meanwhile, to address the filter dispersion issue, this research uses the SVD decomposition to replace the Cholesky decomposition in the classic CKF. Finally, the research indicates that the control strategy can achieve high-precision control of the speed and angle of the permanent magnet synchronous motor, which effectively improves the control performance of the PMSM.

Author Keywords: Generalized Higher-order cubature Kalman filtering algorithm based on singular value decomposition

articleTitle: Bifurcation Analysis of Inverter-Based Microgrids Using Poincaré Map Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The integration of numerous power electronic inverters into AC microgrids has introduced strong nonlinear dynamic characteristics. This poses challenges to the accuracy and effectiveness of traditional linearization analysis methods. Therefore, this paper conducts a nonlinear dynamic stability analysis of inverter-based microgrids using Poincaré map theory, specifically focusing on bifurcation behavior analysis. First, we develop state-space models for each component of the microgrid and construct a complete system dynamic model based on their input-output relationships. Then, by using Poincaré map theory, we derive the system periodic map equation and obtain an explicit expression for its Jacobian matrix. By analyzing the evolutions of the Jacobian matrix's eigenvalues and bifurcation diagrams, we comprehensively investigate the impacts of droop control parameters on the system's nonlinear dynamic behaviors, like Neimark-Sacker bifurcation. Finally, time-domain simulations validate the accuracy of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Measurement of Electromagnetic Radiation Characteristics of Potential Transfer Arc in 10kV Live Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In a 10kV live operation environment, the arc and its generated electromagnetic radiation pose potential risks to operation personnel, equipment, and the surrounding environment. In order to comprehensively understand information such as the intensity, frequency, and radiation scope of the arc, and provide necessary guarantees for safe operation, a measurement method for the electromagnetic radiation characteristics of the potential transfer arc in 10kV live operation is studied. A calculation model of potential transfer transient response is established to obtain the potential at the equipotential steady state. Based on this potential value, the current change frequency corresponding to the peak value of the electromagnetic radiation spectrum under the direct current arc situation is obtained, and the electromagnetic radiation characteristics of the arc are measured. The test results show that the optimal distance for potential transfer is 45cm-55cm. The maximum value of the electromagnetic radiation pulse spectrum is almost consistent with the calculation. At the same time, the change laws of the transfer current pulse and the arc electromagnetic radiation pulse are the same. When the frequency is between 150MHz-250MHz, a concentrated distribution of electromagnetic radiation appears, with the maximum value occurring in the 200MHz frequency region.

articleTitle: A Single-Pole Grounding Fault Line Selection Method for Full DC Offshore Wind Farm Based on Zero-Mode Information Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the development of offshore wind power towards deep and distant seas, all DC wind farm technology solutions can not only avoid the issues of cable capacity rise and reactive power, but also eliminate the need for grid-following control and multiple voltage transformations, which have been widely adopted. However, as a current cutting-edge hot topic, there are many technical gaps in the relay protection of all DC offshore wind farms. For a fully DC offshore wind farm, the fault characteristics of a single-pole grounding fault in the collection line were first analyzed by fault current circuit of single-pole fault. The study found that the zero-mode current at the outlet of the collection line is a decaying sine signal, and the zero-mode current of the faulty line is greater than that of the healthy line. Based on this, a fault line selection method based on zero-mode information extraction is proposed. In this method, the bus zero-mode voltage is used as the starting threshold, and then the fault line is selected by comparing the zero-mode current amplitude of each line outlet. A full DC offshore wind farm model was built on the PSCAD/EMTDC platform to verify the effectiveness of the proposed fault line selection method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Load Frequency Control Strategy Considering Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The integration of energy storage systems into the power grid can achieve load frequency control (LFC) and improve the frequency stability of the grid. To address the challenges posed by the potential instability of control systems during the integration and withdrawal of energy storage systems in the grid, this paper proposes an adaptive control strategy based on asynchronous switching. Firstly, based on multiple scenarios of energy storage systems, a Lyapunov function is constructed to design control parameters; Secondly, using the average dwell time (ADT) technique and a smooth transition strategy, the stability of control parameter switching between multiple scenarios is ensured; Finally, compared with control schemes that do not consider the stability of the control system, simulation experiments show that the proposed method significantly reduces the dynamic impact of energy storage systems on the control system and enhances frequency stability.

articleTitle: Research on Online Data Collection and Detection Method of New Energy Station Based on Multi-Layer Evaluation System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid development of the new energy industry, the scale of wind farm stations continues to expand, and the amount of data generated has also increased sharply. To ensure the efficient and stable operation of the new energy station, this paper intends to build a set of online data collection and detection methods based on a multi-layer evaluation system. Firstly, the data of wind farm stations are collected and pre-processed online, and the online data collection model of wind turbines is constructed. Finally, the online data collection simulation is stratified based on typical wind turbines. Firstly, Fourier analysis is performed on the data to construct the first layer assessment, and then the second layer assessment is constructed based on the ratio of wind turbine output power to generator output power. Based on Matlab/Simulink simulation verification, complete the online data collection and evaluation of the wind farm station, to achieve real-time monitoring of the station operating status, timely warning when the wind farm station output power and current problems, and improve the stability of the wind farm station operation.

articleTitle: A Unified Magnetic Equivalent Circuit Model for Transformer Core Saturation Analysis in Multiphysics Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The saturation model of the transformer is one of the core tools of multi-physics simulation. By combining it with multi-physics simulation, researchers can more comprehensively evaluate the performance of the transformer in actual applications. Geomagnetically induced currents (GIC) induce DC bias in transformers, leading to core saturation and a host of adverse effects. Traditional transformer models often struggle to accurately capture the behavior of the core under nonlinear saturation conditions. To address these challenges, a saturable transformer unified magnetic equivalent (UMEC) model which directly takes B-H magnetization curve to represent transformer core nonlinear characteristic is proposed. The saturable transformer model is based on the model of a magnetic circuit of transformer core. GIC effects on transformer saturation are also studied with the proposed saturable transformer and estimation method.

articleTitle: Research on the Capacity of Energy Storage System in Mountain Distribution Network Based on Double-Layer Dynamic Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The widespread access of distributed power supplies has caused a strong impact on the stability and reliability of the distribution network in mountainous areas, and the introduction of energy storage systems can effectively mitigate its impact. The paper studies the energy storage capacity configuration model based on double-layer dynamic optimization, analyzes the operating constraints of the energy storage system and the dynamic optimal energy storage control strategy. The operation process of the double-layer dynamic optimization system is further designed. Finally, a case study is presented to verify the validity of the paper.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Capacitance Compensation Technology in the Stator Iron Loss Test of Large-scale Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The generator stator core loss test is an effective method to check the insulation of the stator core. When the insulation of the generator stator core is damaged, an eddy current phenomenon will be formed, which will endanger the normal operation of the unit in serious cases. Based on the research and application of capacitance compensation technology in the stator iron loss test of large generators, this paper focuses on the principle of capacitance compensation technology in the stator iron core loss test and the first use of high-current capacitance compensation technology to the transformation of units in operation for more than 30 years, in order to more accurately evaluate generators. Through practical application, it is found that the capacitance compensation technology can effectively reduce the test current and reduce the test risk. The stator core insulation state provides a new application case.

articleTitle: Simulation of Fluid-Thermal Field of Oil-immersed Transformer and Analysis of Local Overheating of Winding
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this paper, based on the coupling calculation method of flow field-temperature field of oil-immersed transformer, in order to take into account the calculation efficiency and accuracy of multiple physical fields, a simulation model of low-voltage winding is established according to the electrical and structural parameters of oil-immersed transformer, and the simulation results of flow field and temperature field of low-voltage winding are obtained. On this basis, the influence of different overheating positions of the winding on local regional temperature of the winding is analyzed according to the simulation results of the temperature field. It is obtained that when overheating occurs at different positions of the winding, the heat in the overheating area will be transferred by the oil flow to the upper part, so that the temperature of each point in the winding oil passage increases linearly with the increase of the overheating temperature in the lower part. The accuracy of this method is 98%, which has important guiding significance for determining the overheat position of oil-immersed transformer and prolonging the service life of transformer.

articleTitle: Study on Protection Strategy for Monopole Grounding in Offshore Wind DC Grid Based on Zero-Mode Component Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rise of deep-sea wind power, interest in all-DC wind farms is growing, but protection methods are under-researched. This paper analyzes fault characteristics of all-DC deep-sea wind power networks during single-pole grounding faults using modal decomposition. It derives analytical expressions for current and voltage, showing mainly capacitive relationships. A floating characteristic starting criterion based on voltage rate of change and voltage difference rate of change is proposed, along with a single-ended protection line selection algorithm using the Pearson correlation coefficient. A pole selection method is also introduced. A PSCAD/EMTDC simulation model verifies the proposed protection algorithm, showing good speed, selectivity, and strong tolerance to transition resistance.

articleTitle: Research on Transient Characteristics of an Improved Phase-locked Loop Topology Suitable for VSC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To solve the problem of deteriorating performance and poor stability of traditional PLL connected to weak AC system, an improved PLL structure is proposed in this paper. By measuring the angular velocity and initial phase Angle of the system respectively, the angular velocity of the system is first stabilized to ensure the synchronization between VSC and AC power grid, and then the initial phase Angle of the system is tracked by PI link to achieve accurate estimation and fast tracking of AC power grid phase Angle value. Finally, taking a classic VSC grid-connected system as an example, the effectiveness and stability of the improved PLL are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Reactive Power Compensation for Distribution Networks with New Energy Access
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In response to the common problems of high active power loss and poor voltage quality in medium and low voltage distribution networks with new energy access, the objective function is proposed to decompose the reactive power optimization mathematical model into three sub-models: maximum, general, and minimum load modes, with the annual energy loss cost of the distribution network and the minimum investment of newly added reactive power compensation equipment converted to each year; Simultaneously using system power flow as an equality constraint and node voltage and reactive power as inequality constraints, an improved genetic algorithm is designed using mutation operator optimization to find the optimal compensation method for medium and low voltage distribution networks. When conducting reactive power optimization on a 36 node distribution network with new energy access in a certain city, representative 35 kV lines were selected for optimization analysis and calculation. After optimization compensation, it effectively maintained voltage stability, reduced network loss rate, and reduced operating costs.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Optimization of Active Distribution Networks Considering Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming at the comprehensive utilization of distributed energy and electric vehicle charging station scale regulation capacity, an active distribution network optimization model that coordinates many active and reactive resources is proposed. Firstly, considering the volatility of photovoltaic (PV), wind power and electric vehicles (EV), a stochastic model is established; secondly, on the basis of traditional reactive power optimization, the reactive output of distributed new energy, energy storage and electric vehicles is fully considered. Then, the rotating second-order cone is used to solve the discrete variables and continuous variables, and the non-convex model is relaxed and converted into a linear solution problem. Finally, the model is analyzed using IEEE33 nodes. The results show that the model improves the optimization ability, further improves the voltage curve, and effectively reduces the system network loss.

articleTitle: A Method to Maximize Torque Density in MGs for Synchronous Condensers and Flywheel ESS
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: For magnetic gears (MGs) employed in flywheel and synchronous condenser energy storage systems (ESS), this paper introduces a method to maximize torque density under stress constraints. Initially, the minimum safe internal air-gap length under stress constraints is determined using the theory of thick cylinders. Subsequently, employing the Precise Sub domain Analytical Method (PSAM) and the stress tensor method, a mathematical analytical model of the magnetic gear's output torque is developed. This yields extensive data on the maximum static torque values. Thereafter, a surrogate model is created based on the Neural Network Radial Basis Function (NNRBF) model, and the optimal solution for torque density is attained using a Multi-Island Genetic Algorithm (MIGA). Finally, the validity of the proposed method is confirmed through Finite Element Analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: A Method for Dealing with Single-Phase Grounding Faults Based on Phase-Controlled Pre-Coordinated Arc Suppression Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to improve the processing ability of single-phase grounding faults in distribution network cable lines, a method of defining cable and overhead line faults using the size of transition resistance is proposed based on the characteristic of low resistance faults in cable lines. The calculation expression of transition resistance used in conjunction with phase-controlled pre-coordinated arc suppression coil is derived. The transition resistance measurement method is verified by digital simulation, and the relationship between damping rate, out-of-resonance, capacitance current and capacitor current observation error and transition resistance measurement error is analyzed in detail. Finally, the transition resistance measurement method was validated through real type experiments, and the results showed that this method can effectively distinguish between high resistance faults and low resistance faults, that is, cable faults and overhead line faults.

articleTitle: Economic Dispatch for Networked Microgrid under False Data Injection Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Due to deep integration between power grids and communication networks, cyber-attacks can be launched more readily in networked microgrids, leading to faulty dispatch command and further affecting the total economic cost. To solve this problem, a novel economic dispatch (ED) method is proposed by considering the impact of false data injection attacks (FDIAs) on measurement state data and control commands. First, the optimal ED model of networked microgrid is established, which innovatively incorporates dual-network coupling characteristics into the conventional dispatch model including objectives (e.g., operating cost) and constraints (e.g., power balance and output limits). Second, the attacked measurement state data and control commands by FDIAs are described and incorporated into the optimal ED model, forming the new reconstructed model. Third, the impacts of FDIAs on economy and security performances are analyzed based on the proposed indicators of cost and line overload risk, which shows that FDIAs inevitably increase both the operational costs and risks of system. Finally, experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed ED for networked microgrid under FDIAs.

articleTitle: Phase-locked Loop Dynamic Preserved Model Order Reduction of Doubly-Fed Wind Turbines Based on Balanced Truncation
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Phase-locked loop (PLL) has gradually become an important part of system synchronization in large-scale wind farms. Although the current reduced order state space model used for real-time simulation has a wide range of applications, the traditional reduced order model mainly focuses on model accuracy and model computational complexity, and can not realize the mechanism preservation of specific links. In order to study the problems of synchronous misalignment and wide-band oscillation in large-scale wind farms, a PLL dynamic preserved model order reduction of doubly-fed wind turbines (DFWTs) based on balanced truncation is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a small-signal model of parallel doubly-fed wind turbine with full order is established. Then, the PLL is separated from the wind turbine system to form two subsystems named decoupled subsystem (PLL) and decoupled main system. Based on this, balanced truncation based on gramian is applied to the decoupled main system with the exception of complete PLL structure. Finally, the reduced order decoupled main system is combined with the decoupled subsystem to form the PLL dynamic preserved reduced order model of DFWTs. The proposed PLL preserved order reduction method of DFWTs is verified with the simulation of 20 DFWTs in parallel effectively.

articleTitle: Geometric Matrix Completion for Missing Data Estimation in Power Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy, the reverse power flow and voltage violation become more and more frequent in power distribution networks. However, due to the lack of measurements in the system, it is difficult to observe the state of the whole system under low-observability scenarios using traditional techniques, which may compromise system operations. To address these issues, we come up with a missing data estimation method based on geometric matrix completion with neural networks to recover data matrix of distribution networks. The proposed method generally has good performance, especially in low-observability scenarios where traditional methods can hardly operate. Numerical results using IEEE 33- and 300-bus illustrate to the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation Strategy and Evaluation Method for Integrated Electricity and Heating Energy System Considering Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With increasing energy scarcity and environmental pollution, further enhancing the economic efficiency and low-carbon performance of integrated energy systems is crucial for achieving a low-carbon transition. In this context, an integrated energy optimization operation model that considers comprehensive demand response and carbon tax costs is proposed. Based on this model, a comprehensive evaluation index system is constructed to assess the optimal scheduling scheme of the system from the dimensions of economic efficiency and environmental performance. Then, the AHP-entropy weight method is used to determine the combined weights of each index and calculate the final evaluation results. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method is verified through simulation case studies.

Author Keywords: integrated electricity and heating energy system

articleTitle: Control Scheme of Distributed PV Plants in Partial Shading Conditions for Improved Transient Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Nearly, distributed maximum power point tracking (DMPPT) technologies based on the DC optimizer (DCO) for each single PV panel, have been widely concerned to mitigate the solar energy loss of photovoltaic (PV) power plants caused by the array mismatch problem under partial shading conditions. However, when the partial shading conditions become severe, the transient stability of the distributed PV generation system will be weakened due to the power imbalance between the PV modules. To solve this problem, a new control scheme for the DCO-based distributed PV plants is proposed to improve the system transient stability when a large disturbance occurs. First, the dynamic response of the Buck-DCO-based PV system under serious mismatch is analyzed. The improved control scheme is then established to deal with the saturation problem of integrators in control systems based on the former dynamic characteristics analysis. Finally, simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Prospect of SF6 Gas Recovery and Reuse Technology for Power Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>), a potent non-CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>greenhouse gas, is extensively used in the power industry due to its excellent insulating properties. However, SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>'s Global Warming Potential (GWP) is 23,500 times that of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and it has an atmospheric lifetime of 3,200 years, making its environmental impact significant and long-lasting and presenting a critical challenge for emission control. In order to curb the direct emission of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, protect the environment, and realize the resource utilization of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>waste gas, many researches are carrying out SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>emission control, ensuring the safe operation of electrical equipment, and saving the operation and maintenance cost of power grid. In this paper, SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>gas recovery technology, used SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>gas purification technology and resource utilization of F-containing waste gas are introduced in detail.

articleTitle: Operational Analysis of Traction Substations Cluster Continuous Co-Phase Traction Power Supply System with Photovoltaics and Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The traction substations cluster continuous co-phase traction power supply system (TPSS) offers an effective solution for power grids with limited access position, enabling long-distance power supply, eliminating the neutral sections in the traditional AC 25kV TPSS, improving the direct utilization of regenerative braking energy, and increase the access flexibility for photovoltaic and energy storage. Firstly, various schemes for photovoltaic and energy storage access to the traction substation for the continuous co-phase TPSS are introduced. Then, a unified power flow calculation model for the continuous co-phase TPSS containing photovoltaic, energy storage, and co-phase power supply devices is developed. Additionally, the TPSS's operational characteristics are analyzed based on an actual urban rail transit line. The results show that the utilization rate of regenerative braking energy reaches 100% by the continuous co-phase TPSS. The photovoltaic and co-phase power supply devices can both improve the power supply capacity of the TPSS while suppressing three-phase voltage unbalance.

articleTitle: Ultra-Short-Term Multi-Step Prediction of Wind Power Based on ModernTCN and Multi-Task Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The intermittent and fluctuating nature of wind energy makes it difficult to accurately predict wind power, leading to low penetration in the wind power grid. To address this problem, this paper designs ultra-short-term multi-step prediction of wind power based on ModernTCN and multi-task learning to improve the prediction accuracy. Firstly, ModernTCN's ability to have a large receptive field and capture cross-variate timing dependencies is exploited to obtain multivariate timing feature information and establish a multi-step mapping of input features to power. Then it is inputted into the MMoE multi-task learning method, and the prediction results are corrected to obtain the ultra-short-term prediction of wind power using multiple expert networks and gating units. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the ultra-short-term prediction accuracy of wind power, and can provide a favourable reference for the scheduling centre to adjust the power generation plan in real-time response to the power demand.

articleTitle: Power System Frequency Prediction Method Considering New Energy Access Ratio and Frequency Support Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the growing demand for electricity around the world, the energy crisis and environmental issues are becoming increasingly severe. Therefore, it is imperative to develop a new type of power system primarily based on new energy generation. However, as the rate at which renewable energy is being utilized increases, synchronous units are gradually replaced, the rotational moment of inertia of the power system decreases, the frequency regulation ability diminishes, and the frequency stability issue under perturbation events becomes more and more prominent. At the same time, the current frequency dynamic analysis method is difficult to meet the frequency stability analysis under the high proportion of new energy scenarios. Therefore, this paper considers the ability of new energy to actively carry out frequency support, based on the regression decision tree model, establishes a power system frequency prediction model based on the new energy penetration rate, the proportion of new energy units actively involved in frequency control, the new energy unit control parameters, and other key factors, and accurately predicts the maximum frequency deviation and the steady-state frequency deviation of the power system after power perturbation, while the importance of each control parameter is analyzed. And simulations are carried out in the test system to ascertain the efficacy of the introduced method.

articleTitle: Collaborative Control Strategy for Mountainous Railway Traction Power Supply System Based on Co-Phase Compensation Device
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this paper, for the characteristics of railway transportation in mountainous areas, the traction power supply system scheme is selected to be compatible with it. It elaborates on the composition of traction substations and cable traction networks within this power supply structure. The paper analyzes the capacitive effects of cable traction networks and the necessity of compensating cable capacitance reactive power. It proposes a multi-substation reactive power coordinated compensation control scheme based on a central controller. Based on the negative sequence compensation principle of the co-phase supply device, a collaborative compensation strategy combining cable reactive power compensation with traction load negative sequence compensation is introduced. Finally, a simulation model of the power supply system for a certain mountainous railway line is established. Simulation of the coordinated compensation control strategy for substations yields satisfactory compensation results overall, validating the feasibility of the compensation approach.

articleTitle: New Energy Station Energy Storage Configuration Strategy Considering New Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper proposes an energy storage configuration method in new energy stations to promote the consumption of new energy. At first, the cost model included three sub-modules of energy storage systems is constructed based on the characteristics of energy storage. Then, taking the intermittency and uncertainty of new energy output into account, as well as the constraints of each energy source in the power generation process, an objective function is established with the goal of minimizing the comprehensive cost of energy storage. The improved cat swarm optimization algorithm (ICSOA) is utilized to solve the proposed model and determine the optimal energy storage configuration for new energy stations. Finally, the feasibility and correctness of the proposed model are verified through some case studies.

articleTitle: A New Method for Calculating Temperature-Controlled Load Electricity Consumption Based on Sensitive Temperature Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid growth of the tertiary industry and residential electricity consumption, the impact of temperature-sensitive loads on power system has significantly increased. This paper proposes a new method for calculating the proportion of temperature-sensitive electricity consumption. Firstly, the Pearson correlation coefficient is used to analyze the correlation between electricity consumption in cold and hot periods throughout the year and the average temperature, highest temperature, and lowest temperature. Subsequently, based on the electricity consumption data in different periods and corresponding temperature data, the average electricity consumption for each degree of temperature is calculated for cold and hot periods. The Pruned Exact Linear Time (PELT) inflection point detection method is applied to identify the corresponding sensitive temperature, and calculate the baseline electricity consumption corresponding to high and low temperatures on weekdays and weekends in cold and hot periods. Finally, the sum of the temperature-induced electricity consumption on weekdays and weekends is calculated, and the percentage of temperature-controlled loads is determined by comparing it with the total annual electricity consumption. The effectiveness of the proposed calculation model is verified using actual electricity consumption data from a province in southern China in 2023.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Strategy for Electrolytic Hydrogen Production Based on AEL and PEMEL
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Electrolysis-based hydrogen production plays a crucial role in achieving the efficient conversion and flexible consumption of green energy. The control strategy implemented in electrolysis systems significantly influences key factors such as energy efficiency and system costs. In this research, we propose a photovoltaic (PV) hydrogen production system featuring the coordinated operation of multiple electrolyzers. This system incorporates both alkaline electrolyzers (AEL) and proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEMEL), taking into account their distinct dynamic operating characteristics. Within this system, two-layer control strategies of the multi-type electrolysis system are designed, and a comprehensive simulation system is developed, encompassing PV power generation, DC/DC converters, and models for both types of electrolyzers. The simulation results verify the effectiveness and stability of the proposed control strategy. In addition, a comparative analysis with alternative hydrogen production methods shows that this multi-electrolyzer hydrogen production solution can reduce PEMEL demand capacity by 22.7%, and has advantages in terms of capacity configuration costs.

articleTitle: A Systematic Evaluation Method Considering the Monitoring Accuracy of Wind Farm Station Data
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Wind station data monitoring is a very important part of meteorology, energy, and related fields. The existing methods are generally direct feedback to wind farm data, without evaluating the accuracy of wind farm detection data. In this paper, a method and system for evaluating the accuracy of wind farm data monitoring are studied. Data of wind farm stations are monitored by data acquisition equipment, and monitoring parameter data of wind farm stations are obtained. The construction of indicators to analyze and evaluate the accuracy of wind farm data detection solves the problem that it is difficult to accurately analyze the accuracy of wind farm data and quantifies the accuracy of wind farm data detection. By analyzing the reliability of wind station data and making early warnings, the problem that it is difficult to accurately analyze the accuracy of wind station data in the existing technology is solved.

articleTitle: Largesignal Stability Analysis of E-SOP Based on T-S Fuzzy Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Flexible interconnection devices enhance the ability of distribution network to accommodate large-scale distributed sources and loads, while the interactive coupling among high proportion of power electronic devices may affect the operational stability of the distribution network. To quantify the effects of system parameters, control modes, and control parameters on the stability of the interconnection systems between different distribution areas via Energy-storage Flexible Multi-State Switch (E-SOP), this paper conducts a study on the large-signal stability of E-SOP based on the T-S fuzzy model. According to the topology and control strategy of the E-SOP, the T-S fuzzy model is derived, the attraction domain estimation method based on the model is given, and the effects of the main circuit parameters, the parameters characterizing the operating point information, and the control parameters on the large-signal stability of the E-SOP are analyzed using the attraction domain. The theoretical analysis results are compared and analyzed with the time-domain simulation results to verify the correctness of the proposed method for estimating attraction domain to judge the large-signal stability of E-SOP using the T-S fuzzy model.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning Active Distribution Grid Load Equivalent Modeling Method Based on Evidential Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With a large number of adjustable loads and new energy sources connected. Distribution networks are increasingly in the form of active distribution networks. This situation introduces more stochasticity and uncertainty into the active distribution network load equivalence modeling problem. At the same time, in the case of high stochasticity and time-varying, the method of constructing the load equivalence model needs to consider multiple influencing factors. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-objective reinforcement learning active distribution grid load equivalent modeling method based on evidential reasoning. This method is divided into five steps. First, a multi-attribute analysis is performed to identify the set of evaluation indicators, the set of candidate solutions, the set of evaluation ratings, and the set of evaluation criteria set, candidate solution set, and evaluation level set. The confidence evaluation vector is subsequently obtained. In the second step, multi-evidence fusion is performed after obtaining confidence evaluation vectors of candidate solutions. The approximate degree of superiority of the candidate solutions can subsequently be obtained. In the third step, utility analysis is used to compare the average utility values of different candidate solutions and select the final candidate. In the fourth step, the active distribution network load equivalence modeling process is modeled as a Markov decision process. In the fifth step, the scenarios determined in the third step are brought into the fourth step to solve for the key parameters of the isotropic model. Simulation results show that the method proposed in this paper can obtain the required load equivalence model for active distribution networks.

articleTitle: Research on Insulation Coordination in MMC-HVDC for Wind Farm Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Flexible DC system is widely used for wind farm integration because of its unique technical advantages. To ensure reliable operation of the system, it is important to evaluate overvoltage levels and develop detailed insulation coordination schemes. Based on the main wiring and operation mode of modular multilevel converter (MMC) HVDC system for wind power integration, the insulation coordination design method of the system is studied in this paper. An MMC HVDC system model for wind farm integration is built in PSCAD/EMTDC software for simulation. Various system faults, such as AC and DC side faults in converter and DC line faults, are simulated to analyze overvoltage phenomena that may occur during operation. By calculating the peak voltage of the observation points, two kinds of arrester configuration schemes are proposed for comparison. The simulation results show that the better lightning arrester configuration scheme can achieve better overvoltage suppression effect. The insulation margin and withstand voltage of main electrical equipment are then determined to ensure the safety of the system in the face of overvoltage.

articleTitle: High Step-Up Bridgeless Converters for Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Energy harvesting scavengers collect the environmental energy sources into the power electronic devices for energy storage, which help wireless sensor nodes (WSNs) feedback signals to achieve the Internet of Things (IoTs). However, the environmental energy source generators usually offer only very low AC output voltages, requiring a high step-up AC-DC converter for power conversion. Thus, this paper proposes a high step-up AC-DC topology family, which can have a bridgeless operation to further avoid the voltage and power loss in the circuits. Then, one specific circuit is focused on. Operation modes and voltage ratio between input and output are analyzed. Finally, the simulations are presented to validate the feasibility and correctness of the proposed circuit.

articleTitle: Malicious Instructions Detection in Distribution Terminal Units - A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the continuous evolution of smart grids, embedded devices such as Distribution Terminal Units (DTUs) have become increasingly vital. However, it also makes DTU s an important target for attack. Among the most prevalent and critical security threats to DTU s are malicious instructions. Traditional anomaly detection techniques are ineffective due to the real-time operational requirements of DTUs. This paper presents a novel approach that utilizes machine learning techniques to identify malicious instructions by analyzing the CPU's power usage patterns. This non-invasive state monitoring approach is swift and highly accurate, achieving a detection accuracy of up to 93%.

articleTitle: Loss Analysis and Junction Temperature Prediction for Modular Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the increasing efficiency and reliability requirements of power systems, optimizing the performance and reliability analysis of modular multilevel converters (MMCs) has become crucial. And the insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT), as the core component of the MMC converter, the accurate assessment of its power loss is crucial for the operation of the MMC converter. In this paper, we firstly describe the topology and operating characteristics of the half-bridge MMC, and analyze the operation of the sub-modules, in order to propose a fast electro-thermal joint calculation method based on junction temperature feedback. The method firstly simplifies the sub-module model and calculates the individual sub-module power loss, secondly establishes the thermal network model of the IGBT device in the half-bridge sub-module, and unites the loss calculated from the output of the electrical simulation with the junction temperature predicted by the thermal network model, and finally verifies the correctness of the electro-thermal coupling model proposed in the paper in Matlab.

articleTitle: An Integrated Energy System Load Forecasting Method Based on CEEMDAN and MTL
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Accurate load forecasting is a prerequisite for achieving optimal system energy dispatch and improving energy utilisation, but the physical characteristics and strong coupling of loads lead to a significant increase in load volatility and stochasticity, which affects forecasting accuracy. In this regard, this paper constructs a new integrated energy load forecasting model: a combined MTL-CNN-GRU and MLR forecasting model. The method firstly uses CEEMDAN algorithm to decompose the load data of the integrated energy system, splitting the time series into sub-components with different complexity; then further adopts the multi-task learning strategy to learn the complex coupling relationship between different load types. The signal can be divided into high-frequency and low-frequency components by calculating the over-zero rate, and MTL-CNN-GRU is used for the high-frequency part of the prediction and MLR for the low-frequency part of the prediction; at last, the two parts of the prediction results are superimposed to obtain the final results. The experimental results show that the constructed model can effectively improve the accuracy of load prediction.

articleTitle: Electric Field Simulation Analysis on the End of Stator Winding for Large Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to study the anti-corona performance of the stator end winding of a large generator, this paper takes the stator end winding of an 18kV hydroelectric generator as the research object to conduct simulation analysis. Firstly, three out-of-phase stator winding models were constructed based on two possible anti-corona structures that may be used for the stator bar of the generator. Then, finite element electric field simulation analysis is conducted using COMSOL Multiphysics software. The research results indicate that a sudden change in the potential of the stator winding at the low resistance and high resistance overlap points of the high-voltage bar as well as at the binding position of the diagonal edge of the bar occurs. The maximum value of the winding air gap field strength occurs in the air domain between the medium and high resistance overlap points of the two stator bars, and the maximum value of the loss distribution occurs at the low resistance and high resistance overlap areas of the highvoltage stator bar. The simulation results show that as the excitation voltage increases, the distribution of potential, electric field, and loss gradually increases. Moreover, under different assessment voltages, all three winding models meet the requirements for the anti-corona performance of the generator stator winding. This indicates that the mixed use of different anticorona structures has a relatively small impact on the distribution of electric field at the end of the stator winding. In addition, in the actual production, attention should be paid to the anti-corona treatment in the area with concentrated electric field distribution, so as to avoid corona discharge, ablation and even winding gap breakdown during the operation of the generator.

articleTitle: Research Status and Prospect of New Power System Point-Wave Measurement Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In today's “double-high” power systems, the proliferation of power electronics in power generation, transmission, distribution, and loads puts the power system in a state of rapid change. Synchronous vector measurement techniques (PMU) based on vector synchronization units have gradually demonstrated their limitations, and emerging applications require more accurate and continuous waveform measurements. Point waveform measurement techniques with continuous, time-synchronized sampled values of the signal can more accurately represent the measurement of the underlying voltage and current waveforms. In this context, the article focuses on the development of point-wave measurement (POW) technology.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of Photovoltaic Array Tilt Angle on the Output Power of Photovoltaic Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: A numerical simulation study was conducted on different photovoltaic array models with varying tilt angles in different wind and sand environments. The installation tilt angles of the photovoltaic arrays (15°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 75°) were simulated. The results showed that excessively large or small installation tilt angles lead to an increase in the amount of dust particle deposition on the surface of the photovoltaic modules. The deposition is minimized when the photovoltaic array is installed at a tilt angle of 45°. Experiments were conducted with five different installation angles (15°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 75°), revealing that the output power loss of the first row of photovoltaic modules was the most significant, while the third and fourth rows were less affected by the tilt angle. The power loss rates of the photovoltaic modules due to the five different installation angles were 1.90%, 1.42%, 1.76%, 1.87%, and 2.01%, respectively. The output power loss rate of the modules increased significantly at installation angles of 15° and 75°, whereas the power loss was relatively lower at 45°.

articleTitle: Pricing Optimization for Public EV Charging Stations Considering User Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Pricing strategy plays a crucial role in public charging stations' operation. A good pricing strategy can not only improve the revenue of public charging stations but also guide the charging behavior of electric vehicle (EV) users. This paper proposes an hourly time-of-use pricing strategy for public charging stations considering user charging behavior to maximize the profit of public charging stations. We first propose a fitting optimization model to characterize the response function between charging demand and charging price, and then develop a pricing optimization model on this basis. Based on the real data from a large public charging station in Shanghai, we perform numerical experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Co-Sale Model for Renewable Energy and Hydropower in Mid-and-Long-Term Electricity Transactions in China
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Renewable energy has been developing rapidly in recent years. Characterized with strong volatility and uncertainty, it's difficult for renewable energy sellers to participate in mid-and-long-term electricity transactions in China. This paper proposes a co-sale model for renewable energy and hydropower. In this model, renewable energy sellers cooperate with a hydropower seller to increase their guaranteed-output. A higher guaranteed-output allows more electricity generated by renewable energy to be sold in mid-and-long-term transactions. The proposed model is tested on an actual co-sale process in Qinghai Province, China. Case study shows that the proposed co-sale model effectively increases the proportion of renewable energy traded in mid-and-long-term transactions. Besides, we detailly analyze the co-sale process and the influence of hydropower-related parameters on simulation results.

articleTitle: Development of a Series HVDC Cable Accessories Based on Silicone Rubber
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The main insulation materials for cable accessories include silicone rubber (SR) and ethylene propylene diene monomer (EPDM) rubber. Compared with EPDM rubber, SR material has become the preferred material for AC cable accessories due to its good electrical, thermal and mechanical properties. Because the electric field distribution mechanisms of DC cables and AC cables are different, the electric field distribution depends on the insulation dielectric constant under AC voltage and the insulation resistivity under steady-state DC voltage. The application of SR materials in DC cable accessories has been affected to a certain extent by factors such as resistivity and space charge accumulation. The authors of this paper modified SR materials and developed medium-voltage, high-voltage, and ultra-high-voltage DC cable accessories, verifying that the electrical, thermal and mechanical properties of SR are also suitable for DC cable accessories.

articleTitle: Accounting for Carbon Emissions from the Manufacturing Process of High Voltage Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Taking high-voltage cable equipment as the research object, this paper focuses on the carbon footprint behaviors and factors in the manufacturing process of cable products. Carbon emission sources are identified across four stages: cable raw material acquisition, production process, usage, and disposal. Based on the life cycle assessment theory and using “lkm of cable” as the reference flow, data on the inputs of raw materials/components, auxiliary materials, energy, and natural resources, as well as the outputs of greenhouse gases, waste, and recyclable scraps corresponding to these four stages, are collected to establish a carbon footprint accounting model for the manufacturing process of cable equipment. To validate the scientificity and operability of the accounting method, a 220kV ZC- Y JL W03-Z cable with a cross-sectional area of 2500mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is selected as the accounting target, and the cradle-to-gate carbon footprint results of this specification of cable from two suppliers are calculated. The carbon footprint accounting model proposed in this paper helps high-voltage cable manufacturers and power grid enterprises to understand the emission sources in detail, clarify the emissions of each production link, provide a scientific assessment method for the low-carbon selection of cable equipment and green grid, and strongly support the “dual-carbon” action of the power grid from the equipment side.

articleTitle: Power Management and Control Strategy Based on Model-Free Control for Hybrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The hybrid energy storage system (HESS) integrating supercapacitor and batterie capitalizes on their respective merits of high power density and high energy density, enabling the smoothing of DC bus fluctuations and power balancing, hence has been widely applied in DC microgrids. Energy management and control stand as the central issues in HESS. This paper comprehensively considers the control at both system and device levels, proposing a power allocation strategy based on virtual impedance droop (VID) and a power control strategy based on the ultralocal model. A SoC (State of Charge) recovery strategy with frequency constraints is devised, building upon the traditional supercapacitor control based on virtual capacitance droop. Furthermore, the applied converter control method based on the ultralocal model significantly mitigates dependency on physical parameters, which enhances the robustness of the control. Ultimately, the efficacy of the proposed two-level energy management and control strategy is substantiated through simulations conducted in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Electrical Equipment Identification Method With Aerial Inspection Image Based on Substation Grid Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The application of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in power system inspection is becoming increasingly widespread. Due to the variety of equipment, multiple transmission line bays, and high similarity among devices within substations, improving the efficiency of UAV inspection in substations is essential. In this paper, a method based on substation grid localization is proposed to associate UAV inspection images with power equipment, aiming to quickly archive UAV inspection photos and differentiate the target equipment inspected. Practical engineering demonstrations validate that the proposed method is applicable to both manual and autonomous inspections.

articleTitle: Frequency Control Strategy of Grid-Forming Direct-Drive Wind Farms Transmitted Through the HC-HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the continuous rise of wind power grid-connected capacity, more and more desert areas will be developed and constructed as new resource bases for wind power in the future. Since this type of wind power base is similar to the island energy network, there is no planning of synchronous generators such as thermal power and hydropower, therefore, the grid-forming control mode is generally adopted. In this paper, a topology of Hybrid Cascaded High Voltage Direct Current (HC-HVDC) transmission system for grid-forming direct-drive wind farms without synchronous power support is constructed. Further, a frequency control strategy for the wind power grid-connected system is proposed. Finally, based on the PSCAD/EMTDC, the electromagnetic transient simulation of the proposed control strategy is carried out to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Frequency Regulation Strategy for Microgrids with High-Penetration of Distributed PV Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: As the share of photovoltaic (PV) generation grows., the intermittent and stochastic characteristics of solar energy may lead to frequency fluctuations., particularly in microgrids with high penetration of PV sources. Enlarging the capacity of installed energy storage can solve this problem., but the energy storage requires additional installation and maintenance costs.
