Therefore., there is increasing demand for PV sources to take participation in frequency regulation. This paper proposes an adaptive PV frequency regulation strategy (APFRS) based on dp/dv control method. The proposed strategy operates the PV sources below their Maximum Power Point (MPP) to realize flexible power regulation., thereby achieving active frequency support. It adjusts the reserved power to regulate frequency in response to load changes. Under conditions of insufficient irradiation., the PV sources will adaptively switch to the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) mode to enhance power support for the system for higher operation efficiency. The proposed strategy can effectively reduce the demand for the capacity of energy storage system (ESS). Moreover., this strategy is fully decentralized and can be coordinated with only local measurements., avoiding the need for a communication network. Matlab/Simulink simulations are presented to validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Diagnosis Method for High Voltage Cable Insulation Faults Based on Multi-Sensory Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming to address the problems of high detection cost, poor adaptability, and low accuracy of the existing high-voltage cable insulation fault diagnostic system, an intelligent diagnostic method for high-voltage cable insulation faults based on multisensory fusion is proposed. First, the detection method effectively decomposes the acquired data information through variable modal decomposition (VMD) and obtains relevant feature quantities; secondly, the current cable insulation fault is predicted according to the feature quantities using the long-short memory neural network (LSTM) algorithm. The experimental results show that the method has good prediction performance, and the detection accuracy can reach 97.02%, which is significant for guaranteeing safe power grid operation.

articleTitle: Stability Constrained Robust Unit Commitment for LCC-HVDC Transmission Power System with Renewable Energy-Thermal Power Bundled
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The transmission of power from large-scale renewable energy-thermal power bundled installations via LCC-HVDC transmission system is considered as a crucial method. To ensure system stability and minimize operational costs, a stability constrained robust unit commitment (UC) model is proposed. First, the model formulates stability constraints, including short-circuit current, voltage stability, and frequency stability. Next, accounting for the N-1 safety criterion, a robust UC model is developed to handle multiple discrete scenarios. Then, a linear equivalent transformation method is devised for the proposed UC model, facilitating the conversion of the original problem into a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) problem. Finally, a modified IEEE 39-bus system is tested to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: LCC-HVDC Transmission Power System with Renewable Energy-Thermal Power Bundled

articleTitle: A Modified LLC-AHB Converter to Achieve Wide Voltage Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this paper, a modified LLC-asymmetric half bridge flyback converter (AHB) that can realize a wide range of voltage gain is proposed. This type of topology utilizes the idea of topology morphing to realize the mode transition between LLC mode and AHB mode by adding bidirectional switches. The optimal design of resonant tank is realized while avoiding the extra resonant inductor of LLC mode, which solves the problem of conventional LLC-AHB converter that the efficiency of LLC mode decreases due to the small LLC magnetizing inductor and the over-resonance due to the small <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{L}_{\mathbf{n}}$</tex> (ratio of magnetizing inductance to resonant inductance). The considerations, optimal design of this topology are discussed in this paper. Finally, the performance of the proposed topology is confirmed by simulation results.

articleTitle: Switching Governor Based Transient Stability Control of Multi-Machine Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper proposes a bang-bang funnel controller based switching governor for improving the transient stability of multi-machine power systems. The proposed governor consists of three parts: a second-order bang-bang constant funnel controller(BBCFC), a conventional speed control loop and a properly designed switching strategy. The switching strategy will activate the BBCFC to restrict the speed of synchronous generator(SG), as well as its first-order derivative with respect to time, within prescribed funnels when severe faults occur in power systems. If the deviation between the speed of SG and synchronous speed is small, then the conventional speed control loop will be selected to guarantee the convergence of the speed of SG to synchronous speed. Compared with traditional governors, the control effort of the proposed governor is much larger, which enables the rapid adjustment of control valve flow area so that the mechanical power input can be changed in time to stabilize the speed of SG. Simulation studies are carried out on a 12 machines power system to test the performances of the proposed switching governor.

articleTitle: Battery Safety Evaluation Based on Risk Control and Collection Data Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper introduces a battery safety assessment method grounded in risk control and data processing of collection, which evaluates the safety performance of batteries in an innovative way. The approach is predicated on the study of internal parameters that influence the safety performance of batteries, leading to the design of an equivalent circuit model. the remaining battery power is derived through the Coulomb counting method, open-circuit voltage method, and capacitance voltage method. Ultimately, safety assessment outcomes are produced by integrating risk control with data collection and processing. In order to perform a safety assessment of the battery, the parameters of the battery equivalent model were first determined based on the specifications of the battery equivalent model. Subsequently, the remaining battery power is obtained by using the ampere-hour integration method, the open-circuit voltage method, and the capacitor voltage method. After obtaining the safety assessment parameters through principal component analysis, the internal parameters of the sample power battery are combined to iteratively train the fault diagnostic model, and the fault diagnostic results of the sample power battery are output to determine the safety assessment data of the power battery. Finally, the data and parameters are used to train the risk control collection model, and then assess the battery safety. This method improves the accuracy of battery charge state estimation, improves the battery safety assessment system, and ensures the stable operation of the system.

articleTitle: Non-Unit Transient Protection for LCC-HVDC Transmission Lines Based on Correlation of Current Derivatives
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The reliability and sensitivity of HVDC transmission line's protection for HVDC system are in need of further improvement. So a new non-unit transient protection based on correlation of current derivatives (CDs) is proposed in this paper. According to the impedance frequency characteristics of converter and DC filter, the correlation characteristics between line current derivative (LCD) and DC filter current derivative (DFCD) are analyzed during fault transients. Simulation results show that the proposed protection scheme can correctly identify internal and external faults and is of high reliability and sensitivity.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Strategy for Power Systems Considering Multi Energy Complementarity
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the continuous development of new power system construction, the proportion of new energy has gradually increased, and its randomness and volatility have brought great challenges to the operation of power system. Multi energy complementation is one of the feasible ways to solve the problem of new energy consumption. The core is how to stabilize the intermittency and randomness of new energy power generation such as wind power and photovoltaic power generation through flexible power sources such as hydropower, thermal power, and energy storage. Flexible power sources such as hydropower, thermal power and energy storage in the power grid are complementary to new energy in different time scales. This paper analyzes the optimal dispatching strategy of hydropower resources, introduces a double-layer optimal dispatching framework that considers the medium and long-term power balance and short-term power balance, and establishes a multi time scale coordinated optimal dispatching model of power system. Through the simulation analysis, the power system optimal dispatching strategy considering multi energy complementarity proposed in this paper can not only ensure the supply and demand balance of the system in different time scales, but also improve the economic operation performance of the system.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Characteristics of Magnetically Coupled Resonant Coils Based on Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of the magnetically coupled resonant wireless energy transfer technology of double helix coil type, the mutual inductance calculation method between the coil coils is investigated by establishing a normalized mathematical calculation model. The objective program is designed to solve the inner diameter corresponding to the maximum transmission efficiency, and the simulation is verified by three-dimensional electromagnetic simulation software (ANSYS). The effect of the incorporation of the metamaterial structure on the transmission efficiency is also analyzed by simulation.

articleTitle: Regional Electricity Carbon Emission Real-time Monitoring Method Considering Green Electricity Transaction Contract
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Constructing a reliable and effective electricity carbon monitoring system is crucial for clarifying users' electricity carbon emission responsibility and achieving “dual carbon” goals. Current systems do not account for the impact of power transactions, failing to distinguish the carbon emission responsibilities behind each transaction. This paper proposes a novel regional electricity carbon emission real-time monitoring method which incorporates power transaction behavior, especially green electricity transaction, based on carbon emission flow theory. The method decomposes electricity flow into transaction flow and non-transaction flow firstly, and then calculates the corresponding carbon emission responsibilities based on their sources independently. Simulations based on the P JM -5 node system validate the method's effectiveness. Results show the proposed method can elucidate the transfer of carbon emission responsibilities associated with power transactions. The method is suitable for the real-time monitoring of carbon emission information in power systems.

articleTitle: CNN-AM-BiLSTM PV Power Prediction Model Based on Keplerian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the increasing scale of installed PV power, the grid instability problem caused by the uncertainty, volatility and intermittency of PV power generation is becoming more and more serious. The traditional PV power prediction models have low prediction accuracy in the case of rapid weather changes. Therefore, a combined CNN-AM-BiLSTM PV power prediction model is proposed to improve the prediction accuracy. First, the historical data are classified using the Random Forest(RF) algorithm to get different types of weather, Convolutional neural networks(CNN) are able to extract features of data, Attention Mechanism(AM) is used to redistribute the weights for the problem that each variant has a different weight to produce energy at different times, The bidirectional long and short-term memory network(BiLSTM) is employed to search the influence of weather features on power generation before and after. Meanwhile, Set the hyperparameters of this model through the Kepler optimizes algorithm(KOA). Finally, the model's effectiveness is verified by comparing it with five other models.

Author Keywords: bi-directional long and short-term memory network

articleTitle: Research on Modeling Method for Thermal Path of Triple-core Optical Fiber Composite Cables in Smart Energy Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Building a smart grid is to accelerate the integration of the four networks on the existing grid technology and infrastructure, and fully utilize the advantages of the power communication network to enhance the level of intelligence. Optical Fiber Composite Low-Voltage Cable (OPLC) is a composite cable that combines optical fiber and low-voltage cable, and has dual transmission functions of power and optical communication. The sharp increase in the temperature of the fiber-optic composite cable jeopardizes the safety of the cable, causing accidents and serious consequences. Therefore, accurately grasping the temperature of the cable is extremely important for the safe operation of the cable. The cable conductor temperature can be measured by indirect measurement method. By measuring the surface temperature of the cable and combining the thermodynamic theory, the temperature at different positions inside the cable can be estimated. The method is convenient and operability is strong. In this paper, the internal structure of OPLC is analyzed, and the transient thermal path model of triple-core OPLC is proposed. Then the particle swarm algorithm is used to identify the parameters of the thermal path model, reduce the error and improve the accuracy of calculation. Finally, through COMSOL Multiphysics simulation analysis. Comparing the simulation data with the calculated data, the error is within the allowable range, thus proving the accuracy of the triple-core OPLC transient thermal path model.

articleTitle: Research on Dual Carbon Economic Operation Optimization of PV Gas Combined Power Generation System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the context of achieving carbon peak and carbon neutrality goals, the development of the power system needs to accelerate the replacement of clean energy. At the same time, it also needs to optimize the energy structure and promote low-carbon, efficient, and sustainable development. As a transitional method, gas-fired power generation has the advantages of strong peak ramping ability and fast start-up, which plays a positive role in achieving low-carbon transformation. This article discusses the cost of electricity consumption, carbon emission cost, and changes in carbon prices. It studies the PV(photovoltaic) gas combined power generation system and solves it using the FMINCON function in MATLAB. The research results show that the optimized scheduling of PV gas reduces the cost of electricity by 27.6% compared to pure gas, and the cost of carbon emissions is reduced by 45.4%. Meanwhile, as carbon price increases, the carbon emission cost and gas-fired power generation cost of the system correspondingly increase almost linearly. The PV gas power generation system is only economically optimal compared to other combined power generation systems. Further exploration is needed to combine more energy generation methods with gas-fired power generation for joint power generation. This will promote the optimization of various aspects of the system and facilitate the sustained transformation of gas-fired power generation towards low-carbon development.

articleTitle: Low-Voltage Regulation Device Based on IGBT Combination Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid development of the economy in rural areas, the residents of the stable reliability of the power supply has put forward higher requirements, but due to the agricultural network has a long transmission radius, weak network structure and other characteristics, resulting in the existence of serious low voltage problems at the end of the line. This paper synthesizes the advantages and disadvantages of the existing low-voltage management technology, and puts forward a low-voltage management technology scheme based on IGBT combinational switch, which is connected to the end of the 10kV line through two transformers in series and parallel, and utilizes the IGBT combinational switch as a transformer tap casting and cutting device to control the regulation of line voltage. The principle analysis and simulink simulation model verification of the scheme, and through the parameter design to complete the prototype development, and finally the prototype test to verify the correctness and effectiveness of the scheme.

articleTitle: Particle Swarm Optimization Based Scheduling Approach for Charging Electric Vehicle Population Addressing Factors Both Traffic and Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper proposes a particle swarm optimization (PSO) based optimal scheduling approach to achieve the minimum average charging time of electric vehicles (EVs) and the coupling minimum generation cost. To this end, an aggregated objective transformed from a bi-objective optimization problem is formulated taking into account the factors associated with the charging behavior of the electric vehicle population on the traffic side and the coupling factors on the power grid side. Further, an enhanced bilevel particle swarm optimization (EBPSO) algorithm is developed to solve the aforementioned aggregated objective. In order to avoid the particle swarm algorithm from falling into local optimums and round-trip motions between particles, learning particles are introduced into the EBPSO algorithm. Finally, the proposed approach is validated by using a coupled environment consisting of a 48-node traffic system and an IEEE 118-bus power system benchmark. The promising results encourage further work of this study in the next step.

articleTitle: Development of a New Type of Vortex Bladeless Wind Turbine for Urban Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Innovation and development of renewable energy devices are crucial for reaching a sustainable and environmentally conscious future. This work focuses on the development of a new type of renewable energy devices in the context of Smart Garden at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, which aims to design a bladeless wind turbine for urban areas, addressing the pressing need for clean energy locally and globally. Traditional wind turbines have been widely adopted in recent decades, while bladeless wind turbines have also displayed their advantages and uniqueness in urban areas. A Vortex Bladeless Wind Turbine (VBWT) is modeled by using Fusion 360 to optimize wind energy generation in urban settings with limited space and buildings-dominated landscape. Optimal parameters of the VBWT were obtained by comparing the results of drag force, lift force and deflection, via the simulations in Ansys. Hardware of proposed bladeless wind turbine has been assembled and developed by 3-dimensional printing. Additional tests and adjustments on hardware further improve the performance of the developed wind turbine. The outcomes of this work have the potential to contribute to future renewable energy initiatives and devote the sustainability efforts in urban energy systems.

articleTitle: A Novel Four-Arm Modular Multilevel Converter with High Power Density
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To further improve the power density of the transformerless medium-voltage power quality control device, a four-arm modular multilevel converter (FA-MMC) topology and its control strategy are proposed in this paper. The FA-MMC is composed of four arms and arm selection switches. Half of the sub modules in each phase are multiplexed through arm selection switches to improve the utilization of the submodules. Compared with the traditional MMC topology, the proposed FA-MMC can reduce the number of submodules by 33.3%. Finally, a FA-MMC system is established on the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform to verify the effectiveness of the proposed topology and control strategy.

articleTitle: Research on the Capability of Electric Vehicles Participating in Ramping Ancillary Services
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper studies the reserve capacity provided by Electric Vehicle (EV) aggregators in the ramping ancillary service market. Considering the uncertain charging behavior and energy demand of EVs, an optimization decision-making model for charging power and reporting ramping capacity of EV aggregators is built. Firstly, considering the risk of insufficient ramping capability response after the EV aggregators are called or the inability to meet charging demand of EVs, a risk cost assessment method based on conditional value at risk is proposed to balance the benefit and risk of providing reserves by EV aggregators, and an optimized model aiming at benefit maximization is built. Secondly, the characteristics and advantages of EV aggregators providing ramping ancillary services under different application scenarios are compared and analyzed based on a simulation example, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Reactive Power and Voltage Optimization for Regional Power Grids with New Energy Stations under the Goal of “Double Carbon”
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In view of the problems caused by the high proportion of new energy grid connection, such as large active network loss and voltage fluctuation, high reactive power cost and environmental protection cost, a reactive voltage optimization model based on the time-series segmentation strategy of new energy output is proposed. The model uses the Top-Down algorithm to segment the process according to the maximum dispersion of the average value of new energy output between each period and the minimum dispersion within each period. It adopts a reactive pricing strategy to allocate the output of reactive power sources reasonably, and takes the minimum sum of standardized active network loss, node voltage deviation, reactive power source cost, and environmental protection cost of thermal power units as the optimization objective. The improved firefly algorithm is used to solve the optimization model. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using the IEEE-30 bus system.

articleTitle: Common Mode Analysis and Suppression of Chained Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The chain energy storage system has the structural characteristics suitable for use in large-capacity battery energy storage systems, but the energy storage battery is large in size, and it introduces certain parasitic parameters in the chain energy storage system, which will lead to the inverter in the switching tube high-frequency turn-on and turn-off process, generating a large common-mode current, which will damage the life of the power devices and jeopardize the stable operation of the system equipment. Firstly, a simplified model of chain energy storage system is established to analyze the common mode voltage intrusion into the battery system pathway of the chain energy storage system. The characteristics and influencing factors of the common-mode current of single inductor circuit and symmetric inductor circuit are studied separately, and it is pointed out that the common-mode current of the symmetric inductor circuit can be effectively suppressed by optimizing the modulation strategy. To this end, an improved one-dimensional modulation strategy is proposed for the symmetric inductor circuit and the power tube switching state, which can effectively suppress the system common mode current. Finally, the correctness of the analysis is verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Restoration Strategy of Distribution Network with Collaborative Operation of Multiple Distributed Generators under Lightning Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the event of a major blackout caused by extreme weather events such as lightning strikes, distributed generators can be utilized to restore critical loads before the main grid resumes power supply. This paper proposes a strategy for restoring critical loads in a distribution network involving mul-tiple distributed generators under lightning weather conditions. Firstly, a method based on Latin hypercube sampling is proposed to calculate the number of distribution line trips in a specific area under lightning weather. Subsequently, a fault restoration decision model for the distribution network under line trip failures is established, which is formulated as a relaxed mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP) problem. This formulation allows for easy resolution using off-the-shelf optimization tools. The proposed method determines the restored topology, the critical loads to be restored, and the power output of the distributed generators. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through numerical simulations on the modified 32-bus test system.

articleTitle: Thevenin Equivalent Impedance Online Identification with Fluctuations on Both Grid and Source Sides
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The power grid integration performance of renewable energy such as wind power is sensitive to the strength of the grid. As an important indicator of the grid strength at the wind farm point of connection, the online identification of grid Thevenin equivalent impedance at the grid side of wind farm is of great significance for risk assessment and strategy optimization of wind power integration system. Firstly, the principle of Thevenin equivalent impedance identification is introduced and the impacts and variation of fluctuation on both grid and source sides on identification accuracy of equivalent impedance are revealed. It clarifies the principle of data screening for the accurate identification of equivalent impedance and online application. Then, a data screening strategy is designed, and an online identification method of grid impedance under source side and grid side fluctuations is proposed. Finally, the proposed method is verified by a simulation scenario with disturbances on both grid and source sides.

articleTitle: Topology Analysis of A High-Gain Isolated DC/DC Converter Based on Graph Theory Simplification
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this paper, a graph theory-based topology simplification approach is used to improve the converter structure. By simplifying the converter structure, the converter can realize the same function using fewer switching devices. In this paper, a new isolated step-up DC/DC converter is designed. It has the advantages of high output voltage gain and small size because it does not depend on the isolation transformer for boosting. Finally, its correctness is verified by Simulink simulation.

articleTitle: Safety and Reliability Credit Evaluation of Secure Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The proportion of coal power generation in the total power generation is close to sixty percent, and coal power generation is the main source of safe and reliable supply in China. In actual production and operation, it is necessary to evaluate the performance credit of coal power generation enterprises and clarify reward and punishment measures to urge secure power supply sources to consciously fulfill power contracts, and abide by trading order. This article formulates a credit evaluation process for safe and reliable power supply, including evaluation criteria such as accuracy of operational parameter declaration, cyber security management, performance deviation rate, equipment reliability, reduced output operation, implementation of dispatch management measures, electricity-coal supply indicators, and a penalty indicator for false information declaration. The rating is divided into five levels based on the total evaluation score, and the evaluation results are linked to the performance guarantee amount, priority electricity plan, auxiliary service assessment fee coefficient, and government supervision, with clear reward and punishment measures.

articleTitle: Coordinated Power Control Architecture for Parallel Matrix Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This article first proposes an isolated grid-connected multi-port energy router based on parallel matrix converters. In the future power system, energy routers for comprehensive management of multiple renewable energy will gradually shift from non-isolated to isolated system which is able to achieve electrical isolation and higher safety for energy sources like lithium batteries and hydrogen production systems. Isolation type multi-port converters are gradually moving towards modularity and compatibility with multiple converters, such as matrix converters with integrated AC/DC characteristics. On the basis of proposed novel multi-port converter, its corresponding coordinated control strategy featuring reasonably utilizing the three control variables to simplify the whole modulation algorithm is developed in this paper. The novel regulation scheme can achieve the coordinated regulation of three modules which can achieve different control goals of highly sinusoidal grid current, stable load voltage, and lifetime improvement.

articleTitle: Research on Idle Load Grid-Connected Control Strategy of Variable Speed Constant Frequency Wind Power Generation System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The doubly-fed wind turbine, recognized for its wide operational speed range, high energy utilization rate, soft grid connection, and adjustable power factor, represents a mainstream choice in wind energy technology. This paper focuses on the modeling and simulation of a variable speed constant frequency doubly-fed wind turbine system. The research encompasses the development of a mathematical model for the grid-connected doubly-fed generator, the design of a control strategy based on stator flux-oriented vector control for the idle load grid-connected mode, and the simulation of the model using S-functions in MATLAB. The simulation results demonstrate that the synchronization time of the stator voltage with the grid side voltage is extremely brief during the idle load grid-connection process. Moreover, the system is capable of maintaining stator voltage synchronization with the grid side voltage even in the event of sudden wind speed changes. Furthermore, even with a voltage difference of 0.1V between the stator and the dq-axis on the grid side, grid connection can be achieved within 0.2 seconds.

articleTitle: Research on Fault Identification Method of Transmission Line Based on CEEMDAN and Current Traveling Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of unsatisfactory identification of transmission line fault diagnosis based on transient current traveling wave, a time series denoising method based on the combination of CEEMDAN and Pearson's correlation coefficient with a feature extraction method is proposed to realize the accurate diagnosis of transmission line fault types. First, the original transient current traveling wave signals collected by the distributed fault monitoring system of the transmission line are decomposed by CEEMDAN to derive the IMF components, and then by calculating the correlation coefficients of each IMF component, the IMF components with lower correlation are discarded and the original signals are reconstructed. Finally, the XGBoost machine learning model is used to identify the reconstructed signal and realize the fine diagnosis of transmission line faults. Comparison experiments with different models show that the method proposed in this paper has better diagnostic effect.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of V-shaped IPMSMs with Asymmetric and Symmetric Rotors
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of three interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSM) featuring distinct rotor configurations, including symmetric rotor IPM, asymmetric rotor IPM, and asymmetric IPM equipped with hybrid permanent magnets. With a unified stator structure and consistent testing conditions, the air-gap magnetic field performance, torque output characteristics, operation efficiency map, demagnetization performance, mechanical stress, and manufacturing cost are thoroughly compared. Based on the above evaluation, the advantages of asymmetric rotor design using magnetic field shift (MFS) effect and hybrid permanent magnets are verified, particularly in enhancing torque density and suppressing torque ripple. Ultimately, this study comprehensively evaluates three topologies and identifies directions for future design improvements.

articleTitle: Research on Ash Cleaning Technology Based on Thyristor Converter Valve TCU
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In transmission lines, converter stations usually play the role of converting alternating current and direct current. The converter valve is the core equipment. In the case of long-term operation, the converter valve in the valve hall has serious dust accumulation, which may cause the occurrence of flashover and affect the stability of power supply in the power system. Therefore, it is necessary to carry out regular cleaning of the valve hall equipment. When cleaning the electrical equipment in the valve hall, it is usually necessary to carry out a power-off operation, which consumes a lot of manpower and material resources, and affects the transmission efficiency. This paper proposes an efficient purge cleaning method, which greatly shortens the traditional cleaning method to two working days. It improves the efficiency of maintenance work and ensures the reliability of power supply.

articleTitle: Distributed Control Strategy of DC Microgrid with CPL Based on Convex Relaxation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: For the direct current(DC) microgrid contanining constant power loads(CPLs), this paper proposes a novel distributed control strategy employing the convex relaxation approach, which enables the system to stabilize at the position of the optimal power flow(OPF) solution. For the non-convex OPF problem, the first step is to convexify it using an appropriate convex relaxation method and verify the accuracy of the proposed convex relaxation method at the same time. Secondly, the Karush- Kuhn-Tucker(KKT) optimality conditions of the relaxation problem are solved, and the results are equivalently transformed to identify the synchronization term that can be utilized in the control strategy, so as to achieve distributed control under optimal power flow. Finally, the proposed control strategy is verified using simulation examples and numerical analysis.

articleTitle: Study on Lightning Intrusion Wave Overvoltage of DC Filter in Ultra High Voltage Direct Current Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: As an important equipment of the converter station, the DC filter bears the overvoltage of the lightning invasion wave on the DC line. It is very important to study the overvoltage of the lightning invasion wave under different operating conditions. This paper introduces the configuration of the DC filter and the lightning arrester in the UHVDC transmission system, and establishes the simulation model of the DC filter under different operating conditions. Through the analysis and calculation of the overvoltage of the lightning invasion wave in four operating conditions of the single stage, the data of the overvoltage of the lightning intrusion waves at each point of the DC filter are obtained. The research results provide a theoretical basis for HVDC transmission system's DC filter's lightning intrusion wave overvoltage.

articleTitle: Impedance Network Modeling of GFL and GFM Converters System Considering AC/DC Couplings
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid development of grid-forming (GFM) control technology, integrating GFM control into grid-following (GFL) control-dominated systems has been attached with great importance due to the enhancement of grid supporting capability. To keep the normal operation of such GFL/GFM hybrid system, its small-signal stability needs to be studied, while the current research mainly focuses on the GFL/GFM converters' ac-side dynamics and usually ignore their ac/dc couplings. Therefore, this paper proposes an impedance network modeling method for GFL/GFM multi-converters system, and then a nodal admittance matrix retaining both ac and dc nodes is obtained. With such model, system marginal unstable condition can be accurately determined. Further, the influence of the capacity ratio between GFL and GFM converter is discussed. Simulation results of a typical GFL/GFM hybrid system verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis of Multi-Machine Power Systems Based on Sum of Squares Programming and Coherency Dynamic Equivalents
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Transient stability analysis (TSA) of large-scale power systems is one of the most computationally significant tasks. To reduce the difficulty of this task, this paper uses a coherency-based dynamic equivalent method to obtain the aggregation model of multi-machine systems, which is a valid approach to reducing the size of power system model. Based on this aggregation model, the expanding annular domain (EAD) algorithm based on sum of squares (SOS) programming is employed to estimate the domain of attraction (DA) of the aggregation model, which provides an approximate description of transient stability of the original system model. The validity of our proposed methodology is illustrated on a 15-machine 73-bus system. Simulation results show that the proposed method can provide better estimates in terms of DA and critical clearing time (CCT) for large-scale power systems.

articleTitle: Short Term Load Forecasting Based on Data Driven
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: It is difficult to process large data volume by using traditional short term power load forecasting model which is provided with strong randomness and the forecasting accuracy is hard to satisfy the requirements of the smart grid. Therefore, this paper proposes a kind of data-driven short term load forecasting method based on the gated recurrent unit (GRU) neural network to predict power load in some area and make comparative analysis on the forecasting results with the results of the traditional method. The comparison results indicate the proposed method takes into full consideration of the time sequence and nonlinear of power load and is feasible in deeply excavating data characteristics of power consumers. Meanwhile, the short term forecasting property of this method is superior to the traditional method and is able to meet the demand of the smart grid for high precision.

articleTitle: Impedance Modelling and Stability Analysis of Joint Photovoltaic and Battery Based Energy Storage System Under Weak Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In conventional grid-following (GFL) photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems, power fluctuations can be smoothed by attaching grid-forming (GFM) energy storage (ES) converter. In heterogeneous systems containing GFL and GFM converters, the output impedance model and the cascade system stability criterion can be utilized to study the grid-connected stability of the system. However, most of the existing impedance models are single-machine impedance models or simple parallel models that do not fully consider the frequency coupling effect between different converters and grid impedance, making it difficult to accurately assess the stability of heterogeneous systems under high grid impedance. In view of this, taking the two-machine heterogeneous grid-connected system as an example, this paper analyzes the coupling effect between the output impedance of the system and the grid impedance, and finds that the grid impedance has an additional effect on the output impedance of the paralleled system. Based on this, the small disturbances stability of the paralleled system under weak grid is discussed. The results of the simulation experiments show that the stability analysis based on the improved impedance model in this paper realizes the accurate judgment of small disturbance stability of the system under weak grid.

articleTitle: Dynamic Model Construction of Surge Arrester Based on W-MOPSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Metal oxide surge arresters are of great significance for surge arrester configuration, insulation coordination research, and system reliability calculation. Their accurate modeling depends on precise parameter calculation, and model parameter optimization is a complex multi-objective optimization problem. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-objective particle swarm optimization method based on the Weighted Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (W-MOPSO) algorithm to optimize the parameters of the surge arrester dynamic model. This allows the surge arrester dynamic model to be applicable to steep lightning current simulation, lightning current simulation, and switching current transient simulation simultaneously. The W-MOPSO algorithm performs Pareto dominance ranking on the global optimal solution of the weighted sum of multiple objective functions to obtain a Pareto optimal solution set. Finally, the model construction and parameter optimization analysis are performed using the YH5WZ-17/45 surge arrester as an example. By comparing the predicted residual voltage with the experimental results and comparing the optimization effects of four different algorithms, the surge arrester dynamic model optimized by the proposed algorithm can make the absolute value of the relative average error of multiple optimization objectives less than 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>/0, effectively promoting the optimization of dynamic surge arrester modeling parameters and ensuring the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling and Simulation of a Variable Speed Pumped Storage Unit along with Experimental Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This article studies the method of constructing a refined numerical model of water, machinery, and electricity for a variable speed pumped storage unit based on the MATLAB platform. Firstly, the overall model architecture of the variable speed pumped storage unit is introduced, including the hydraulic mechanical subsystem and the electrical subsystem. The hydraulic mechanical subsystem mainly consists of modules such as water pump turbines, upstream and downstream reservoirs, pressure pipelines, pressure regulating chambers, and speed controllers, while the electrical subsystem includes modules such as doubly fed induction motors, inverters, and power grids. Subsequently, the mathematical models and control strategies of the doubly fed induction motor and inverter in the electrical side model were elaborated, as well as the modeling methods of the water pump turbine, pressure pipeline, regulating chamber, upstream and downstream reservoirs, and governor in the hydraulic mechanical side module. Among them, the water pump turbine adopts the improved Suter curve processing method, while the pressure pipeline and regulating chamber are modeled based on the characteristic line method (MOC). Experimental comparisons were conducted using the empirical platform of variable speed pumped storage units at the National Key Laboratory of Hydraulic Engineering, Wuhan University. The experimental results show that under the two control strategies of power priority and speed priority, the model simulation results are highly consistent with the physical experimental results, with a maximum error of no more than 10%, verifying the reliability and accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: A Differential Protection of High-Penetration Active Distribution Network Based on Adaptive Braking Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to solve the problem that classical current protection is difficult to apply when a large number of inverter-interfaced distributed generations (IIDGs) are connected to distribution network, A novel scheme of current differential protection based on adaptive braking coefficients is proposed. The protection scheme adapts the braking coefficient based on the phase difference and amplitude ratio of positive-sequence current fault components on both ends of the protected line. The simulation results in PSCAD show that compared with classical differential protection scheme, the proposed protection scheme effectively meets the protection requirements of active distribution networks across various fault scenarios, offering high sensitivity, reliability, and resistance to transition resistance.

articleTitle: A Control Method Based on Improved Cuckoo Algorithm for Photovoltaic Hybrid Hydrogen Production System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In view of control issues associated with renewable energy hydrogen production systems, this study focuses on the hybrid hydrogen production system consisting of a photovoltaic-ALK +PEM electrolyzers and proposes a power control strategy based on the improved cuckoo algorithm. By implementing this control method in the DC-DC converters of electrolyzers, the system achieves stable operation and rapid convergence of DC bus voltage. Compared to PI control, the control scheme based on the improved cuckoo algorithm comprehensively enhances the system's performance, ensuring swift stability of DC bus voltage and precise control outcomes. This proposed method not only realizes coordinated control of multiple types of electrolyzers, but also considers the system's rapid response capability and anti-interference ability during the entire process.

articleTitle: Research of Parallel Cable Crosstalk Characteristics Based on TLM
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With regard to the parallel wire crosstalk problem in electrical and electronic systems, the degree of wire crosstalk decreases with increasing wire spacing, but when the spacing increases to 10 cm, increasing the spacing no longer effectively reduces crosstalk. The degree of wire crosstalk increases with increasing wire length and wire ground height, with a linear increase with increasing wire ground height. The phenomenon of wire crosstalk exhibits cyclical changes with changing signal frequencies, with a periodic variation frequency approximately equal to the frequency value corresponding to twice the wire length when electromagnetic waves have wavelength of the wire. Crosstalk voltages at the integer multiples of the frequency value appear in the vicinity of the maximum crosstalk voltage. This article uses the transmission line matrix (TLM) method to calculate the effects of cable type, wire spacing distance, wire length, and wire ground height on wire crosstalk, and explores effective methods for reducing wire crosstalk. Research shows that in comparison to increasing the spacing distance, selecting cables with an anti-interference layer is an effective method for reducing crosstalk. Coaxial cables have the best anti-interference performance, and can reduce near-end crosstalk voltage to 0.02 V.

articleTitle: 3D Pairwise Point Cloud Registration Network for Power Equipment Based on Multi-scale Features
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The diverse range of power equipment, each with its unique shape, poses a challenge for precise registration. This paper advances a 3D paired point cloud alignment model that is founded on multi-scale feature extraction, attempting to alleviate the negative impact of outliers from two aspects. Initially, a multi-scale feature extraction model is formulated to enhance structural information across various levels, thereby enhancing the discriminative capabilities of point features. Secondly, the transformation matrix is utilized to extract the internal points of the source and target point cloud. A constraint function is then incorporated to steer the registration process, enhancing the inductive bias of the model and augmenting its generalization capabilities. Finally, the applicability of this method is verified on power automation equipment of various shapes. Experimental conclusions indicate that the method which described in this paper attains an MAE value of 0.31 on the ModelNet40 dataset, while also effectively registering previously unseen power equipment, showing good generalization ability and practical application potential.

articleTitle: Fault Current Limiting Control for AC Side of MMC-HVDC Based on Switched Bang-Bang Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Limiting the fault current level of modular multilevel converter (MMC) high-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems is beneficial to reduce the cost of current limiting devices and alleviate the stringent protection time constraints. In this paper, a fault current-limiting strategy based on switched bang-bang control for the AC side of MMC-HVDC system is proposed. The proposed method in this paper is capable of limiting the fault current to an acceptable range within short time. And it not depend on exact system model with a simple control law and small computation. In MMC-HVDC system, the designed switched bang-bang control scheme limits output current of system when it is detected to be overcurrent, and the vector controller is used during normal operation. The performance of the switched bang-bang control strategy is verified by time domain simulation using PSCAD.

articleTitle: Finite-time Control Strategy for Electro-hydraulic Servo Systems Considering Output Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: A finite-time control method based on the barrier Lyapunov function is proposed for the output constraints and external load disturbances existing in the steam turbine electro-hydraulic servo system. Firstly, the barrier Lyapunov function with constraint boundary is constructed, and the problem that the output of the system may be destroyed, leading to performance degradation, is solved by the parameter setting of the boundary function. Secondly, a finite-time controller is designed based on the finite-time control theory and combined with the backstepping construction method to solve the influence of disturbances on the stability and tracking accuracy of the system in the steam turbine electro-hydraulic servo system, and the finite-time stability of the closed-loop system is proved by stability analysis. Finally, the simulation results show that for an electro-hydraulic servo system with output constraints, the control strategy proposed in this paper allows the system's position output to quickly track the desired trajectory in a short period. The barrier Lyapunov function can make the system output satisfy the constraints, and the finite-time controller based on the barrier Lyapunov function can make the system track the upper desired trajectory quickly and accurately with strong robustness.

articleTitle: A Multi-objective Optimization Strategy for Building Energy Performance Based on Adaptive Thermal Comfort Considering Different Climatic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems can affect indoor thermal comfort and building energy efficiency significantly. However, previous approaches lead to high energy costs Thus, this paper proposes an optimization strategy for HV AC systems to decline energy consumption while ensuring adaptive thermal comfort in different climate regions. In this paper, we create two different usage building models. NSGA- II is executed within the MATLAB environment to tackle the optimization process that couples supply air velocity and temperature setpoints. The proposed optimization strategy defined adaptive indoor thermal comfort boundary and decreased energy consumption significantly of the HVAC system compared to the conventional control strategy. It is found through investigations that the proposed strategy can effectively reduce energy consumption by up to 15.92% compared to mixed-mode ventilation. Results also establish that the proposed strategy is more effective in office buildings and colder areas. Simulation results verify the validity of the strategy.

articleTitle: Data-driven Condition-based Maintenance Schedules of Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Scientific maintenance schedules are an effective way to reduce maintenance costs and promote asset management efficiency in distribution networks. With the increasing integration of a large number of stochastic distributed generators (DGs), the deterioration rate of distribution equipment may accelerate significantly owing to heavy/over loading. Conventionally, the distribution networks maintenance scheduling is based on run-to-failure or simplified scheduled maintenance strategies, without considering the integration of DGs and the health condition of distribution equipment. In this paper, the Markov decision model is applied to formulate the condition-based maintenance scheduling problem of active distribution networks. The operation of DGs and failure probability of distribution equipment are considered. The Q-learning method is adopted to optimize the maintenance schedules. Case studies show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Small-Step Real-Time Simulation for VSC Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The voltage source converter (VSC) has been widely used in the new power system. Its electromagnetic transient simulation has the characteristics of low simulation speed and high resource consumption. In this paper, the small-step real-time simulator for VSC based on field programmable gate array (FPGA) is established. Firstly, the fixed-admittance model for VSC is established to improve the calculation speed of the primary system. At the same time, the parallel computing process of the primary system is designed to achieve small-step real-time computing of the primary system for VSC based on the parallel computing architecture of FPGA. Secondly, according to the logic of the control system for VSC, the serial-parallel computing process of the control system is designed, and the controller for VSC is implemented based on FPGA. Finally, the performance of the established FPGA simulator is verified based on the control experiments on PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Designing Transient Stability Controllers for Power Systems via Sum-of-Squares Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Traditional stability controllers are constructed based on the equilibrium points of power systems and fail to meet the performance criteria under large disturbances. In this paper, an algorithm has been proposed to design transient stability controllers for power system using Sum-of-squares (SOS) programming which is a powerful technique able to answer many analysis questions for nonlinear systems. Since the SOS programming only deals with polynomial systems, first we recast the power system model into polynomial form. Then we derive the algorithm from the Lyapunov Theory to search for stability controllers of power systems, by introducing the so-called target region and expanding the estimated stability region. The effectiveness of our algorithm is demonstrated on the IEEE 3-machine-9-bus power system.

articleTitle: Design of Flexible Interconnection Nodes in a Regional Multi-Energy Hybrid Energy Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the wide application of distributed power generation and energy storage devices, the construction of energy Internet based on new energy and Internet technologies has been developing rapidly. The design of power routers connecting power grids, distributed power generation devices, energy storage devices and loads can meet the demand for energy interconnection, thus realizing the optimal scheduling and management of power consumption by loads and power generation by distributed power sources. This paper proposes the basic composition of a community energy network, with the power router as its smallest terminal to control and dispatch the home power generation system. On the basis of analyzing the design requirements of the power router, we propose a plug-and-play, multi-input and multi-output power router scheme based on solid-state transformers to realize the connection of new energy outputs, energy storage devices and loads of the home power generation system, and to carry out unified control and scheduling.

articleTitle: TiO2 Modified Self-Healing Microcapsules Based on Microfluidic Techniques Achieving UV-Induced Healing in Dielectric Polymers
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Dielectric polymers, widely used in various applications, are often subjected to prolonged mechanical, electrical, and thermal stresses, which can result in minor localized damage and increase the risk of insulation failure. To address this, we have developed self-healing microcapsules using micro fluidic techniques. These microcapsules are designed to rupture upon slight damage to the polymers, releasing the core repair agent that fills and cures the damaged area under external UV light. To enhance the UV protection of the repair agent, TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles were incorporated into the microcapsule shell, acting as a UV shielding medium. The self-healing capacity and intrinsic properties of the microcapsules and their composites were evaluated using scanning electron microscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, broadband dielectric spectroscopy, and a power frequency breakdown test platform. The results demonstrate that the inclusion of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles provides effective UV shielding, preserving the reactivity of the core repair agent. Consequently, the composite materials not only achieve self-healing of mechanical damage but also maintain the excellent intrinsic properties of dielectric polymers.

articleTitle: Will Grid Construction Keep Up with the Pace of AI Development?
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, its dependence on electricity is also deepening. The development trend of AI shows that the demand for computing power will increase sharply in the future, which will lead to a significant increase in the power consumption of AI systems. At present, the development of global energy construction and transmission and distribution networks faces huge challenges. Especially in the context of renewable energy gradually replacing traditional energy, how to ensure the continuous supply of energy and the stable operation of transmission and distribution networks has become a crucial issue. This paper deeply analyzes the latest trends in the development of AI technology, focusing on the demand and consumption of AI for power resources, and compares it with the current energy generation, revealing the possible imbalance between supply and demand in the future. At the same time, this paper also evaluates the current status of energy construction and transmission and distribution network infrastructure, and explores its development potential and trends. By comparing the changes in energy generation and AI power consumption, the support capacity of the existing power grid for future load growth is analyzed. Results show that although the construction of energy and transmission and distribution networks is advancing rapidly, there may still be a risk of lag in the face of the rapid growth of electricity demand brought about by AI technology. This requires relevant departments to adopt more proactive strategies to accelerate the construction of energy infrastructure and the intelligent upgrade of power grids to ensure that the power grid can keep up with the speed of AI development and achieve stable and reliable energy supply.

articleTitle: Grid-Connected Operation Control Technology of Doubly-Fed Wind Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the aggravation of the energy crisis, wind energy has attracted the attention of all countries. The traditional wind turbine has low efficiency and large reactive power, which affects the productivity and grid-connected reliability. This paper puts forward a control strategy of Double Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) system, which realizes constant frequency by rotor excitation compensation for speed difference, and controls speed by adjusting output power to meet the maximum output power of wind turbine. The specifics of the paper are as follows. Firstly, this paper introduces the main components of DFIG system, the model of the system in dq coordinate axis and the theory of maximum wind energy tracking. Secondly, sinusoidal vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM), grid-side converter modeling, and control strategy are presented. Then, the modeling, control strategy and simulation of rotor-side converter are introduced. Finally, the whole model is built and simulated, and the results meet the target.

articleTitle: Research of Pumped Storage Governor System Based on Adaptive Variable Parameter Control Law
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the accelerated construction of new power systems, pumped storage systems need to be further upgraded. The governor system is an important part of pumped storage units. In order to optimize its configuration structure and speed control accuracy, this paper optimizes two regulation methods. One is an adaptive variable parameter PID control law based on unit frequency, and the other is an adaptive variable parameter PI control law based on unit power. This article specifically studies the high-precision control algorithm and corresponding hardware components of a high-precision speed controller system. The application results show that the method proposed in this article can effectively improve the synchronization control accuracy and optimize system efficiency.

articleTitle: A Rolling Prediction Method for Distribution Network Load Based on PID Control Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Load forecasting in distribution networks plays a crucial role in their operation. Addressing the limitations of data-based forecasting methods, such as data dependency and lack of interpretability, this paper proposes a tracking prediction method based on control theory. The stability and steady-state error of the proposed method are theoretically validated. Finally, the proposed method is compared with AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average(ARIMA), AutoRegressive Distributed Lag(ARDL), and Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM) in terms of forecasting performance using actual load data. The results show that the proposed method achieves smaller forecasting errors and significantly reduces computation time compared to deep learning-based methods such as LSTM. This new approach provides a novel perspective for power load forecasting.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of Substation Communication Network Based on Fault Tree and Minimum Cut Set Method
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Digital substations use communication networks instead of hard wiring to achieve information sharing, but require higher reliability. This article takes the protection system of a classic digital substation as the research object, and uses fault tree and minimum cut set method to calculate its reliability. Firstly, study the three-layer structure of classic digital substations and construct equivalent models of equipment components at each level. Then, based on the equivalent models of each component, a fault tree is drawn, and the minimum cut set is determined through the fault tree. Finally, the reliability of the digital substation protection system is calculated using the minimum cut set method. The calculation example shows that the reliability of the classic digital substation protection system using a dual redundant communication network structure is even better than that of traditional substations.

articleTitle: A Numeric Study of Long-Cycle Energy Storage Planning for Power Grids with High Penetration of Renewable Energy on a Full-Horizon Operation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: For large-scale renewable energy bases primarily intended to supply power to the mains grid, they exhibit high local renewable energy penetration rates and exhibit seasonal and volatile output characteristics. Therefore, energy storage configurations need to be based on the characteristics of renewable energy generation and the operation strategies of the mains grid. Renewable energy has obvious seasonal characteristics in power generation and possesses fluctuations when integrated into the grid. These characteristics put forward two challenges for energy storage planning: a. developing an energy storage planning model that integrates operational characteristics and b. addressing the seasonal and fluctuations of renewable energy in medium- and long-term energy storage planning. To summarize, simply embedding operation strategy into the planning model is no longer sufficient to characterize these operational properties, while the multitude of operational scenarios seriously prolongs the solution time. A two-dimensionally clustered unit commitment model is employed from a previous study to plan the energy storage for a power grid with large-scale renewable integration in this paper. The model emphasizes the importance of tailoring energy storage configurations to the specific generation and operational characteristics of the mains grid. The paper highlights the practical application of a comprehensive approach that considers both the fluctuations and the seasonal variations in renewable energy generation, and it underscores the role of advanced planning models in optimizing energy storage solutions to ensure the reliability of the power grid.

articleTitle: A Method to Improve the Torque Density of the Multiple-pole Few-slot PMSM with Unequal Tooth Pitch
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To enhance the torque density of the multiple-pole few-slot PMSM with unequal tooth pitch, a special stator structure containing additional teeth is proposed. Initially, a magnetic field model of the motor is developed, analyzing the magnetic flux density distribution under no-load conditions. The analytical expression for the no-load flux per phase is derived and corrected using the magnetic circuit method. Factors influencing the flux magnitude are examined to determine the optimal angle for the additional teeth. Finally, finite element simulation is employed for validation. The no-load back electromotive force (EMF) of the motor with various additional tooth angles is compared to that of a motor without additional teeth. Simulation results indicate that the optimal angle of the additional teeth aligns well with theoretical values, and the additional tooth structure significantly enhances the no-load back EMF, demonstrating a substantial improvement in motor torque density.

articleTitle: A VDCOL Improvement Strategy for CLCC with Improved Inputs
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission technology based on controllable line commutated converter (CLCC) avoids the problem of conventional DC phase commutation failure and provides a brand new way for HVDC transmission to the grid. A voltage dependent current order limiter(VDCOL) optimization control method based on the improved input, which improves the fault response characteristics of CLCC and increases the AC voltage recovery speed of the receiving end grid, is proposed with respect to the technical characteristics of the CLCC controlled converter. Finally, a unipolar CLCC-HVDC simulation model is established to verify the effectiveness and universality of the optimal control based on PSCAD (power systems computer aided design) simulation software.

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Power Prediction Based on STL-AOA-Transformer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Precise short-term wind power forecasting plays a crucial role in ensuring the effective and secure functioning of wind power installations. To improve the accuracy of short-term wind power forecasts, in this paper, a hybrid short-term wind power forecasting model STL-AOA-Transformer based on seasonal and trend decomposition using Loess (STL), arithmetic optimization algorithm (AOA) and transformer is proposed. AOA is used to optimize the parameters of transformer. STL is employed for the purpose of breaking down the initial data into modal components characterized by reduced volatility, in order to effectively capture the data features. These modal components are then fed into the AOA- Transformer for the prediction of short-term wind power and the subsequent derivation of the ultimate forecasted value. The efficacy of the model was assessed through testing and validation using authentic data spanning four seasons and four stations, and compared to three other models. The results show that the model fits the data well and has high prediction accuracy, which has important practical value.

articleTitle: Anti-Disturbance Current Regulation Strategy for LCL-Filtered Single-Phase Inverters Based on Constant Funnel Bang-Bang Control
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper proposes a constant funnel bang-bang control based current regulation strategy for LCL-filtered single-phase inverters subject to unknown disturbance. First, the dynamic mathematical model of the inverter system is established in a single-input, single-output form. Accordingly, the bang-bang current controller (BCC) is designed, which can guarantee global stability, produce high-quality output current, and exhibit strong robustness against disturbances, as it does not depend on the accurate system model. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of the Combustion and Thermoacoustic Characteristics in an Annular Combustor with Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Low emission combustion technology for gas turbine and aero-engine industrial has attracted more and more attention by the aeronautic community. Hydrogen fuel is believed being a promising alternative fuel for gas turbines and aero-engines in the next generation of propulsion system. In this work, a novel type of annular combustor with multi-point direct injection (MDI) burners for burning pure hydrogen is proposed for gas turbines and aero-engines. The MDI burner is featured with several multi-point injectors arranged in inclined direction, which forms a swirling flow to enhance the mixing process of hydrogen and air. Meanwhile, the MDI burners are beneficial for flame stability and preventing flashback. The flow structure, combustion process and NOx emission of a single MDI burner are numerically studied with hydrogen fuel under different air flow rate Qair and the equivalence ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\phi$</tex>. Then, the cold flow and combustion characteristics of the annular combustor with 12 MDI burners are investigated by the steady RANS method to understand the flow structure, temperature field and NOx emission under different operation conditions. Furthermore, the thermoacoustic property of the annular combustor is investigated to obtain the acoustic modes, including the longitudinal modes and azimuthal modes.

articleTitle: A New Type of Prefabricated Cabin Monitoring System for Distribution Rooms
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In response to the common problems of low work efficiency and difficult quality assurance in traditional equipment operation status monitoring systems for prefabricated cabins in distribution rooms, a new type of monitoring system for prefabricated cabins in distribution rooms is proposed by adding infrared dual view, intelligent air switch, air conditioning controller, and connecting sensors such as temperature and humidity sensors, door status sensors, water immersion sensors, and smoke monitoring sensors to the intelligent gateway of the distribution network. The system adopts a message integrity authentication method to prevent some key information from being maliciously tampered with by third parties, thereby improving the intelligent monitoring level of prefabricated cabins in distribution rooms.

articleTitle: Distributed Control Method for Multi-User Side Energy Storage SOC Based on Consensus Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In recent years, user-side energy storage has developed rapidly and is widely used to save electricity costs for industrial and commercial users. Compared with source-side and grid-side centralised energy storage, user-side energy storage is more decentralised, with smaller single capacity and larger quantity, which is not easy to carry out centralised regulation and control. In contrast, the distributed control method has the characteristics of strong control robustness and stability, which is more suiTABLE as the SOC coordinated control of a large number of distributed energy storage. In this paper, a distributed energy storage SOC coordinated control algorithm based on improved consensus algorithm is designed, which can achieve SOC consensus control of multiple user-side energy storage, and compared with the centralised control scheme, it has the features of small computation amount of the central controller and strong robustness of the controller. Simulation results show that the distributed energy storage SOC coordinated control algorithm based on the improved consensus algorithm designed in this paper can effectively achieve the consistent control of multiple user-side energy storage in the station area.

articleTitle: Extended State Observer Based Super Twisting Sliding Mode Control of SMES-DVR For Sensitive Load Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Dynamic voltage restorer with superconducting magnet energy storage reduces the coupling between the DVR and the power grid, offering greater toughness and a wider voltage compensation range. For SMES, the DVR grid-connected inverter part can be regarded as the power electronic load. SMES-DVR compensates for voltage dips with transient energy exchanges between the SMES and the grid. The nonlinearity, parameter uncertainty, and load disturbance of the DVR system will make it difficult to track the reference signal and keep DC-link voltage at the desired value. Hence, an efficient controller must be designed to compensate the intricate correlation related to the SMES-DVR. A novel sliding mode controller is proposed for SMES-DVR based on the super-twisting sliding mode controller (STSMC) and extended state observer (ESO).
