The proposed controller not only can regulate the DC-link voltage tending to target value with a shorter transition time and smaller overshoot, but also has a strong anti-interference ability because of the disturbance estimation of the extended state observer. Finally, the simulation results based on MATLAB/Simulink indicate that SMES-DVR with the proposed SMC controller can promptly compensate for the voltage sags/swells of the sensitive loads and effectively reduce the total harmonic distortion.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment and Control Method for High Load Transmission Lines Based on Feasible Control Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the risk assessment of power system lines, the probability and severity of risk occurrence are two important indicators for measuring operational safety. In order to increase the reliability of high load operation of power lines, the risk of voltage and power exceeding limits during line operation is calculated and analyzed, and the power grid is scheduled and controlled under reliability requirements. This article proposes a risk assessment and control method for high load transmission lines based on feasible control domains. The developed risk assessment model comprehensively takes into account the likelihood and potential impact of load fluctuations. The simulation analysis of the IEEE33 bus system shows that the increase in load will affect the risk index of line overload. Based on risk assessment in the feasible control domain, controlling the line can improve the stability of the system and increase the safety of the power system.

articleTitle: Integrated Energy System Flexible Energy Resource Optimal Scheduling Based on Stackelberg Game
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The full utilization of flexible energy resources is an important way to improve energy utilization efficiency, promote energy transformation and promote the goal of “dual carbon”. In this paper, carbon emission trading (CET) and green certificate trading (GCT) are incorporated into the low-carbon economic scheduling model with integrated energy system (IES) energy flexible energy resources. In addition, this paper comprehensively considers the profit relationship between operators and energy suppliers, and solves the low-carbon economic scheduling model based on genetic algorithm-mixed integer linear programming (GA-MILP). The simulation experiment analysis shows that the low-carbon economic dispatching scheme in this paper can effectively guarantee the benefits of both operators and energy suppliers, and realize the energy saving and carbon reduction of the system.

articleTitle: An Overview of the Application of Game Theory in the Coupled Green Power-green Certificate-CCER Market
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The decision-making process in the green power-green certificate-CCER coupled market is subject to constraints and influences from a multitude of factors. Game theory, which studies the interactions of decision-making subjects and their equilibrium state, has been applied to a certain extent in the current transaction with the electricity spot market as the main body. Therefore, this paper provides an overview of the current state of game theory applications in the coupled green power - green certificate - CCER market. The game behavior in the coupled market is initially classified. Subsequently, the game strategies of generators and sellers under cooperative and non-cooperative relationships, the strategy choices of sellers and users based on the Stackelberg game, as well as the non-cooperative, cooperative and evolutionary game behaviors among generators and sellers are analyzed.

articleTitle: Abnormal Behavior Modelling of Electricity Market by Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The rapid development of electric power technology has exacerbated issues with anomalies in market transactions, making effective identification and regulation of these anomalies a pressing task. This study proposes a trading behavior analysis model for market players, leveraging a stepwise regression algorithm and introducing a monitoring module based on the ARM Cortex series microcontroller. The model enables deep assessment of transaction data, timely detection of anomalies, and pattern mining for accurate regulatory support. The monitoring module enhances real-time monitoring and dynamic feedback, leveraging the ARM Cortex microcontroller's efficient data processing and low-power characteristics. Experimental validation shows the model's significant advantages in evaluation and error control, effectively identifying anomalies and demonstrating its potential to enhance electricity market regulation.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Based on Nutcracker Optimization Algorithm Improved Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid expansion of photovoltaic power plants in recent years over the world, accurate power prediction of photovoltaic generation is essential for ensuring the safe operation of power grids, developing effective dispatching plans, emission reductions, smart grid integration, and enhancing the efficiency of renewable energy usage. To improve the accuracy of photovoltaic power prediction, this paper proposes a nutcracker optimization algorithm to finely tune the extended parameters and enhance the information-capturing ability of the bidirectional long short-term memory method. The results indicate that the proposed approach demonstrates superior performance in the photovoltaic power prediction task. Compared with the other recurrent neural network methods, the mean squared error does not exceed 546.81 kW2. The mean absolute error is 15.35 kW. The root mean square error is 45.93 kW, and the R2 value is greater than 0.98.

articleTitle: Detection Method of Abnormal Operation State of Power Metering Equipment Based on Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of low detection accuracy and slow detection speed when the existing detection methods detect the abnormal operation state of power metering equipment, an abnormal operation state detection method of power metering equipment based on extended Kalman filter is proposed. According to the operation principle of power metering equipment, set the operation state detection standard. The equivalent model is constructed according to the composition structure of power metering equipment, and the real-time operation data of each equipment component are collected and processed under the model. Using the extended Kalman filter algorithm, the operating state characteristics of power metering equipment are extracted, and the abnormal operating state detection results are obtained by comparing with the set standard. The experimental results show that the state quantity detection error and missed detection rate of the designed detection method are lower than the preset value, and the detection delay is less than 5.0s, that is, the accuracy and speed of the designed detection method meet the design and application requirements.

articleTitle: A Time-of-Use Pricing-Based Hybrid AC-DC Microgrid Photovoltaic and Storage Configuration Method for Wastewater Treatment Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the carbon peak action plan, it is proposed to accelerate the development of new power systems and actively promote ‘renewable energy + energy storage’ and integrated source-grid-load-storage systems. Wastewater treatment plants are crucial urban infrastructure with high and stable base loads, resulting in significant energy consumption. Some structures in wastewater treatment plants have ample space for photovoltaic installation, making the addition of solar and storage systems on existing or new buildings an effective means for reducing emissions and enhancing carbon reduction. This paper proposes a hybrid AC-DC microgrid for wastewater treatment plants, addressing their load and energy consumption issues. Based on the source-load-storage control method and time-of-use electricity price, a photovoltaic and energy storage capacity configuration method was proposed, which reduced system losses, reduced costs, and promoted the low-carbon transformation of wastewater treatment plants.

articleTitle: PWM Algorithm for Dual Three-Phase PMSM with Open-Delta Winding Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To address the challenge of deep field-weakening in traditional permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs), the third-harmonic-magnetic-field-based pole-change PMSMs has been proposed. The rotor's permanent magnets generate both a fundamental magnetic field and a significant third harmonic field, while the stator employs two sets of three-phase open-delta windings with a 30° phase shift. Due to the unique stator winding structure and the substantial third harmonic component in the rotor's magnetic field, large third harmonic currents are induced in the windings, causing additional copper losses. This paper presents two new six-phase PWM modulation algorithms and an Equally Amplitude Staircase Injection Modulation (EASIM) method to counteract the third harmonic currents. The proposed solutions are validated through simulations, confirming their correctness and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on Evaluation Index System of County Distribution Network Planning under New Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The traditional evaluation indicators for distribution network planning can no longer meet the needs of energy transformation, digital transformation, and intelligent enhancement in the distribution system. This paper summarizes the current planning evaluation index system, combines it with research findings of new power system evaluation indexes. It constructs a set of index system suitable for evaluating the new county power system's planning scheme. The goal is to expedite the construction of the new county power system and adapt to the new situation of county distribution network development. The indicator system, which consists of 12 secondary indicators and 55 tertiary indicators, is focused on the five dimensions of clean and low-carbon, security and abundance, supply and demand synergy, economic efficiency, adaptability, and intelligence. The entropy weighting method is used, using a specific planning scheme as an example, to confirm the viability and practicability of the suggested planning evaluation indicator system. This system can aid in the development of the new county electric power system and provide decision-making support for the planning scheme.

articleTitle: Building Energy Flexibility and Flexible Scheduling Potential Based on the Characteristics of Energy Use Behaviour
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to investigate the influence of energy consumers' behavior on the flexible load regulation potential of residential buildings, the residents' energy use behavior patterns was obtained through questionnaires, the K-means clustering algorithm was used to classify the energy use patterns, the evaluation indexes were established and then combined with simulation to explore the optimal scheduling potentials of various types of energy use patterns. The results show that when the constraints of “peak and valley tariff policy”, the objective of minimum electricity cost and the percentage of electricity cost reduction are used as the evaluation indexes for optimal scheduling of households with various energy use patterns, the households with the highest potential are those with the B2 pattern during winter working days, and the electricity cost can be reduced by 33% after the load flexible scheduling.

articleTitle: Open-Circuit Fault Ride-Through Strategy of a High-Frequency-Bus Based Multi-Active Bridge Converter with Decentralized Control
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the high penetration of various distributed energy sources and DC loads in modern power systems, multi-port converters have received extensive attention due to their bidirectional conversion and port isolation functions. Among them, the power converter with a high-frequency-bus structure based on the multi-active bridge (MAB) circuit has apparent advantages in the application of AC / DC hybrid systems due to its few transformation links and high power density. In practical applications, the blocking removal caused by sub-module open-circuit faults or other types of faults will cause transient impacts on non-fault modules, which in turn will cause system security problems. In order to ensure the stable operation of the power converter, this paper proposes an integral compensation fault ride-through strategy based on decentralized control. Its essence is to control the adaptive adjustment process of the sub-module by compensating the shift angle. The simulation results show that this strategy can suppress the transient impact of voltage and current after open-circuit faults to ensure the safe operation of non-fault ports.

articleTitle: Sustainable Clustering Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the modern field of power and renewable energy, advancements in data analysis technology are key to driving innovation and sustainable development. However, existing clustering algorithms and neural networks are inefficient and inaccurate when processing large-scale, high-dimensional data, and they consume significant computational resources. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Sustainable Clustering Neural Network (SCNN). By introducing Gaussian units based on joint Gaussian distribution and combining them with a max-pooling layer, we propose a universal clustering module with a competitive update mechanism. This module includes two sets of trainable parameters, allowing for flexible adjustment of the shape and position of the Gaussian distribution to fit different data distribution characteristics. During clustering, feature selection and dimensionality reduction are achieved through the max-pooling layer, effectively enhancing the model's clustering performance. The competitive update mechanism further promotes competition among Gaussian units, enabling each unit to focus more on specific clusters, thereby improving the accuracy and stability of the clustering results. Experiments on the MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets achieved clustering accuracies of 93.38% and 72.83%, respectively, demonstrating strong competitiveness compared to existing methods. The code is available at: https://github.com/ZS520L/HGL-CAE.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study on Full Position Automatic Welding Technology for Low Alloy Pressure Steel Pipe With Pad Groove Structure in Pumped Storage Power Station
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Pumped storage power stations have higher energy conversion efficiency and greater peak shaving capacity. They are currently the most mature, economically efficient, flexible, safe, long-lasting, environmentally friendly, and widely used energy storage technology. With the transformation of energy structure, pumped storage power stations have experienced rapid development. This article conducts research on the full position automatic welding technology of low-alloy pressure steel pipes with cushion plates and groove structures for pumped storage power stations. Through the blasting test of pressure steel pipe models, the feasibility of the full position automatic welding technology of the cushion plate groove structure is verified. The use of this technology can improve the welding efficiency and quality of low-alloy pressure steel pipes in pumped storage power stations. Promoting this technology can achieve single-sided welding and double-sided forming inside the pressure steel pipe, reducing the demand for external space of the pressure steel pipe during construction, thereby reducing the excavation section of the water conveyance tunnel and the amount of concrete backfilling work, which is of great significance for energy conservation and reducing project costs.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimal Power Flow Solution Using CSVPSO
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Optimal power flow (OPF) is essential for achieving the objectives of maximizing power security as well as minimizing fuel costs and emission amount of thermal plants. Few studies focus on the collaborative optimization of multi-objective OPF problems. In this paper, we improve the traditional particle swarm optimization (PSO) and adopt PSO of constriction ranges of search space and velocity (CSVPSO) to solve the problem. The problem is simulated on IEEE-30 node system. The result shows the advantages of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Flexible Power Load Control Based on Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The characteristics of high randomness and low controllability of new energy power generation have gradually increased the pressure on the supply and demand balance of the power grid and continued to rise in costs. Therefore, the stable control of building energy systems is considered to be an increasingly severe challenge. Using advanced control strategies to control building energy storage can significantly improve the building's energy flexibility, allowing the system to operate more stably. Reinforcement learning (RL) has been shown to be effective in smoothing out peaks in system power consumption. However, when energy management is expanded from a single building to a building cluster, uncoordinated control strategies for each building may lead to excessive peaks in the building cluster, negatively affecting the stability of the power grid. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a coordinated energy management method based on hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (HRL). Compared with traditional reinforcement learning (RL), HRL introduces a hierarchical structure so that each agent can learn information from other agents and can handle more complex and large-scale problems. The controller designed in this paper aims to optimize the energy consumption of each building while smoothing the overall load curve of the building complex. Experimental results show that compared with traditional rule-based manual optimization controllers, the HRL controller performs well in coordinating energy management, not only improving energy utilization efficiency but also enhancing the stability and reliability of the power grid.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Voltage Measurement System for Overhead Transmission Lines Based on Electric Field Integration Method
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The accurate measurement of line voltage is of great significance for power calculation, overvoltage online monitoring and relay protection. According to the conservatism of the space electric field of the transmission line, the feasibility of measuring the line voltage by the electric field integration method is theoretically verified. Established a vertical line with transmission lines perpendicular to the ground as the integration path. Based on the characteristics of electric field integration, a non-contact electric field sensor was designed. The measurement of the output electric field signal of the sensor node was completed through the designed multi-channel synchronous acquisition circuit, and the real-time calculation, waveform display and analysis of electric field integration were achieved. A three-phase horizontally arranged transmission line test platform was built, and the measurement test of transmission lines with different voltages was carried out. The feasibility of the proposed electric field integration method is proved by simulation and experiment, which provides another measurement method and system for non-contact voltage measurement.

articleTitle: Research on Distributed Control Algorithm of Virtual Power Plant Based on Communication -censored
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To improve the communication efficiency of distributed control algorithm for virtual power plant, a distributed control algorithm for virtual power plant based on communication-censored is proposed to realize efficient communication. For the DC optimal power flow problem of virtual power plant, the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with faster convergence speed is adopted, and communication-censored is added in the process of updating iteration. Different from the traditional algorithm, communication is carried out after each iteration. The distributed control algorithm of virtual power plant based on communication-censored can communicate and exchange information only when the difference between the two iterations is large enough, which effectively reduces the communication cost. In addition, the validity of the algorithm is verified on a 6- bus system.

Author Keywords: the alternating direction method of multipliers

articleTitle: A Data Valuation Framework for the Electricity Market Data
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the context of the digital transformation of the electricity market, the electricity transaction data held by exchange centers have significant application potential. This paper proposes a comprehensive data valuation framework to assist power trading centers in extracting the value of electricity trading data. The framework integrates the cost and revenue approaches, evaluating electricity market data from the perspectives of data cost and relative value. Furthermore, accounting for the characteristics of electricity market data, our approach includes data quality, data significance, data application, and data risk within the relative value dimension. Using real electricity market data from the power exchange center, we validate that the proposed indicator system can comprehensively and dynamically reflect the value of electricity trading data.

articleTitle: Optimal Control Strategy for DC Microgrid Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: On the premise of stable DC bus voltage, in order to solve the problem that the output of DC microgrid fluctuates greatly and it is difficult to schedule, a new optimal control strategy for DC microgrid scheduling is proposed. Taking the minimum root-mean-square error between external active output and planned active output of DC microgrid and the minimum root-mean-square error of DC bus voltage deviation as the optimization objective function, and considering the constraints of state of charge of energy storage battery and DC bus voltage deviation, an optimization model of DC microgrid scheduling is established. Firstly, the structure of DC microgrid is analyzed, and the mathematical model of power electronic equipment whose main structural modules are incorporated into DC bus is established. Secondly, the maximum output power of photovoltaic cells is calculated by disturbance observation method, and the photovoltaic output control strategy is determined. Based on the planned output curve issued by the main grid, the charging and discharging current of the energy storage battery is controlled by using the active power output from the microgrid. Then the traditional control strategy of energy storage system is improved, and the traditional voltage outer loop is changed into active power loop, and the traditional PQ control mode of DC/AC inverter is optimized, and the traditional active power and reactive power loop is changed into DC bus voltage and reactive power loop. Finally, based on MATLAB/simulink simulation platform, the simulation system of DC microgrid is established with 24 hours as the scheduling cycle. The simulation results show that the proposed control strategy is effective.

articleTitle: A Novel Coordinated Dispatch Method Considering Hydrogen Energy Storage and Battery Energy Storage System in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The distribution network dispatching with hydrogen energy storage system (HESS) in days cannot adapt to the long-time scale fluctuation of wind power. In addition, the long-time scale storage character of HESS is not fully utilized. So, a coordinated multi time scale dispatching with hydrogen energy storage system and battery energy storage system (BESS) in distribution networks is proposed. Firstly, the mathematic model of HESS and BESS are presented, respectively. Different hydrogen production and power generation time intervals of HESS and BESS are determined based on the fluctuation of wind/ photovoltaic power. Secondly, the coordinated multi time scale dispatching model with HESS and BESS are established to minimize the sum of power losses and wind/photovoltaic curtailment cost. The different time scale fluctuation of wind/photovoltaic power are adapted by determining capacitor switching, status of switches, charging and discharging power of BESS, hydrogen production and power generation of HESS. Finally, the standard IEEE33 distribution network simulation numerical demonstrates that the costs are decreased compared existing methods.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Allocation of Energy Storage in Power System with High Proportion of Renewable Energy under Extreme Events
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper investigates the optimal allocation of energy storage in power system with high proportion of renewable energy under extreme events. In order to solve the optimal configuration problem of energy storage participating in primary frequency regulation of high-proportion new energy system, a control strategy of primary frequency regulation of energy storage based on nonlinear variable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> coefficient was firstly studied. On the basis of this, an energy storage location and capacity configuration method for high-proportion new energy power system was proposed. This method adopted multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm, energy storage capacity, location and control parameters were taken as decision variables, and the root mean square of system frequency deviation, the vulnerability index of power grid and the net cost of energy storage were taken as optimization objectives to obtain the Pareto solution set. The weight of each objective was obtained by information entropy, and the optimal solution was calculated by the Technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution. Finally, the optimal energy storage configuration scheme of regional power grid is given through simulation analysis of practical examples, and the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed energy storage location and capacity configuration method and control strategy are verified.

articleTitle: Analysis of A Cable Sheath Voltage Limiter Explosion Accident
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper analyses an exploding cable sheath Voltage limiter accident and reveals the unstable intermediate state of the it during moisture exposure by simulating water ingress tests of the Voltage limiter as well as insulation resistance and lightning overvoltage tests at various levels of moisture exposure. It was found that deposits or adsorbed layers accumulate on the surface of the valve sheet of the cable sheath Voltage limiter, increasing the resistance of the electrode surface and leading to an increase in resistance. The cause of this explosion accident may have been the failure of the insulation tester used to detect water ingress during the pre-test experiments due to the low conductivity of the hydride of ZnO. As a result, moisture was present inside the protector. When an overcurrent occurs, the liquid water in the moisture rapidly vaporises into water vapour, resulting in a sharp expansion in volume, generating a high pressure that exceeds the withstand capacity of the shell, ultimately leading to a rupture or explosion of the shell.

articleTitle: Voltage Stabilizer Based on Flexible DC to Compensate for Terminal Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The normality of user-end voltage is very important. With the development of the economy, addressing the issue of low voltage on the user side caused by continuously increasing loads has become a current research hotspot. This paper considers a low voltage governance device based on a flexible DC transmission system. This device features power factor correction and can effectively reduce line losses. Firstly, a model and control strategy for the boost PFC rectifier circuit at the front end and the inverter circuit at the back end are established. Secondly, the rationality of the model and control strategy is analyzed using Bode plots. Finally, simulation and experimental verification are conducted. The results show that this device can effectively address the low voltage problem on the user side and improve system voltage stability.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Wind Turbines Based on TimeGAN-Stacking
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The lack of sufficient fault samples to support the training of fault diagnosis models in wind turbines often leads to monitoring systems missing or misreporting faults. In response to the above issues, this article proposes a fault diagnosis method for wind turbine pitch system based on TimeGAN-Stacking. At the data level, due to the imbalance of the original sample categories, a Time Generative Adversarial Network (TimeGAN) is used to track the dynamic changes in the probability distribution of wind turbine operation data step by step, while optimizing the global and local distribution of the generated samples, effectively balancing and expanding the comprehensive sample set of wind turbine faults; At the model level, establish a Stacking integrated model that integrates the advantages of multiple fault diagnosis devices to further improve fault diagnosis capabilities. Finally, the proposed method was tested based on actual wind field data, and the results showed that the TimeGAN-Stacking fault recognition method can effectively diagnose wind turbine faults and has good recognition performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Volume-Price Relationship of Green Certificates under Different Policies Based on VAR Models
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: At present, China's green certificate market is booming, and with the continuous improvement of policies, the green certificate market tends to mature and the price of green certificates tends to stabilize. However, the relationship between green certificate price and policy, and the trading volume of green certificates is still not effectively discussed. This paper first analyzes the impact of policies on green certificate prices using the interrupted time series method, and then analyzes the relationship between green certificate prices and green certificate trading volume using the VAR econometric model. It can be found that the issuance of policies affects the price of green certificates, and the relationship between the volume of green certificates traded and the price of green certificates also changes with the issuance of policies.

articleTitle: Suppression of Fundamental Frequency Component Through a Novel Kalman Filter for On-Line Diagnosis of Induction Motor Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: For diagnosis of induction motor faults through motor current signature analysis, spectral leakage of the fundamental frequency component (FFC) is one of the key factors deteriorating its reliability, because in the spectrum of the stator current (SC) signal, the widened peak of FFC can easily cover up some fault characteristic harmonics, especially the sideband harmonics (SBHs). Herein, a novel model containing both linear and nonlinear parts is proposed for developing the Kalman filter (KF) with enhanced FFC suppression performance. The developed KF is a combination of the extended KF (EKF) and linear KF (LKF). When implementing the KF, the EKF based on the nonlinear part of the model is first exerted on the supply voltage signal to estimate the fundamental frequency (FF) of the power grid. Secondly, based on the linear part of the model, the LKF utilizing the estimated FF as its inherent parameter is exerted on the SC signal to estimate the FFC. After subtracting the estimate of FFC from the SC signal, the peak of FFC in the spectrum is suppressed significantly, leading to effective identification of SBHs, even at the slip as low as 0.5%. The KF based on the novel model proposed in our research exhibits much more excellent FFC suppression effect than KFs based on purely (non)linear models.

articleTitle: Online Parameter Identification for Multiport Magnetic Networks Energy Routers
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: A bstract-Multiport magnetic network energy router (MMNER) is attractive for DC micro grids with the advantages of high-power density and electrical isolation. Parameter identification is essential for MMNER since the parameters may change with aging and thus deteriorates the output performances. This paper proposes a forgetting factor recursive least squares (FFRLS) method-based parameter identification. By constructing the model system equations with the introduction of forgetting factor and solving them using the recursive least squares method, the equivalent connection inductance parameter identification results are finally obtained. The proposed FFRLS method can effectively identify parameters of MMNER, and accordingly improve the reliability of power control for MMNER. Besides, the simulation results show that the error of identified parameters (average value) are all within 1%, proving the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Half-bridge Modular Multilevel Converter Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Modular multilevel converters are widely used in engineering fields because of their low loss and high waveform quality. However, when the number of its sub-modules is high, the switching tubes in the power module are prone to open-circuit and short-circuit faults, which seriously affects the safe operation of the MMC. In order to improve the reliability of the modular multilevel converter converter operation and quickly detect the faults, this paper proposes a detection method based on the combination of hardware circuit and capacitive voltage increment ratio to quickly diagnose the switching tube faults in power modules. Firstly, the switching tube fault characteristics of the power module are analysed, and mathematical relationships are established according to different fault characteristics; secondly, the predicted voltage at the two ends of the capacitor during normal operation is used to diagnose the fault by comparing it with the actual detection voltage. Then, the category of the fault is quickly determined by combining with the hardware. Finally, the simulation is carried out by using Matlab/Simulink, and the results show that the proposed method can accurately and quickly locate and identify the power module faults, which solves the problem of difficult diagnosis of power modules.

articleTitle: Characteristic Analysis of Flux Switching Linear Machine for Gravity Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Gravity energy storage technology, which transfers energies between the electric power and the gravitational potential energy, shows outstanding potentials in balancing the energy conflict between power station and public demands. This paper introduces a gravity energy storage system that operating in the engineering shafts or abandoned mines, which uses linear permanent magnet machine as the transformer to achieve energy storage and release process. The working principle of the gravity energy storage system with linear machine is introduced. Most importantly, the paper detailed analyzes the characteristic behaviors of the linear machine from electric motor and generator parts. The influence factors that affect the electromagnetic performances of the linear machine is analysis. The driving and generating performances of the linear machine are simulated and analyzed to validate its efficiency and feasibility.

articleTitle: The Impact of EGR Technology on the Performance and Emissions of n-Butanol/Diesel Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This study uses A VL_ FIRE software to simulate the combustion chamber of n-butanol and diesel blended fuel in a 4190ZLC-2 medium-speed diesel engine. It investigates the effects of n-butanol blending ratios (0%, 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, 20%, 30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and EGR rates (0%, 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) on engine combustion performance and emission characteristics. Simulation results indicate that increasing the n-butanol blending ratio effectively reduces CO emissions, though NO generation increases. Introducing 10% EGR significantly lowers the mass generation of both, benefiting marine environmental protection. However, this results in decreased in-cylinder pressure and temperature, impacting the engine's power performance. This research provides a scientific basis for the use of n-butanol blended fuel in marine diesel engines and offers references for emission reduction using EGR technology in practical applications.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Electromechanical Hybrid Simulation of Multi Fed DC Power Grid with CLCC Converter Station
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The structure and working principle of CLCC are analyzed, the simulation software E-Tran Plus is used as the interface, combined with the mature software PSCAD and PSSE to form an electromechanical-electromagnetic hybrid simulation platform, the functions and principles of the simulation software are introduced in detail, and a simple electromechanical-electromagnetic hybrid simulation is carried out through a small system to compare with the pure electromagnetic simulation study. The theoretical and simulation results show that the electromechanical-electromagnetic hybrid simulation model using E-Tran Plus interface software is characterized by high accuracy and fast speed, which can better reflect the dynamic characteristics of the AC system and is closer to the actual engineering, and it provides an important reference value for the future large-scale electromechanical-electromagnetic hybrid simulation study of AC and DC power grids.

articleTitle: Study on Power Capture Performance of the Edinburgh Duck Wave Energy Converter Based on a CFD Model
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The Edinburgh Duck Wave Energy Converter (ED-WEC) is one of the most efficient wave energy converter. To predict the wave-structure interaction process and further the wave power capture performance of the ED-WEC, two most commonly used tools, i.e. the potential theory model and the Computational Fluid Dynamic (CFD) model, are two competitors and both require meshing of the Duck. Since the Duck is quite long, a direct meshing of the Duck is impossible because the mesh count will be high enough that beyond the capacity of the software. Meanwhile, the large length of the Duck permits reducing the three-dimensional wave-structure interaction problem to a two-dimensional problem, which rules out the potential theory model since most potential theory based software naturally define the velocity potential in three-dimensional space. As a result, the CFD model is employed in this paper to solve the two-dimensional wave-structure interaction problem of the ED-WEC, and the results are compared with the potential theory model concerning a short Duck. It is found that the numerical wave tunnel established in the CFD model is able to generate waves with high quality. The difference of the hydrodynamic response predicted from the CFD model and the potential theory model is small at low wave amplitudes but grows significantly at high wave amplitudes, suggesting that the wave-structure interaction for a Duck with infinite length is slightly different from a short Duck and the CFD model is able to capture nonlinearities within the wave-structure interaction process. Based on the CFD model, the high wave power capture efficiency of the ED-WEC is visually demonstrated by an overlaying image consisting of five water-phase snapshots.

articleTitle: Research on Composite Energy Storage and Impedance Matching Strategies for Variable Load Pulse Acoustic Transmitters
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: A composite energy storage and adaptive impedance matching strategy was proposed in order to reduce the power capacity requirements of pulse acoustic transmitters. The composite energy storage system was composed of lithium-ion batteries and supercapacitors, and the state of the energy storage system was estimated based on external characteristic parameters. The energy distribution was dynamically adjusted according to the overall transmitter source demand; An adaptive impedance matching network was designed for load transducers under different hydrostatic pressures, optimized broadband matching topology parameters, and dynamically adjusted the matching network based on hydrostatic pressure feedback; Through verification under different operating conditions, the results show that the composite energy storage and impedance matching strategy can improve the system power factor, reduce the apparent power demand and the energy storage design capacity. The proposed method has high engineering practical value and can be used as an effective energy system design method.

articleTitle: Local Optimal Reactive Power Control of PV with Day-Ahead Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In view of the difficulties brought by the strong uncertainty of photovoltaic (PV) output to the optimal control of reactive power in distribution networks, a local optimal reactive power control method of PV with day-ahead load forecasting is proposed in this paper. First, some basic assumptions about operation conditions and optimal reactive power state in distribution networks are put forward, and a two-sided reactive power control framework including master station and PV controllers is established. Secondly, long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network is used for day-ahead load forecasting, and the expressions of optimal reactive power reference of PV plants are derived. Finally, a case study is conducted to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed method can rapidly and optimally control the PV reactive power output, reduce the energy loss of the distribution network, and improve the voltage quality.

articleTitle: Load Risk Assessment Method for Flexible Transmission Line Based on SOP Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Flexible transmission technology has significant advantages in new energy grid connection, long-distance, large-capacity transmission, and power supply to passive networks. In this paper, a load risk assessment method for flexible transmission lines based on SOP is proposed, with the objective of minimizing the total risk of the system, and establishing a risk assessment model that takes into account the optimization of SOP parameters, uncertainty, reliability and economy of the flexible line. Particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to solve the model. The results are used to configure the SOP and perform risk assessment of the FDN at this point to improve the accuracy and efficiency of load risk assessment. Validation and analysis is carried out with IEEE 33-node network. This research can provide crucial decision support for power system operation and management.

articleTitle: An Overview of Essential Technologies for Retrofitting Thermal Power Generation Units into Synchronous Condensers
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In HVDC systems, variations in the AC voltage at the converter station can jeopardize the secure and stable functioning of the converter. To prevent commutation failure and stabilise the voltage, dynamic reactive power support is required in the AC system. Transforming current thermal power units into synchronous condensers offers a cost-effective and practical solution. The key technologies, including reactive power compensation capacity optimisation, condition monitoring technology, operation and configuration optimisation in the conversion of thermal power generation units to synchronous condensers are reviewed in this paper, and the development trends are forecast.

articleTitle: Steffensen's Acceleration Method for ADMM for Solving EV Charging Optimization Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Charging control strategies determine the charging schedules of electric vehicles (EVs) to meet the travel demands of residents. Due to the bandwidth of the communication system, the scalability, and the robustness of the controller, distributed model predictive control (DMPC) approaches are widely adopted for EV charging control. This paper proposes a novel Steffensen Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (S-ADMM) algorithm to accelerate the solving process of DMPC charging control planning problems. Via a case study, the performance of the proposed S-ADMM algorithm and the traditional ADMM algorithm are compared. The S-ADMM algorithm shows better performance in terms of convergence speed.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Synchronous Condensers for Overvoltage Suppression in High-Proportion Wind Power System Based on Validity Index
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Faults in high proportion of new energy delivery systems may lead to large number of new energy units being disconnected from the power grid due to transient overvoltage. Configuring synchronous condensers at new energy plants or collection stations is an effective means to suppress transient overvoltage. This paper proposes a practical configuration method of synchronous condensers for overvoltage suppression in high-proportion wind power system based on greedy strategy. First, an overvoltage suppression validity index based on electrical distance is proposed to evaluate the current most needed position for configuring synchronous condensers. Based on the proposed overvoltage suppression validity index, configuration of the synchronous condensers is carried out under the greedy strategy. The effectiveness of the proposed method lies in its ability to obtain appropriate installation positions for synchronous condensers in a reliable order. Feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed approach are demonstrated in the case study section.

articleTitle: Influence of Boiler Model on Simulation of Primary Frequency Regulation of Thermal Power Units
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of new energy integration into the grid, frequency safety issues in the power system have become prominent. The importance of unit frequency regulation capability and grid frequency dynamic analysis has become increasingly prominent. At present, the primary frequency regulation model commonly used in power simulation for thermal power units does not include the boiler module, and its simulation results differ significantly from the actual situation in large frequency difference accidents. Although adding a boiler model can improve simulation accuracy, it is still necessary to clarify how the boiler and boiler control model affect the primary frequency regulation of the unit. This paper combines medium-to long-term simulation of power systems and thermodynamic principles to provide a detailed model of primary frequency regulation with boiler dynamics. On the basis of detailed models, three models are simplified. And the effectiveness of all models is verified. By comparing the simulation frequency differences of different models in a single machine load system, this paper concludes that the dynamic control of the boiler has a small impact on primary frequency regulation, but the influence of boiler physical dynamics increases with the increase of frequency regulation power. The conclusion of this paper clearly answers the necessity of boiler models in primary frequency regulation, which is helpful for the selection of thermal power unit models in advance frequency warning.

articleTitle: Lightweight Authentication Technique for Distributed Control of Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Propose a two-party anonymous lightweight reverse firewall authentication scheme to solve the problem that the stored data of distributed control smart terminals for power distribution networks are easily attacked. The scheme achieves identity information privacy protection by using random pseudonyms, and the elliptic curve-based construction effectively reduces the computation amount, thus achieving lightweight and low-latency authentication. In addition, the scheme is resistant to attacks. Compared with other lightweight authentication protocols, The analysis results indicate that the protocol offers enhanced security and reduced runtime.

articleTitle: Regional Differential Backup Protection Suitable for the Collection Lines of Large-Scale Photovoltaic Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid expansion of large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power stations has necessitated intricate two-stage aggregation systems within stations, where thousands of PV generation units are consolidated via cables and overhead lines before reaching the booster station. Complexity in wiring poses challenges, as malfunctioning coordination of aggregation line protection post-fault can lead to misoperations, tripping non-faulty branches, expanding power outages, and hampering grid-connected efficiency. To enhance reliability and speed of protection, A regional differential backup protection tailored for aggregation lines in large PV stations is proposed in this paper. The traditional differential protection is set as the primary safeguard protection and minimal regional differential protection is set as backup protection. Our strategy, under limited communication constraints, reliably identifies the smallest backup protection zone and, in cases of primary protection refusal, swiftly isolates faults with minimal action scope and duration. MATLAB simulation validates its adaptability to complex PV station wiring, ensuring reliable fault isolation. The synergy between backup and primary protections ensures speed, selectivity, and reliability in protection operation.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Power Oscillation of Secondary Reheat Unit Considering the Characteristics of the Valve
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The power oscillation has a bad impact on the safety and economy of power plants and power grids, and the causes and solutions of the power oscillation problem of secondary reheat units are not mature. In order to quickly solve the power oscillation problem of the secondary reheat unit, a simulation and analysis method of the power oscillation of the secondary reheat unit considering the characteristics of the valve adjustment was proposed. By analyzing the influence of operating parameters and adjusting parameters on the characteristics of the valve, the modular modeling of the secondary reheat unit is carried out, and the power model considering the secondary reheating process and the actuator model considering the adjusting characteristics of the valve are proposed, then the optimized adjusting parameters are proposed based on this. The simulation analysis was carried out with reference to the actual power oscillation case, which verified the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the effectiveness of the proposed method are provided an effective decision-making reference for the cause finding of the power oscillation of the secondary reheat unit.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch of Multi-Energy Generation Systems Considering CSP and Advanced Adiabatic CAES
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The supply-demand balance of the power system is gaining prominence as the installed capacity of new energy keeps rising. These problems can be effectively alleviated through flexible and controllable concentrated solar power (CSP) and advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage (CAES), which have internal thermal storage devices and can be interconnected to achieve mutual thermal assistance during operation. In this paper, the thermal energy storage (TES) device of CSP is connected to the TES of CAES through a thermal pipeline, and the constraints of the TES considering thermal energy mutual assistance are established to limit the way of energy flow in the TES under the joint operation condition. Finally, the model of the joint system of CSP-CAES is constructed, and the day-ahead dispatching plans are obtained with the objective of minimizing the total operation cost. The results show that this strategy further enhances the new energy consumption based on ensuring the balance between system supply and demand, which verifies the effectiveness of the strategy.

articleTitle: Distribution Substation Risk Assessment Under Rainfall Flood Based on HEC-RAS
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In recent years, rainfall flood disasters have occurred frequently, which bring great threats to the power system, especially distribution substations, causing widespread outages. It is crucial to effectively assess the distribution risk under rainfall flood disasters. Nonetheless, many studies nowadays are aimed at repair work after rainfall flood, and few studies have conducted flood risk assessments of pre-disaster distribution substations. To address this gap, this article proposes a model-driven rainfall flood risk assessment method for distribution substations. Firstly, the flood evolution model HEC-RAS is used to establish a flood model for the 100-year rainfall in the study area. Then the flood risk map and flood depth of the study area are obtained through model simulation calculations. Afterwards, the distribution substations contained in the area are visualized with the flood inundation by Arc-GIS. Finally, the risk of the distribution substation is assessed by combining the flooding vulnerability curve of the distribution substation, which provides a scientific basis for the pre-disaster rainfall flood emergency command decision of the distribution substation.

articleTitle: Reactive Power Absorption Capability of Dual-Excited Condenser With Symmetric Excitation Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy and ultra-high-voltage direct current (UHVDC) systems into the power grid introduces challenges such as commutation failure and transient overvoltage issues. This paper explores the reactive power absorption capability of dual-excited synchronous condensers with a symmetric excitation scheme, which can address these challenges more effectively than conventional synchronous condensers. The dual-excited synchronous condensers, equipped with two sets of excitation windings, can operate with negative excitation, thus enhancing reactive power absorption. The study delves into the basic principles of operation; the excitation winding structure; and the reactive power capability of dual-excited synchronous condensers. Compared to an asymmetric dual excitation scheme, the rotor with a symmetric dual excitation scheme offers a broader range of excitation emf adjustment and is easier to design and manufacture. The stability of the dual-excited condenser is improved through the coordinated regulation of d-axis and q-axis excitation. A detailed electromagnetic transient simulation model developed in PSCAD demonstrates that dual-excitation synchronous condensers can stably absorb over 2 p.u. of reactive power, a performance level that surpasses the limitations of conventional synchronous condensers.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-frequency Damping Control Method of Energy Storage for New Energy Station
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the large-scale access of new energy sources such as wind power and photovoltaic, the interaction between new energy sites composed of many power electronic equipment and the power grid is increasing, which is easy to induce multi-frequency oscillation phenomenon in the power grid. In order to understand the multi-frequency oscillation between new energy and power grid, a new energy station system model including wind power, photovoltaic and thermal power generation units is established in this paper. Then, the oscillation characteristics of the power grid under different operating conditions are analyzed, and the characteristic frequencies of different frequency bands are aggregated and divided into low frequency oscillation, sub-synchronous oscillation and high frequency oscillation in turn by eigenvalue analysis. Then, with the help of the fast response characteristics of energy storage, a multi-band oscillation suppression system of power grid is constructed. By dividing the frequency bands of power grid frequency and voltage oscillation, the damping effect of different frequency bands is improved to realize the effective suppression of multi-band oscillation. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Pilot Protection for LCC-HVDC Hybrid System Considering Three-Phase Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: LCC-HVDC systems are widely used in China. However, commutation failure remains an inherent flaw in thyristor-based converter systems that has yet to be eliminated. Additionally, during the occurrence and restoration of AC line faults at the inverter side, the equivalent DC system exhibits nonlinear characteristics, leading to uncertain impacts on the adaptability of traditional protections in AC grids with inverter stations. The Tellegen's theorem, which is only related to the circuit topology and is not affected by branch nonlinearity, is proposed in this paper to be applied in AC systems with inverter stations. Considering the three-phase coupling of lines, a novel pilot protection method that is not influenced by the characteristics of inverter stations is proposed and tested in a PSCAD simulation system to validate its feasibility.

articleTitle: Optimal Reactive Power Control Strategy for Islanded VSG System under Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In microgrid systems, virtual synchronous generator (VSG) serves as an interface to various distributed power sources, which can effectively improve the inertia and damping of the system. The VSG system under conventional linear control has low control accuracy and poor perturbation resistance, to which this paper introduces adaptive perturbation compensation on the basis of conventional sliding mode control, which improves the robustness of the system on the basis of ensuring the stability of the system. Meanwhile, for the problem that reactive power cannot be proportionally distributed and circulating current is generated due to the inconsistency of line impedance when multiple VSGs are connected in parallel, a consensus-based adaptive virtual impedance control strategy is proposed, which realizes the precise distribution of reactive power and effectively suppresses the circulating current at the same time. Finally, the reliability and superiority of the above control strategy are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: A Mode-Switching-Based Transient Regulation Method for Grid-Forming Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: For grid-forming converters, such as Virtual Synchronous Generators (VSGs), the existing low voltage ride through (LVRT) strategies based on mode switching are not applicable during transient regulation due to the integral characteristics of the power outer loop. To address this, the paper analyzes the causes of fault overcurrent in VSGs during fault occurrence and recovery periods. During faults, effective suppression of fault current is achieved by adjusting the current reference value. For the overcurrent issue during fault recovery, the paper proposes a method of reassigning the power reference value to avoid the impact of power integral switching. Finally, simulations based on Matlab/Simulink verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis and the accuracy of the regulation methods.

articleTitle: Mathematical Morphology-Based Fault Identification for Distribution Network with DFIG
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the large-scale access to the distribution grid by new energy power sources, the short-circuit currents provided by doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) increase the transient complexity of the grid. This is due to their low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) requirements in case of faults on the distribution network. Consequently, traditional power system relay protection schemes are impacted. Therefore, a multi-resolution morphological gradient-based fault identification method for distribution network is proposed. This method focuses on the short-circuit currents characteristics of DFIG. It aims to achieve accurate fault identification when DFIG is connected to the distribution network. A appropriate data window is selected and then the multi-resolution morphological gradient (MMG) is processed to obtain the morphological gradient characteristics of the currents signal. After analyzing the peak-to-peak ratio of gradient characteristics, a criterion is constructed which is used to correctly classify different types of faults and select the fault phase. A distribution network model with DFIG is constructed in MATLAB/Simulink, and the effectiveness of the proposed fault identification method is verified.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of EVs Aggregation Based on Extended Markov Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The precise aggregation method is of great significance for Electric vehicle population (EVP) to participate in grid ancillary services as a flexible resource. In this paper, considering the difference of charge-discharge characteristics and charging power of EV batteries, the Markov chain model of three states is extended to five states, and the one-step transfer probability is calculated according to the relationship between the charging power and the state of charge when calculating the Markov chain state transition matrix, which solves the problem of the explosion of the Monte Carlo method with the increasing number of individuals and parameters. Simulation examples are used to verify that the aggregation model based on extended Markov chain has good accuracy.

articleTitle: Trading Strategies for Renewable Energy Power Producers Based on Green Electricity-Tradable Green Certificate-CCER Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The generation of China's renewable energy are steadily increasing, prompting the emergence of renewable energy market trading mechanisms such as green certificate trading and CCER trading. The primary challenge now lies in how to promote renewable energy consumption through market-based approaches. Therefore, research on the coupling relationships between the green electricity market, tradable green certificate market, and CCER market is essential. This paper first considered the inherent interrelationships among the green electricity, tradable green certificate, and CCER market, establishing a trading strategy model for wind and solar power producers operating within these interconnected markets. Secondly, the Conditional Value at Risk (CvaR) theory was introduced to quantify the uncertainty risk of price fluctuations in various markets. Finally, the CPLEX solver was employed to solve the model, obtaining optimal trading strategies for power producers. The results show that this model effectively increases the profitability for wind and solar power producers while ensuring expected revenue stability.

articleTitle: Bidding Strategies for Differentiated Energy Blocks in Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: After the carbon peak and carbon neutrality targets were proposed, China is actively promoting the construction of the new power system. This has led to the emergence of diverse and differentiated new market players. It is urgent to design a new electricity market to satisfy the demands for optimal energy resource allocation in the new power system. In order to solve this problem, in this paper, four types of energy blocks are introduced, and their optimal bidding strategies in energy block-based markets are proposed. First, the mathematical models of the period block, sustaining block, curve block and variable block are established according to their physical characteristics. Next, the decision-making models of these energy block player are established. Then, the multi-player generalized Nash game model in the energy block-based electricity market is established, and the Gauss-Seidel Fixed-Point Iteration method is proposed to solve the game equilibrium. Finally, the numerical simulations are carried out in the IEEE-9 bus system. It shows that the established energy block models are effective and the clearing price of the energy block-based market is more stable.

articleTitle: Study and Analysis on Biodegradation Performance of Alkyl Benzene Insulating Oil Used in Oil-Filled Submarine Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Oil-filled submarine cable is widely used due to the mature technology, excellent electrical performance, and the ability to continuously drain oil after failure, which can prevent the rapid expansion of faults caused by seawater infiltration. While, following a failure of this kind of cable, it is essential to investigate the biodegradation of alkylbenzene insulating oil after leakage and assess if it aligns with the degradation rate specified by cable suppliers. Research findings indicate that the degradation of submarine cable insulating oil in natural seawater reaches 13.2% in 7 days and 44.0% in 28 days. In the presence of activated sludge bacteria, the biodegradation rate is 50.9% in 7 days and 75.9% in 28 days, deviating slightly from the expected degradation rate, possibly due to the specific marine environment. It is crucial to evaluate the seawater degradation efficiency of the project post-oil leakage, so as to conduct environmental assessments based on the leakage situation and formulate targeted measures for recovering insulating oil, active bacteria that have no impact on the environment can be added when necessary to increase the degradation rate. Additionally, the study reveals that alkylbenzene insulating oil with fewer alkyl branched chain carbon atoms on the benzene ring degrades faster under similar conditions. Therefore, when selecting alkylbenzene insulating oil, it is recommended to choose the to choose the one with less branched alkylbenzene.

articleTitle: Reservoir Capacity Prediction for Pumped Storage Pumping Station Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The storage capacity of pumped storage pumping station is an important monitoring object for pump station operation, and predicting the storage capacity is an important operational management task. Predicting storage capacity can help staff arrange pumping and energy storage in a reasonable manner, maximizing energy efficiency and economic benefits. This paper used back propagation network (BPNN) and long short-term memory network (LSTM) for storage capacity prediction, including the storage capacities of upper and lower reservoirs. Trained and tested these two models by using historical storage capacity data. evaluated their performance in predicting future storage capacities. Used performance indicators <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$MAPE,\ RMSE$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> to reflect the accuracy of prediction models. At the same time, draw distribution and scatter plots of the predicted values of the two models and the actual values of the test data. The experimental results showed that compared to BPNN model, the LSTM model exhibits higher accuracy and generalization ability in predicting the storage capacities of pumped storage pumping station. The predictions of the capacity for the upper and lower reservoirs showed an increase of 1.67% and 0.39% in MAPE, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$21.1840m^{3}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.2908m^{3}$</tex> in RMSE, and 0.1494 and 0.0292 in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: Adaptive Learning Based Load Forecasting Curve Data Extraction for Power Grid Operation Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Given that load forecasting data is often generated by different departments within the power system or obtained through predictive analysis tools, there are often discrepancies in format and time scale compared to the requirements of the Security-Constrained Unit Commitment (SCUC) algorithm. Typ-ically provided as load curves, this data necessitates conversion of format and refinement of time scales to meet the needs of SCUC input. This paper proposed a multi-time-scale data extraction method based on adaptive learning rates (ALR), aimed at addressing the mismatch between load forecasting data and SCUC algorithm inputs in power system operation planning. The proposed method dynamically adjusts the learning rate according to the local slope and variability of the curve, automatically adapting the ALR for data point extraction. This approach ensures high-precision data extraction across different time scales and complex curve scenarios, reducing the workload of manual data extraction and enhancing the intelligence and automation of the process.

articleTitle: Novel Control Structures for Parallel Two-Stage Converters Based on Shared SVPWAM/SVPWM
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Current-source converters are favored for their special and wide output voltage range. In order to increase power transmission, the structure and control strategies of parallel current-source converters have been developed. Meanwhile, two-stage cascaded current-source converters have an extremely wide output voltage range. However, until now, the control strategy for two-stage parallel current-source converters has not been studied. Therefore, this paper focuses on the control structure of current-source converters with this particular topology. Based on the proposed control architecture, multiple parallel current-source converters only need to use the same SVPWM or SVPWAM (Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation) (Space Vector Pulse Width Amplitude Modulation), eliminating the need for each parallel converter to use its own modulation scheme as in traditional droop control architectures. Even in the presence of differences in parameters among paralleled branches and filters, sinusoidal grid current, unit power factor, IOOOV output for the load can still be achieved. Simulation results also validate the correctness of theoretical analysis and the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Switching Sequence Based Energy Prediction Controller Design for Bidirectional DC-DC Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this paper, a bi-directional DC-DC converter energy prediction controller based on switching sequence is designed as an example of Buck-Boost converter, which combines the idea of energy balance with predictive control, establishes a bi-directional DC-DC converter energy prediction model, and establishes a simplified objective function from the perspective of energy, and at the same time introduces the switching sequence to achieve a fixed switching frequency of the converter. The simulation model is constructed and compared with the traditional PI controller, and the simulation results show that the dynamic response time and overshoot of the DC bus voltage of the bi-directional DC- DC converter with the energy prediction controller are significantly reduced compared with that of the PI controller, and the voltage fluctuation of the DC bus can be stabilised more quickly.

articleTitle: GSHC-Net: Image Restoration Network Based on Gated-Supervised and Hierarchical Cascaded for Transmission System in Adverse Weather
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: During the inspection of the transmission system, adverse weather conditions may result in visual occlusion, rendering the condition of transmission lines and power equipment components difficult to identify. To comprehensively address this issue, the study proposes a multi-stage image restoration network based on gated-supervised and hierarchical cascaded feature fusion scheme (GSHC-Net) to mitigate degradation effects in inspection images caused by adverse weather conditions. The main contribution is on two aspects: Firstly, to tackle the blurred characteristic details of power equipment components like transmission lines under adverse weather conditions, the gated-supervised attention network (GSAN) is proposed. This method employs a gated supervised attention mechanism and an adaptive convolution kernel to restore the fuzzy target details in recovered images so as to improve the overall visual quality. Secondly, a hierarchical cascaded feature fusion scheme (HCFFS) is presented to utilize the contextual semantic feature information efficiently. This scheme minimizes information loss during recovery processes for enhanced authenticity and accuracy of the recovery results. Finally, experiments reveal that GSHC-Net can improve the visual quality indexes of degraded images under different adverse weather, such as PSNR, by 4% on average.

articleTitle: Research on Improvement of “Manual Zero Crossing” Breaking Technology Under Medium Voltage and High Current Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The “manual zero crossing” breaking technology is an effective technical solution to solve the current breaking problem in medium and high voltage DC power systems. Under short-circuit conditions, the arc current is too high, usually above 20kA. On the one hand, the reverse pulse current injected during the forced commutation process leads to a very high current drop rate in the vacuum arc chamber, with a drop rate of about - 300A/µ s near the zero crossing of the arc current, and an initial transient recovery voltage transient of about -6kV after the zero crossing of the current. Vacuum circuit breakers often experience heavy breakdown after the arc current crosses zero, leading to disconnection failure. In response to this issue, this article proposes improvement measures from two aspects: reducing the voltage rise rate and current rise rate of the vacuum arc chamber.
