In the vacuum arc chamber series diode scheme, when the vacuum circuit breaker experiences arc reignition after the arc current crosses zero, the vacuum arc will cross zero again and extinguish the arc with the reverse blocking of the diode; And during the reverse blocking period of the diode, due to the blocking of the main circuit current of the DC system by the diode, energy is prevented from continuing to be injected into the vacuum arc gap, providing sufficient “zero rest” time for the vacuum arc and reducing the rate of voltage rise; The scheme of series connection of saturated reactors in vacuum arc chambers, with the continuous transfer of current, reduces the current in the vacuum circuit breaker to a small value before zero, and the saturated reactor exits the saturation state. The equivalent inductance rapidly increases, effectively slowing down the commutation process and generating a low current change rate range before the vacuum circuit breaker extinguishes. Reduce the initial plasma concentration in the vacuum gap after the arc and improve the recovery process of the medium after the arc. Two schemes can ensure reliable arc extinguishing of the vacuum arc chamber at two oscillation zero crossing points, improving the reliability of the vacuum circuit breaker in breaking large DC currents.

articleTitle: Ultra-Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Prediction Based on CNN-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Considering that the prediction accuracy of photovoltaic power strongly depends on factors such as weather patterns and climate conditions, a ultra short term photovoltaic power generation prediction method based on CNN-LSTM is proposed. Firstly, based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), features are selected and training and testing datasets are divided, and local features of the input data are extracted through CNN. Secondly, utilizing Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks to extract temporal features of data, fully mining the temporal and spatial correlations of photovoltaic measurement values, and analyzing the error distribution of prediction results to verify the robustness of subsequent control strategies. Finally, the proposed model is validated using data from a certain photovoltaic power station. The prediction results indicate that the predicted trend of photovoltaic power generation under different weather conditions is highly consistent with the actual photovoltaic power generation. Statistical analysis was conducted on the error distribution of the prediction model on the test set to obtain the distribution of photovoltaic power prediction errors and their kernel density estimates. The relative error of 90% of the prediction results was less than 7%.

articleTitle: Control Strategy for High-voltage Chained SVG Pre-charged De-side Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the promotion of the “double carbon” goal, the most clean energy is gradually replacing traditional energy, but the instability of new energy generation, long-distance transmission of electricity, grid aging and other problems will affect the quality of electricity. Reactive power compensation can effectively improve these problems. High-voltage chain SVG is one of the effective reactive power compensation programs in high-voltage field at present. It has the advantages of low harmonic content, fast response speed, continuous adjustment, and low loss. However, the high-voltage chained SVG system also brings a series of instability problems. This paper analyzes the high-voltage chain SVG pre-charging DC side capacitor voltage control, through the DC side capacitor voltage feedback and the equalization coefficient and then change the modulating wave sent, realize the charging and discharging of the DC side capacitor of the unit itself to achieve the DC side capacitor voltage equalization, to ensure the stable operation of the high-voltage chain SVG system

articleTitle: The Optimal Planning Method of Distribution Network Considering the Access of Electrothermic Coupling Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The access of renewable energy and thermoelectric coupling equipment poses a challenge to the stable operation of distribution network. In this paper, the energy storage system in the distribution network is configured. NSGA-II algorithm is used to solve the problem by taking planning cost, node heating temperature fluctuation and distribution network voltage deviation as objective functions. The simulation results based on IEEE-33 node test system show that with the configuration method described in this paper, the node heating temperature fluctuation is reduced by 8.53% and the node voltage deviation is reduced by 6.94% at a cost of $462,711.9 per year. In addition, simulation experiments are designed to verify the effectiveness of the optimal configuration method.

articleTitle: Research on Pricing Strategy of Shared Energy Storage and Integrated Energy Microgrid Cluster Transaction Based on Stackelberg Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid development of renewable energy technologies, shared energy storage systems play a crucial role in enhancing the efficiency of integrated energy microgrid clusters. This paper introduces the cooperative operational architecture of multiple microgrids, including shared energy storage, and thoroughly analyzes the interactions and interests of each participant. The study further explores how to achieve synergistic energy optimization among microgrids using shared energy storage, considering the spatial and temporal complementarities of their net load characteristics. Additionally, the dynamic game relationships among microgrid operators (MO), shared energy storage operators (SESO), and user aggregators (UA) are analyzed, highlighting how the strategies of MO and SESO mutually constrain each other and together form the leadership layer of a Stackelberg game, with user aggregators in the lower layer. Finally, the paper demonstrates the uniqueness of the Stackelberg equilibrium and employs a combination of genetic algorithms and quadratic programming to solve it. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through case studies.

articleTitle: A Modified Power System Frequency Response Model Incorporating DFIG Primary Frequency Control Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Wind turbines (WTs) provision of frequency support has become a must due to the reduction of system inertia caused by their replacement of conventional synchronous generators (SGs). The addition of frequency control complicates WT's frequency response, which hinders power system’ planning and operation for the assurance of frequency stability. To address this issue, the paper takes doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) based WT as an example, and proposes a modified power system frequency response (SFR) model. Firstly, allowing for the mechanical and control behavior of DFIG electromechanical dynamics, a synthetic motion equation model is built to explicitly characterize its inertia and damping characteristics. Then, considering system power balance relation, a modified SFR model is constructed by inserting the DFIG submodule. And lastly, time-domain simulation is conducted in Matlab/Simulink to verify the accuracy of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Research on High Performance Electromagnetic Transient Simulation Platform of HVDC Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: High performance electromagnetic transient simulations play an indispensable role in the field of modern electronic design and research and development, providing engineers with the ability to predict and optimize product performance during the design phase, significantly reducing the number of iterations required in the actual manufacturing and testing process, and effectively reducing the cost and time of research and development. These software not only have a critical impact on improving the efficiency and performance of product design but also play a crucial role in promoting technological innovation and achieving autonomous control of the industry. Restricted by modelling and simulation capabilities, computational efficiency, scalability and other aspects, traditional electromagnetic transient simulation tools are difficult to adapt to the needs of new power systems. In this paper, we design a power modelling and simulation software for a new type of power system. The software supports a variety of numerical integration methods, adapts to the characteristics of new power systems, effectively eliminates the problem of numerical oscillation, and can construct multiple control system models with the same structure but different parameters. This paper takes the Tianzhong DC project as an example, builds a simulation model in the SimuNPS environment, and verifies the rationality and superiority of the simulation platform by comparing it with the traditional electromagnetic transient simulation software.

articleTitle: A Modular Multiport Input-Independent Output-Series Photovoltaic MVDC Integration Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To solve the problem of unbalanced output voltage caused by photovoltaic (PV) power mismatch when PV is integration into medium voltage DC (MVDC) grid, a modular hybrid-connected three-port converters (TPCs) with output voltage balancing is proposed in this paper. The system consists of multiple modular pulse-width modulation plus phase-shift (PPS) controlled TPCs, which achieves the independent maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of all PV panels, feature low voltage stress and soft switching. The bidirectional ports of TPCs are connected in parallel to build a low-voltage DC (LVDC) bus. By adjusting the output voltage and the voltage of bidirectional ports, mismatched power of PV can be transferred between all submodules (SMs) through LVDC bus, thus achieving the output voltage balancing. The working principle of TPC is analyzed in detail, and simulation and experiment are carried out to verify the feasibility of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Research on Marker Recognition Method for Substation Engineering Progress Monitoring Based on Grounding DINO
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The traditional progress monitoring method for substation engineering mainly relies on manual work, which is time-consuming and laborious. Based on this, this paper proposes a new marker recognition method for substation engineering progress monitoring based on Grounding DINO. This method uses Grounding DINO to recognize the key markers of substation engineering and combines the weights of the markers to monitor the construction progress of substation engineering. Grounding DINO is a large-scale visual object detection model with strong generalization in feature extraction ability. We further use LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) method to fine-tune and optimize its feature extraction network, so that it can improve the recognition accuracy and reliability of key markers in different stages of substation engineering infrastructure at a small data cost. Thus, the construction progress of substation engineering can be carefully monitored. We selected 24 kinds of key markers of substation engineering to carry out experiments, and the results showed that the average recognition accuracy of key markers can reach 95.13%, which effectively proved the effectiveness of the improved Grounding DINO model. In addition, this article used the proposed method to analyze the construction progress of the Xiantao Xianxi 200kV substation engineering, and the results showed that our method could effectively monitor the construction progress of the substation engineering. It proved that our method had great application market and potential.

articleTitle: Big Data Analysis and Visualization System for Large-Scale Pumped Storage Power Station Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The traditional operation and maintenance management of pumped storage power station group exists problems such as data analysis and mining is not systematic, and the level of intelligence is low. This paper researches the large-scale pumped storage power station big data analysis technology system of multi-source data fusion, and based on this, develops the large-scale pumped storage power station equipment visualisation and big data decision analysis system, constructs the data transmission platform, and realizes the standardized storage of multi-source data. Meanwhile, intelligent algorithms are developed based on the data and platform foundation, while applications are deployed to verify their reliability. This is helpful in promoting the intelligent and digital transformation of pumped storage power station groups.

articleTitle: Fast Risk Assessment for Power Systems Considering Cascading Failures: A State Similarity Method
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Due to the immense computational burden, considering cascading failures (CF) in power systems during operation becomes highly challenging, especially for systems with a high proportion of renewable energy. To address this issue, this paper proposed a cascading failure risk assessment method based on state similarity (SS), effectively handling large-scale scenarios without reduction. The method employs multi-parameter programming to divide massive scenarios into different critical regions (CR). Utilize the topological features within the same critical region, referred to as similarity features, to simplify the analysis process. This approach transforms the complex iterative optimization problem into a set of linear equations in each CR, thereby improving computational efficiency. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through the IEEE 39-bus test system.

articleTitle: Research on Efficiency Optimization Technology of CLLLC Resonant Bidirectional DC / DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The research on CLLLC resonant converters usually improves transmission efficiency by optimizing the parameter design, but the converter efficiency is low at light load. In this paper, this paper uses the optimal asymmetric voltage offset (OAVC) control to realize the active bridge converter's wide range of soft switching operations. The optimal equivalent resistance is obtained by the fundamental wave equivalent of the circuit, and the transmission efficiency is optimized under the adaptive load. The constant voltage output is realized by adjusting the inverter side switch tube, and the optimal equivalent resistance is obtained by changing the rectifier side switch tube. Finally, through multiple sets of simulation tests, it is verified that the efficiency of the proposed method is maintained above 90% under different load conditions. Under the light load condition with an output power of 100 W, the efficiency of the proposed method is improved by 30% compared with the traditional method, achieving high-efficiency transmission.

articleTitle: Uninterrupted Fast Switching Technology Between Power Supplies Based on Parallel Trigger Gap
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Induction motors, frequency converters and other voltage sag sensitive loads (VSSLs) require that the power supply interruption time should not exceed 30 ms, otherwise the normal operation of the equipment may be affected. In order to guarantee the safe and stable operation of sensitive loads, this paper proposes a uninterrupted fast switching control method for dual power supplies based on the technical route of trigger gap in parallel with fast circuit breaker. This methodology has the advantages of simple structure, high reliability, and switching time of no more than 20 ms. Then the residual voltage characteristics after power loss of induction motors and frequency converters are analyzed, as well as the effect of power switching time on the inrush current of these VSSLs at the switching instant. Accordingly, an uninterrupted switching control strategy between power supplies with both fast switching mode and in-phase switching mode is given, which helps to significantly reduce the impact of voltage dips on the operation of VSSLs.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis on the Synergistic Development between Electricity and Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Under the “dual carbon” targets, the coupling between different energy systems such as electricity, hydrogen, gas, heat, and cooling is becoming increasingly urgent. Hydrogen has emerged as a crucial agent connecting the power industry with various end-use sectors. This paper innovatively proposes the three levels of understanding the synergistic development of electricity and hydrogen. The three levels specifically entail: the coordinated value of electricity and hydrogen within the renewable energy system, the system synergy based on physical coupling, and the industrial chain synergy grounded in industrial layout. Then, the analysis framework including the three major values, the four synergy mechanisms and the supporting policies and market requirements are proposed. At last, the four synergy mechanisms are elaborated in detail to illustrate how electricity and hydrogen could work together. The paper could provide important guidance and is of high value to the theory of synergy between electricity and hydrogen.

articleTitle: Short Term Power Load Forecasting Model Based on XGBoost-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Short-term power load forecasting is able to effectively help power companies to map out electricity generation schemes, allocate grid resources, provide system security analysis and facilitate power market transactions, which can help to ensure a stable and reliable supply of electricity, and has become more and more important in the operation and management of power supply enterprises. In order to upgrade the precision and economy of power load forecasting and enhance the intelligent level of load forecasting, this article establishes a short-term power load forecasting model on the basis of XGBoost-BiLSTM(eXtreme Gradient Boosting- Bi-directional Long Short Term Memory). First, the load data is preprocessed to remove the dirty data that affects the forecasting results. Then the load data is input into XGBoost and BiLSTM models for feature learning. Finally, Stacking is used to fuse the two training models. The research results show that XGBoost-BiLSTM short-term power load forecasting model can improve the precision of load forecasting and provide effective help for power load forecasting.

articleTitle: Evaluation on the Construction of New Power System of Different Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The report of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China has set the direction for the high-quality and leapfrog development of energy and electricity in the new era and put forward higher requirements. To actively implement the “dual carbon” strategy and promote the construction of a new energy system, the evaluation of the power system should also be based on the new stage of development and guided by new development concepts. The development of the new power system first needs to ensure the reliability, safety, and electrical energy quality of the power grid, and ensure the unique characteristics of the new power system in resource optimization, cleanliness, and economy. Based on this, a comprehensive evaluation index system for the construction of the new power system has been established. Corresponding indicator data from four power grid companies nationwide from 2014 to 2023 was collected, and finally, the AHP-TOPSIS method was used to evaluate the comprehensive scores of each power grid company. This provides a multi-level, long-term, comprehensive, and holistic evaluation of the current status of new power system construction in the power grid.

articleTitle: Analysis of Wind Turbine Vibration Suppression Based on a New Damping System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With global warming, extreme weather conditions in coastal areas have increased significantly. Offshore wind turbines are facing worsening environmental loading conditions, which will undoubtedly exacerbate the top vibration and structural damage of wind turbines. In this paper, we design a damping system for top vibration damping of wind turbines. The modeling results show that, for the new damping system, the nacelle displacement can be guaranteed to be within a reasonable range by choosing the appropriate design stiffness and damping. Finite element analysis shows that it can quickly restore the nacelle to a smooth state in the range of conventional loads. The new damping system can reduce the response of the wind turbine in many aspects such as displacement, bending moment, and stress. This is of great significance for the development and design of offshore wind turbines.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Wind-Solar-Energy Storage Capacity for Large-Scale Renewable Energy Bases Based on Golden Section Search Method
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Recently, China has initiated the construction of large-scale new energy bases to transmit the abundant wind and solar energy from the northwest to the eastern regions. The capacity configuration of wind-solar-storage system significantly influences the effect of new energy transmission. This paper investigates the optimal capacity configuration of wind-solar-storage system for large-scale new energy bases and proposes a configuration method based on the golden section search algorithm. First, a three-stage transmission power curve arrangement method for HVDC systems is proposed based on the load curve of the receiving-end power grid. Using the derived HVDC operation curve, a hyper optimization model for the optimal capacity configuration of wind-solar-storage system is constructed, and the golden section search method is adopted to solve the optimization model. The effectiveness of the proposed method lies in its ability to optimize and determine the appropriate wind-solar-storage capacity ratio efficiently, while minimizing the number of iterations. Feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed approach are demonstrated in the case studies.

articleTitle: Load Forecasting Analysis of Overhead Transmission Lines Based on EMD-LSTM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The power system needs to maintain the immediate balance between the generating power and the load, and the load has the characteristics of nonlinear, time-varying and uncertain. In order to solve this problem, a predictive model is developed by integrating empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network. This model takes into account the impact of weather meteorological characteristics, date characteristics and historical load data to accurately forecast short-term power load. Firstly, feature extraction and signal denoising are carried out by empirical mode decomposition to eliminate the fluctuation of data. Secondly, the pre-processed data is trained by LSTM, and the output results are reconstructed. Finally, load forecasting is carried out, and the forecasting effect of EMD-LSTM combined forecasting model is compared with back propagation (BP) neural network forecasting model, LSTM neural network forecasting model and EMD-SVM forecasting model respectively. The results show that the combined prediction model of EMD-LSTM neural network has the best prediction effect and improves the prediction accuracy effectively.

articleTitle: Matching Optimization of Wind-Solar Complementary Power Generation System Based on Joint Probability Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The intermittency, randomness and volatility of wind power and photovoltaic power generation bring trouble to power system planning. The capacity configuration of integrated energy system including wind power photovoltaic usually does not consider the uncertainty of wind power output, resulting in too idealized system capacity configuration and low equipment utilization. In this paper, Copula theory is applied to establish the joint probability distribution model of wind farm and photovoltaic power plant output, and the typical daily output sequence is obtained. A capacity matching method of wind-wind complementary system based on stochastic programming is proposed to effectively suppress the output fluctuation of new energy generation. Finally, a typical daily wind-solar output scenario is generated according to the measured data, and the capacity ratio of the wind-solar complementary system is optimized by analyzing the example.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Oscillation Assessment of Traction Power Supply System Integrated with Railway Power Conditioner
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The inclusion of railway power conditioner (RPC) is a reliable way to address power quality problems in traction power supply system. However, the structure of the traction power supply system will change due to RPC, which will also cause a change in the law of low-frequency oscillation. This paper aims to evaluate the low-frequency oscillation of the traction power supply system integrated with RPC from the perspective of impedance analysis. Firstly, a low-frequency oscillation model is established for the traction power supply system. An assessment method for the sensitivity of each parameter to the amplitude and frequency of low-frequency oscillations is further proposed. Finally, the correctness of the proposed method is verified by MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Degradation Prediction for Fuel Cell Based on Random Forest Regression and Grey Wolf Optimizer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Accurately predicting the degradation of fuel cells and then extending their lifespan through reasonable management measures is crucial. This paper proposes a novel method that combines random forest regression with grey wolf optimization algorithm to predict the degradation of fuel cells. First, the measurement data is reconstructed using a Gaussian average weighted smoothing method to reduce the measurement noise. Then, a degradation model of fuel cells is established using random forest regression. Finally, the hyperparameters of the random forest are optimized using the grey wolf optimization algorithm to improve the accuracy of degradation prediction. The effectiveness of this method is verified through degradation experiments conducted at two different load currents. The test results demonstrate that proposed method can significantly improve the accuracy of degradation prediction and outperform other methods in terms of precision.

articleTitle: Influence and Analysis of PFC of DFIG on the Ultra-Low Frequency Oscillations Mode of Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The large-scale integration of renew abIes into power systems leads to the decrease of system inertia. Grid codes require renewable generators, e.g., wind turbines (WTs), to actively participate system frequency regulation. Whereas, the addition of frequency control inevitably induces the electromechanical interactions between WTs and power systems. In this paper, the influence of primary frequency control (PFC) of DFIG on ultra-low frequency oscillation of power system is studied. Firstly, a modified two-area four-machine test system is built, via numerical simulations, we identify that high gain of DFIG PFC can possibly stimulate an ultra-low frequency oscillation around 0.06 Hz. Subsequently, a small-signal model of such system is constructed and a closer analysis on this phenomenon is carried by eigenvalue and participation factor analysis. The key control parameters related to this mode is identified, and investigated by eigenvalue sensitivity analysis. Time domain analysis are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the analysis above.

articleTitle: Cost-Effective Single-Phase to Three-Phase Power Conversion for Rural Electrification in Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In several rural or remote areas, single-phase distribution systems are commonly utilized due to considerations of construction and maintenance costs. However, the demand for three-phase power in these areas is increasing due to social development. To solve this demand, a single-phase to three-phase power flow controller for low- and medium-voltage single-phase AC systems is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the proposed system consists of a reversing YN dll transformer and three half-bridge converters to achieve the feature of single-phase to three-phase conversion. Secondly, employing control strategies based on rotating coordinates, this system not only achieves the unity power factor as well as compensates for the harmonic currents generated by the loads, but also blocks voltage fluctuations from the grid such as grid voltage sags, swells, and harmonics to ensure the security and stability of the loads. Finally, the static and dynamic performance of the system under each operating condition is verified by simulation, demonstrating its rapid response capabilities.

articleTitle: Research on Substation Load Forecasting Method Based on GRA-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To optimize load-side resource allocation, power grid companies require advanced substation load forecasting, especially in regions with significant load fluctuations. These fluctuations are influenced by seasonal demands for cooling and heating, changes in electric vehicle (EV) energy consumption, and the complexity introduced by renewable energy sources. Traditional forecasting methods fall short in accurately analyzing and predicting these dynamics. This paper addresses these challenges by first analyzing the previous year's load data at the substation level, breaking it down into base load, seasonal demands, EV load, and renewable energy output. It then constructs a detailed feature set including weather conditions and holidays, and uses Grey Relational Analysis (GRA) to identify features strongly correlated with load. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are employed for predicting various load components, with the results aggregated to estimate total substation load. This method, combining load decomposition, GRA, and LSTM, is validated against historical data from a northern region of China and outperforms traditional forecasting algorithms, significantly improving substation load forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: Prediction of Dissolved Gas Concentration in Transformer Oil Based on VMD and ISABO-KELM
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of significant time series volatility and insufficient prediction accuracy in the prediction of dissolved gas concentration in transformer oil, a new prediction method is proposed, which incorporates the Variational Mode Decomposition(VMD), the improved Subtraction-Average-Based Optimizer(ISABO), and the Kernel Based Extreme Learning Machine(KELM). Firstly, the original gas concentration sequence is decomposed using the VMD method to eliminate the non-stationarity and modal aliasing in the data; then, ISABO incorporating the Bernoulli chaotic mapping, Piecewise chaotic mapping, and the golden sine method is designed to enhance the optimization efficiency and the effect is verified by six test functions; and finally, the The core parameters of the KELM algorithm are optimized using ISABO to achieve accurate prediction of each component of the dissolved gas concentration in oil, and the components of the prediction results are superimposed to arrive at the final predicted value of dissolved gas concentration. The experimental results show that compared with the existing SVM and KELM models, the MAE value of this method on the test set is reduced by 10.32% and 7.95%, the RMSE value is reduced by 12.01 % and 8.98%, and the R2 value is improved by 20.04 % and 17.36%, which indicates that this method has higher accuracy in the prediction of transformer gas concentration.

articleTitle: Study on the Output Power Characteristics of Photovoltaic Modules under Different Sand Flow Velocities
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In desert environments, the output power of photovoltaic (PV) modules is influenced by various factors. It is particularly important to investigate the impact of different wind speeds on the output power of PV modules in the northwestern regions of China, where solar resources are abundant and windblown sand is prevalent. By simulating the wind and sand erosion in a desert PV power plant using a wind tunnel, this study examines the effect of dust deposition on the output power of PV modules under different wind speeds (5 m/s, 10 m/s, and 15 m/s). The study reveals that the output power of the PV modules in the first three rows increases with the wind speed. However, the first row experiences the highest power loss rate, with a maximum value of 6.8%. The power loss rates for the second and third rows are relatively low at wind speeds of 5 m/s and 10 m/s, around 1%. At a wind speed of 15 m/s, the power loss rates for the second and third rows increase to approximately 2%. The power loss rate of the fourth row of the PV array generally shows a trend of first increasing and then decreasing, with the maximum power loss rate occurring at a wind speed of 10 m/s, reaching 2.13%. At a wind speed of 15 m/s, the maximum power loss rate is 1.79%, and at a wind speed of 5 m/s, the power loss rate is the lowest, at 0.71%.

articleTitle: Key Technology Research and Application of Integrated Controller for 300MW Variable Speed Pumped Storage Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Based on the actual engineering requirements of large capacity variable speed pumped storage units (VSPSU) of 300MW and above, this paper analyzes the key issues of comprehensive control of variable speed pump storage units. Firstly, information exchange methods between various systems are proposed. Then, a comprehensive control system scheme for VSPSU s is formed, and further realizes collaborative control strategies for different scenarios, including automatic power generation/pumping control, automatic voltage control, power generation start-up and grid connected operation, etc. The modeling and analyze results of this work can promote the research and application comprehensive control technologies of VSPSUs.

articleTitle: Study of Droplet Transfer and Spatter in Pulsed Gas Metal arc Welding for Pressure Pipeline Welding
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Pulsed gas metal arc welding (GMA W-P), a prevalent welding method for pressure pipelines, has attracted widespread interests due to its flexible parameter adjustment, superior welding performance, and robust environmental adaptability. However, inappropriate droplet transfer mode and electric parameters may lead to intense spatters, worsening the weld quality. Facing these issues, this study aims to in-situ monitor the droplet transfer and spatter generation processes in pressure pipeline welding, using a high-speed camera and electrical sensors. The objective is to reveal the mechanisms underlying different droplet transfer modes and spatters, thereby providing valuable reference and determination of process parameter (welding current and arc voltage) to diminish common spatters.

articleTitle: A New Type of Forced Commutation Vacuum DC Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In medium and high voltage DC power systems, traditional forced commutation breaking technology has the problem of breaking failure due to heavy breakdown after arc current crosses zero when turning off short-circuit current. This article proposes a new type of forced commutation vacuum DC circuit breaker from two aspects: reducing the current drop rate during short-circuit breaking process and the voltage rise rate during transient recovery process. A mathematical model was constructed, and the short-circuit breaking principle of the circuit breaker was analyzed in detail. This aspect was optimized from several aspects such as branch stray inductance, auxiliary commutation input time, arc voltage, etc. Finally, a test circuit was constructed to verify the high current breaking test. The results show that through the conduction and diversion effect of the auxiliary switch, without significantly affecting the rapid current transfer process, the current drop rate near the arc extinguishing can be effectively reduced, and a sufficiently long low current change rate range can be maintained; Meanwhile, after the arc is extinguished, the transient recovery voltage at both ends of the vacuum circuit breaker can be clamped at a relatively low level for a relatively long time. The new commutation scheme simultaneously improves the arc current characteristics and post arc recovery voltage characteristics of vacuum circuit breakers. Compared with existing improvement schemes that only focus on pre arc current characteristics or post arc voltage characteristics, it has more obvious advantages in improving the reliability of DC vacuum circuit breakers in high current breaking.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation Study on the Hydrodynamic Performance of Circular Oscillating Buoy Wave Energy Generation Device
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Wave energy, as an environmentally friendly and sustainable energy source, possessed substantial development potential and held significant application value in the domain of new energy technologies. To enhance the capture efficiency of wave energy, a novel oscillating buoy-type wave energy generation device was designed. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) method was applied to numerically simulate the hydrodynamic performance of the wave energy generation device, providing a theoretical foundation for optimizing the design of wave energy generation devices. Firstly, a numerical wave tank was established, and the effectiveness and accuracy of the numerical wave tank were validated. Secondly, a hole was made at the center of the circular oscillating buoy, and the CFD software Star-CCM+ was used to numerically simulate the hydrodynamic performance of the buoy with openings. This paper considered different aperture sizes of the buoy under two sets of different conditions, including 200mm, 300mm, 400mm, 500mm, 600mm, 700mm and 800mm. Based on the numerical simulation results, through statistical analysis, the oscillating force and oscillating motion amplitude data of the oscillating buoys with different apertures were obtained, covering the maximum, minimum, average, variance, and mean deviation values for each aperture size of the buoys. Thirdly, the vorticity of eight typical oscillating buoys was compared and analyzed in this study, thereby investigating the inner mechanism between force and vorticity. Through statistical analysis of the hydrodynamic performance of a circular oscillating buoy with different aperture sizes, the following conclusions can be drawn: Under the same operating conditions, the oscillating buoy with a 300mm aperture exhibited the largest maximum oscillating force, while the buoy with an 800mm aperture demonstrated the smallest maximum oscillating force. As the aperture size increased, the oscillating force and amplitude generally exhibited a fluctuating decrease. Further analysis using vorticity plots revealed that the buoy with a larger aperture size exhibited more vorticity, indicating greater energy dissipation and smaller oscillating force. Conversely, the buoy with a smaller aperture size exhibited less vorticity, suggesting less energy dissipation and therefore larger oscillating force.

articleTitle: Research on Optimized Scheduling of Hybrid Energy Storage for VPP Based on Wind-Solar Complementary Power Generation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid growth of new energy capacity under the “dual carbon” policy, power systems require greater flexibility. Efficient storage technologies like pumped hydro and compressed air energy storage are crucial but insufficient alone. A Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) is needed to fully meet demand. This paper proposes a multi-objective Virtual Power Plant (VPP) dispatching scheme based on Battery Energy Storage (ES), Pumped Storage (PS) and Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES). A VPP scheduling model is developed, considering the complementarity of various distributed energy sources, Time-Of-Use (TOU) pricing, and Tiered Carbon Trading Prices (TCTP). Using the K-means clustering algorithm, typical annual wind and solar power output scenarios are identified and optimized using the IVYA algorithm. Results indicate that the ES-PS HESS delivers the best performance. Compared with using PS alone, the VPP operating costs decrease by 32.08%, carbon emissions are reduced by 1556.21 Kg, interaction costs with the grid turn from a cost of 2017.36 ¥ to a profit of 2096.55 ¥, and carbon trading costs decrease by 20.83%. Compared with a single energy storage system, the HESS demonstrates higher regulation capability and operational economy, providing strong support for the low-carbon economic operation of new power systems.

articleTitle: Zeroth-Order Feedback Optimization for Inverter-Based Volt-VAR Control in Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Significant penetration of wind power into power systems gives rise to severe power quality concerns, especially voltage violations. In wind farms, the system model parameters are usually inaccurate or even unknown, which brings great difficulties to the implementation of conventional model-based control methods. Moreover, wind farms are usually partially observable since only a few measurements are available at critical nodes. To provide a practical Volt/Var control (VVC) strategy for such networks, a novel model-free VVC method based on zeroth-order feedback optimization is proposed in this paper, which doesn't rely on any system model parameters. Firstly, the proposed method continuously collects system output measurements and evaluates the objective function value at the current input and at the measured output, thus constructing gradient estimates. Then, the control inputs are updated via an accelerated gradient projection algorithm, where the step length is selected based on Barzilai-Borwein-like rules for constrained optimization to improve the speed of convergence. Numerical tests exhibit a promising performance of the proposed method in voltage control.

articleTitle: Active Thermal Control of Grid-Forming Converters Based on DC-link Voltage Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Grid-forming control, as a key technology for building new power systems, enables inertia and damping characteristics of converters to actively support grid frequency and voltage. However, GFM-based converters are often required to generate short-circuit currents in excess of the rated value to support grid voltage recovery during transient faults, which poses a greater challenge to their electro-thermal stresses. At the same time, the over-issuance of short-circuit current will lead to the aggravation of junction temperature fluctuation, which will shorten the lifetime of the power devices and bring new challenges to their reliability. Based on the above problems, this paper firstly establishes a corresponding electrothermal coupling model for the GFM converter synchronized based on DC voltage. Subsequently, an active thermal control technique based on the adaptive adjustment of switching frequency is proposed, which can not only reduce the junction temperature of the power device under the same short-circuit current amplitude, but also further reduce the junction temperature fluctuation of the power device. Finally, the corresponding circuit as well as thermal circuit models are established by simulation software to verify the effectiveness of the strategy.

articleTitle: Construction of Road Network Model and Power Prediction for Electric Vehicles in Weak Link of Urban Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming to predict the charging and discharging power of electric vehicles, a Power Prediction method for Electric Vehicle is proposed by considering their real-time State of Charge (SOC) values and desired SOC values. Firstly, targeting weak links in urban power grids, a road network model was constructed based on Markov chains and a spatiotemporal travel chain for electric vehicles, whereby real geographic coordinates of urban areas serve as the research subject. Then a model was established for the charging and discharging load of electric vehicles at weak links in the power grid. Finally, based on real-time State of Charge (SOC) values and desired SOC values, the charging and discharging power of electric vehicles was predicted. The proposed method for predicting the charging and discharging power of electric vehicles can not only mitigate the impact of a large number of electric vehicles connecting to the grid on its weak links and improve the stability of the distribution network, but also significantly meet the actual charging power demand of urban electric vehicles. Through the study of cases, the effectiveness of the method was validated.

articleTitle: Full Life Cycle Economic Analysis of Flexible Retrofit of Thermal Power Units Under New Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In recent years, with the development of UHV power grid and the large-scale grid-connection of new energy sources, the structure and operation characteristics of the power system have undergone major changes, posing new challenges to the safety and stability of the system, and traditional thermal power units are facing the pressure of being crowded out of the output space and early retirement. Adding phase modulation function to thermal power units through flexible transformation has become an effective way to improve system voltage stability and promote the development of thermal power plants. In this paper, the economy of flexible transformation of thermal power units is analyzed in detail from three stages of manufacturing, operation and scrapping during the whole life cycle of thermal power units. The results show that the modified thermal power unit can participate in both the electricity energy market and the auxiliary service market, and the equipment utilization rate and income are greatly improved. At the same time, it is found that by providing reactive power compensation, the phase modulation transformation of thermal power units can maintain the voltage stability of the system, reduce the network loss, and is more economical than the new modulation camera. Therefore, the flexible transformation of thermal power units is an important measure to realize the safe and stable operation of the new power system, and has significant economic benefits and wide application prospects.

Author Keywords: phase modulation transformation of thermal power units

articleTitle: Research on Photovoltaic Power Prediction Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The output of photovoltaic (PV) systems is significantly influenced by factors such as sunlight and weather conditions, leading to substantial variations. Ensuring stable electricity supply is crucial for meeting consumer demands. Accurate PV power forecasting enables grid operators to anticipate fluctuations in PV generation, facilitating timely scheduling and operational decisions to ensure grid stability and reliability. This article provides a comprehensive review of advanced deep learning methods applied in PV power forecasting, summarizing research developments from both domestic and international perspectives. It discusses key factors influencing PV power prediction, including solar irradiance intensity, temperature, and weather conditions. Additionally, it elaborates on prevalent forecasting techniques, with a particular focus on deep learning approaches and hybrid model predictions. The aim is to equip researchers and practitioners in the PV sector with a thorough understanding of how deep learning methods can innovate and advance power forecasting practices, thereby driving technological progress and industry development.

articleTitle: $H_{\infty}$ Tracking Control for the T-S Fuzzy-Based SS-IPT System with Coil Misalignment
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To cope with the coil misalignment problem existing in the inductive power transfer (IPT) system, an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> tracking control strategy for the practical series-series (SS)- IPT system is put forward in this paper. For this purpose, an augmented Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy modeling methodology is successfully constructed by introducing an integrator of the error between the actual and the reference system output signals first. Then an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}^{-}$</tex> parallel distributed compensation (PDC) fuzzy control framework is designed to ensure desired tracking control performance. Subsequently, sufficient conditions based on extended Lyapunov functional method are employed to achieve the asymptotic stability of the augmented T-S fuzzy-based SS-IPT system and the disturbance suppression index. Finally, a simulation example with regard to the SS- IPT system is developed, which demonstrates that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> PDC fuzzy control strategy proposed in this paper can maintain the constant output voltage of the SS- IPT system.

articleTitle: Regenerative Braking Control Method for Electric Unmanned Vehicles Based on Speed Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to improve the energy recovery rate of electric unmanned vehicles during operation, ensure the safety and economy of vehicle operation, a speed prediction based regenerative braking control strategy for electric unmanned vehicles is proposed. The road condition recognition algorithm based on offline training neural network model and the vehicle speed prediction method based on improved Markov chain are adopted to make the predicted values more accurate. Using sliding sampling window method for online pattern recognition of vehicle driving status, and converting predicted speed values into power requirements for vehicle operation, then solving the torque applied to vehicle tires through model predictive controller to determine the optimal solution for braking torque control of electric unmanned vehicles. The experimental results show that the average range of the vehicle has increased by 29.11%, and the energy recovery rate has reached 44.11%. Therefore, this study indicates that electric unmanned vehicles using regenerative braking control strategies can effectively control the energy recovery efficiency during the braking process and expand the range.

articleTitle: Peak Shaving Power Construction Path for Renewable Energy Consumption Considering Medium and Long-term Carbon Prices Changes
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the investment of large-scale renewable energy power bases, enhancing the peaking capacity of power systems to ensure long-term economic benefits has become the focus of attention. Compared to energy storage-based peaking, leveraging gas turbines and deeply retrofitted thermal power plants for peaking presents more economic advantages. However, such peak shaving operations, when implemented with modified coal-fired power plants and gas turbines, will inevitably increase carbon dioxide emissions, leading to additional peaking costs under carbon quota policies. To address this, a long-term dynamic change oriented renewable energy power base retrofitting method is proposed in this paper, taking into account the long-term economic benefits of thermal power plant retrofits, gas turbine investments, and energy storage. However, the traditional, crude linearization of carbon emissions models for deeply modulated gas turbines can lead to deviations from economically optimal decisions. Thus, a refined, nonlinear carbon emission model is established in this paper and solved by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. Case studies based on a real-world power system in Northwest China is employed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Review of Photovoltaic Power Generation Forecasting Techniques and Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Due to global warming, the global demand for renewable energy is gradually growing. Photovoltaic(PV), which accounts for about 47.3% in the field of renewable energy, is an important part of this sector. Accurate PV power generation prediction is particularly important to meet the increasing energy demand. This paper analyzes the factors affecting PV forecasting, describes in detail the advantages and disadvantages of various forecasting models, and summarizes the model evaluation indexes used at this stage. It is found that accurate PV forecasts consider a variety of weather factors, and only highly correlated data as model inputs can have a favorable impact on the model. The length of the model prediction time directly affects the prediction accuracy of the model, and short-term predictions tend to be more accurate than long-term predictions. A single model, either a physical model or a deep learning model, has good prediction results in different scenarios, but lacks generalization and stability. Based on these findings, this paper proposes some suggestions to improve the prediction accuracy, including considering high correlation factors, training the weather data for classification, studying cloud motion, and a single model by optimization or mixing multiple models to get more stable results. This study synthesizes and analyzes the articles in recent years to provide a reference for improving PV prediction accuracy and promoting the efficient use of PV energy.

articleTitle: Frequency Security-Constrained Day-Ahead Dispatch Considering Flexible Load Power Support
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The randomness and uncertainty of renewable energy have brought great challenges to the frequency security of power systems. In the foreseeable future, flexible loads with frequency support capability will be widely integrated. As flexible loads and power systems belong to different stakeholders, how to coordinate the benefits of both entities to ensure frequency security still needs to be studied. This paper establishes a frequency security-constrained day-ahead dispatch method considering the incentive price-based power support of flexible loads. Firstly, the power system model with frequency security constraints is constructed, where an innovative method for frequency constraints based on convex relaxation is used to reduce the calculation while meeting engineering requirements. Secondly, an incentive price decision-making strategy for frequency regulation between the power system and the flexible loads is proposed, where the Stackelberg game is introduced to depict the different interests of the two stakeholders. Furthermore, the multi-agent feature leads to the multiplication of the power system's incentive price and the flexible loads' frequency regulation capacity, which makes the optimization model bilinear. This challenge is transformed using the strong duality theory, and the frequency security-constrained day-ahead dispatch model considering the uncertainty intervals is established, which can be easily solved by the classic two-stage optimization algorithm. Case studies show that the proposed method can effectively incentivize flexible loads to perform power support, and has good effects in ensuring the frequency security and the robustness of the power system.

articleTitle: Power Forecasting Model for Photovoltaic Generation System Based on Long Short Term Memory Network
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this work, power forecasting model for photovoltaic generation system based on Long Short Term Memory Network (LSTM) is presented. In the field of photovoltaic power generation, due to the strong randomness and intermittedness of photovoltaic power generation, large-scale grid-connection has a great impact on the load of energy storage grid, so photovoltaic prediction has a great reference significance for resource management and scheduling. This paper studies the photovoltaic power generation prediction method based on LSTM. With light, humidity and temperature as model input and power generation as model output, a LSTM prediction model for photovoltaic power generation prediction is constructed to solve the problem of gradient disappearance and gradient explosion. The experimental results of actual data show that the test set RMSE of the proposed model is 0.16859, R2 is 0.93203, and the prediction effect is good.

articleTitle: Dynamic Parameter Identification Method of Synchronous Machine with Arbitrary Rotor Position Based on three-Phase Connected DC-Decay Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The three-phase short-circuit test is a common method for measuring transient parameters of large synchronous machines. The experimental process is complex and carries certain risks. Traditional stationary test methods can enhance the safety of parameter identification experiments; however, the required rotor pre-positioning for these experiments is difficult to implement in large synchronous machines. To address these issues, this paper proposes a synchronous machine parameter identification method based on a three-phase connection of the DC decay test at arbitrary rotor positions, grounded on the principle of signal input experiments. This method equivalently transforms the DC decay test of the three-phase connection at arbitrary positions into independent rotor d- and q-axis pre-positioned DC decay tests. Using the simulated annealing particle swarm optimization algorithm to fit the current response signal, the machine's dynamic parameters are calculated. The validity and accuracy of the proposed parameter identification method were verified through experiments on a 172 MV A synchronous machine. This method requires low testing equipment, involves fewer tests, and has simple data processing, making it safe and reliable.

articleTitle: Optimal Reserve Determination for Diversified Frequency Regulation Resources via Frequency Constrained Unit Commitment
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable energy sources, the frequency security of power systems is increasingly challenged. In this paper, we propose a frequency constrained unit commitment (FCUC) to determine the optimal reserve for diversified frequency support resources (DFSRs), ensuring that the system's frequency response capability after power disturbances meets the specified requirements. DFSRs and load frequency relief (LFR) are considered based on the inertia dependent frequency reserve (IDFR) model, and a joint model-data driven approach is proposed to address the challenges of frequency response analytical expression and maximum frequency deviation constraint convexification arising from the consideration of LFR. Finally, the proposed FCUC is transformed into a mixed-integer linear programming model and validated through case study on the IEEE 39-bus system, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on Automatic Mapping Technology of Substation Monitoring System Based on Decision Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming at the status quo of substation monitoring system with large number of graphics, high cost of drawing labor, and difficulty of manual adjustment after drawing, this paper proposes a method to analyze the mapping behavior of monitoring system based on a large amount of monitoring system interval mapping data accumulated in different regions in the engineering practice, establishes a self-learning corrective mechanism by combining with the analysis of the mapping behavior, and adopts the decision tree algorithm to train and learn the model and generate the training model based on the trained model and combined with the automatic mapping technology. The decision tree algorithm is used to train and learn the model of each region and generate the training model. Based on the trained model and combined with the automatic mapping technology, the interval maps of the monitoring system are automatically generated according to the characteristics of the region and the behavioral characteristics, and the actual engineering test proves that the method researched in this paper has the effect of enhancing the automation application of the automatic mapping of the monitoring system, which greatly reduces the workload of the onsite engineers, and at the same time, the training and selection of the model do not affect the implementation of on-site engineering. At the same time, the model training and selection are carried out under the condition of not affecting the implementation of on-site engineering, which improves the efficiency of engineering production under the condition of meeting the accuracy and practicality, and solves the problem of drawing interval diagrams for substation monitoring system under the huge data and differentiated needs of users.

articleTitle: Active Scheduling Optimization for Electric Vehicle Charging Considering User Preferences
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the increase in the number of electric vehicles, the charging load of electric vehicles has become an important new type of load in the urban distribution network, which also brings new challenges to the stable operation and safety of the power system. Therefore, on the premise of meeting the charging needs of users, it is of great research significance to study the effective charging scheduling method that not only ensures a lower charging cost for users but also reduces the load variance of the power system. This paper formulates a multi-objective active scheduling mathematical model considering the charging behavior preferences of different charging users (charging distance, charging time, charging price, etc.) and proposes an improved NSGA-II algorithm to solve the model. Experimental results show that our proposed active scheduling optimization method considering the users' charging behavior preferences is effective in guiding users to charge in an orderly manner.

articleTitle: Coordinated Scheduling Method of Hydrogen- Integrated Multi-Energy District in Joint Market Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper proposes a coordinated scheduling method for a hydrogen-integrated multi-energy district (HMED) to realize the effective., profitable., and green operation of HMED. A joint market mechanism including capacity., energy., and ancillary service markets is developed considering the coordination of annual and daily decisions of HMED. A hybrid hydrogen storage system including both daily and seasonal hydrogen storages is modeled to achieve intraday and cross- seasonal peak shaving. It is proved by case studies that the proposed coordinated scheduling method can improve the economy of and the flexibility and capacity adequacy provided by HMED., moreover., it can optimize the integration of hydrogen facilities.

articleTitle: Performance Study of the Direct Cooling Thermal Management System for Blade Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The blade battery offers a longer lifespan, enhanced safety, and improved space utilization and battery pack integration. However, its heat generation distribution differs from cylindrical or square cells. To address this, we designed a shunt-controlled direct cooling plate tailored to the heat generation characteristics of blade batteries. Using numerical simulation, we evaluated the thermal management system's performance. Under 1.5 C charging and equal refrigerant mass flow rate, the shunt-controlled direct cooling plate effectively maintained the battery module's maximum temperature and temperature difference within acceptable limits. Compared to serpentine channel and liquid cooling plates, the new design lowered the battery module's maximum temperature by 1.3 K and 3.7 K, respectively, and reduced the temperature difference by 280/0 and 11°/0. We also analyzed the effects of inlet refrigerant temperature and mass flow rate. Increasing the refrigerant temperature raised the maximum battery temperature but improved temperature uniformity. Conversely, increasing the mass flow rate enhanced heat dissipation but significantly increased system pressure drop. This study provides valuable insights for developing direct cooling thermal management systems and designing new cooling plates for power batteries of new direct cooling plates.

articleTitle: Air Conditioning Load Cluster Electricity Aggregation Model Based on Multi-Dimensional Clustering and Double Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The participation of multi-type air conditioning (AC) load aggregation in power grid demand response can better help the power grid to suppress the peak-valley difference and absorb renewable energy generation. Considering the strong correlation between AC power consumption and environmental data, an AC load power aggregation model based on multi-dimensional clustering and double decomposition is proposed in this paper. First of all, data preprocessing is carried out on the obtained AC power consumption data and use environment data. Secondly, grey relation analysis (GRA) is used to select the factors with strong correlation with the power consumption of AC load as input variables, and then partitioning and selecting clusters (PSC) -Kmeans ++ clustering method is used to aggregate the original data after screening. Then IVMD-PE-CEEMDAN, an innovative algorithm synthesizing the improved variational mode decomposition, permutation entropy, and complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise methods was used for secondary decomposition to ensure the decomposition effect, mining the data characteristics, and improving the aggregation effect of the model. This method aims to improve the accuracy and reliability of the air conditioning load aggregation model for smart grid applications.

articleTitle: Flow Field Simulation and Model Order Reduction Techniques for Hydro Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To explore the operational patterns of pumped storage power stations in order to meet the demand for real-time acquisition of three-dimensional velocity field data of turbines, the paper establishes a three-dimensional reduced-order model of a turbine based on finite volume method simulation. Using Pera Sim Fluid software to perform numerical simulations of a Francis-99 turbine under various operating conditions and construct a dataset. Modal and modal coefficient extraction is performed on the dataset through Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), and a mathematical relationship between operating variables and modal coefficients is established using Radial Basis Function (RBF) method, thereby achieving rapid prediction of the three-dimensional velocity field of turbines under arbitrary operating variables. The results show that this model can achieve interpolation prediction within the operating range with a small number of samples, demonstrating high generalization and accuracy. The average relative error of the computational results is 0.02%, with a numerical error of less than 0.5 m/s, and the average time for obtaining turbine velocity field data is reduced to 0.5 seconds.

articleTitle: Short-term Power Load Prediction Method for High Voltage Power Cables Based on IGOA-VMD-LSTM-MHSAM
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Short-term power load prediction of high-voltage power cables (HVPC) is an important basis for the development of its maintenance plan. Aiming at the current problem of low accuracy of HVPC short-term power load prediction, this paper proposes a HVPC power load prediction method based on IGOA-VMD-LSTM-MHSAM. Firstly, for the typical nonlinear characteristics of HVPC power load, the parameter optimization of Vibrational Mode Decomposition (VMD) is achieved by using Gannet Optimization Algorithm (GOA) improved by Sine chaotic mapping and nonlinear convergence factor, and the parameter optimization of VMD is adopted. IGOA to decompose the HVPC power load into several Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). Then Multi-head Self-Attention Mechanism (MHSAM) is introduced into Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to improve its feature extraction capability, thus obtaining the LSTM-MHSAM HVPC power load prediction model. Finally, the effectiveness of the LSTM-MHSAM model is verified using the actual power load data of a 220kV HVPC in a city in China. The experimental results show that the proposed prediction model for HVPC short-term power load prediction results are closer to the actual load. Compared with the traditional forecasting methods, the proposed model has higher accuracy and stability, and has certain potential for practical application.

articleTitle: Strategy of Smart Grid Disaster Recovery and Scheduling Based on Cloud Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In response to the emergence of new challenges in the digitization of the power grid, disaster recovery construction, driven by laws and regulations, is gradually becoming normalized. Disaster recovery has become a fundamental compliance requirement for key industries. Considering the issue of low resource utilization and high costs associated with traditional scheduling data disaster recovery solutions, enhancing grid data processing efficiency and strengthening grid risk prevention capabilities have become focal points in the construction of power systems. Under this backdrop, this paper proposes integrating cloud computing technology with smart grid systems and puts forward a disaster recovery business solution featuring dual-active in the same city and multi-active in different locations. Leveraging the efficient data computing capabilities of cloud computing, a unified platform tailored for security zones is designed to enhance grid big data processing efficiency. This platform achieves minute-level one-way synchronization of data across instances. Additionally, exploring business-oriented scheduling methods on this foundation, a comprehensive disaster recovery strategy for power scheduling data based on cloud computing technology is formulated.

articleTitle: Research on Photovoltaic MPPT Based on Improved Butterfly Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To solve slow response speed and poor stability of traditional MPPT algorithms under rapidly changing environmental conditions, a MPPT control strategy combining improved butterfly algorithm and disturbance observation method is proposed. Firstly, the butterfly position in the population is initialized by Tent map, increasing the search space; Secondly, Gaussian mutation strategy is introduced to make the algorithm break out of local extremes; Then, a dynamic probability switching mechanism is adopted to balance the weight relationship between global and local search, improving algorithm optimization efficiency; Finally, in the later stage, disturbance observation method is used to track the maximum power and reduce power oscillation. Simulation examples show that the proposed algorithm can find the maximum power point quickly and accurately under both static and dynamic shading conditions, and the power output is more stable.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Demand Response Potential in Air Conditioning Systems Considering Detailed Energy Flow Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Evaluating the demand response potential of air-conditioning systems can support mitigating power shortages caused by the surge in air-conditioning loads during summer. Existing evaluation models often fail to fully account for the energy consumption of each subsystem within the air conditioning and the user's willingness to respond. To address this issue, this paper proposes a demand response potential evaluation model for air-conditioning systems based on detailed energy flow characteristics. This model optimizes the energy efficiency of air-conditioning system loads. First, the energy consumption model of the air-conditioning system is developed by analyzing its energy flow characteristics. Next, a regional temperature regulation strategy based on user response willingness is established. An improved adaptive genetic algorithm is then employed to solve the optimization problem. Finally, the model's rationality and effectiveness are verified through simulations of an air-conditioning system in a large shopping mall. The simulation results demonstrate a 46% increase in algorithm iteration speed and a reduction in energy consumption by 2391 kW. Additionally, the demand response potential of the air-conditioning system improves by 7% compared to other models, ensuring the safe and stable operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Optimizing Scheduling Strategies for Microgrids with Electric Vehicles Considering Spatiotemporal Two-Dimensional Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper first briefly reviews the development of electric vehicle battery swapping load, microgrid optimization scheduling, and power demand response technology. Considering that there are a large number of time-adjustable and spatially transferable power loads in the power changing station, load fluctuations of electric vehicles and the increasing number of power changing stations require microgrids not only to achieve load balance in space, but also to adjust load fluctuations in time. It is of great research value to explore the power demand response of EVS on a spatiotemporal scale. In this context, this paper discusses the optimal operation of microgrids containing electric vehicles taking into account renewable energy consumption. First, the impact of battery swapping station loads on the power grid is analyzed, and a basic optimization model of microgrids is constructed. Secondly, the hierarchical analysis method is used to obtain the spatiotemporal satisfaction; finally, a microgrid battery swapping load scheduling strategy model considering spatiotemporal satisfaction and renewable energy consumption is constructed, and simulation analysis is performed using the YALMIP toolbox and CPLEX solver. The results show that the microgrid battery swapping load scheduling strategy considering spatiotemporal satisfaction and renewable energy consumption can provide a theoretical basis for microgrids to implement charging and discharging price incentives for battery swapping stations, while promoting the microgrid's consumption of renewable energy and reducing carbon emissions. In addition, this strategy optimization can promote the optimal allocation and use of energy resources, improve the operational efficiency and responsiveness of the entire grid.

articleTitle: Analyzing Transient Voltage Stability Using DA of A State-Reduction Model of Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: High complexity is one of harsh problems in transient voltage stability analysis (TVSA) of power systems. To overcome this difficulty, a state-reduction model incorporating induction motors (IMs) has been considered. And an expanding interior algorithm based on Sum of Squares (SOS) programming is adopted to estimate the domain of attraction (DA) of the state-reduction model for TVSA. First the state space is transformed to polynomial space using coordinate transformation. Then based on Lyapunov stability theorems, relaxed constraints for the DA are derived. Then the expanding interior algorithm based on SOS programming is utilized to simultaneously optimize the Lyapunov function and the DA.
