The proposed methodology is validated through modified IEEE test cases, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness in enhancing transient voltage stability assessment in complex power systems.

articleTitle: Research Status and Prospects of Wideband Measurement Technology for New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the large-scale renewable energy access to the power system, the signal state, fault form, and stability state have changed, to cope with this challenge, measurement technology is required to be able to accurately identify the complex signals and deeply perceive the weak signals, to realize the fine and rapid measurement of the full-band information within the fields of power system monitoring, electromagnetic transient protection, equipment intelligence, and power metering. Based on the summary of related literature, the development and application of broadband measurement in these fields are summarized from high-frequency signal sampling, frequency and position sensing, to fault sensing, and then to data transmission, and the future development of broadband measurement is predicted.

articleTitle: Loss Sensitivity Calculation and Analysis Based on Graph Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Loss sensitivity in electricity systems refers to the responsiveness of power losses in electrical transmission and distribution networks to various influencing factors. This concept is critical for optimizing the efficiency and reliability of power delivery from generation sources to end consumers. Especially in the electricity market trading process, network losses, although only a small part of the total cost, have a significant impact on each specific transaction and grid user. Therefore, in-depth understanding and analysis of the impact of generation transactions on the grid network loss can provide a basis for the power purchase plan for the grid to provide reference for the grid network loss management, which is of great significance. The current mainstream calculation and analysis method for network loss sensitivity is the marginal loss coefficient method, which determines the network loss share of each bus by analyzing the impact of bus injected power on the total network loss changes, but the nature of its serial calculation cannot properly solve the balance between real-time analysis of network loss optimization and accuracy, and with the increase in system size, this problem has gradually become a major obstacle to the realization of real- time analysis. This paper presents a novel parallel computing method based on graph computing for determining the sensitivity of system network loss and node-injected power. Graph computing is a parallel computing method that stores, computes, and analyzes the information in a system by constructing a topological graph model and based on it. The method alleviates the computational burden associated with calculating network loss sensitivity as the scale of the power system expands by leveraging the parallel computing capabilities of graph databases. Furthermore, it facilitates the graphical calculation and analysis of network loss sensitivity through the utilization of graph storage.

articleTitle: Analysis on Electricity System low-carbon Transformation — A Case Example from Fujian Province
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper uses SBM-NDEA model to measure the efficiency of electricity low-carbon transformation in 30 regions of China, and analyzes the level of electricity low-carbon transformation between Fujian province and other regions, further divides the transformation efficiency of power sector in Fujian province, and deeply explores the optimization path. We find: (1) the average efficiency of China's electricity low-carbon transformation has fluctuated around 0.45 in the past decade, and the eastern and western regions are greater than the national average level; (2) for Fujian Province, the electricity low-carbon level of Fujian province leads, but the electricity low-carbon transformation efficiency growth rate of Fujian province still needed further improvements, which is mainly caused by the inefficiency of electricity transmission and distribution department; (3) the construction of the spot market of electric power helped to solve the efficiency problem of the power transmission and distribution departments in Fujian Province to some extent, but there are still many deficiencies. Finally, we provides some suggestions for the optimization of electricity transmission and distribution department in Fujian.

articleTitle: A Closed-loop SOC Estimator for LiFePO4 Batteries Using Improved Neural Network and Particle Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Accurate estimation of the state of charge (SOC) is vital for the safe operation of battery systems. Traditional SOC estimation methods encounter challenges with LiFePO4 batteries due to their flat open circuit voltage characteristic in the middle range of SOC. Therefore., this paper proposes a closed-loop SOC estimation algorithm which improves the self-attention mechanism to build a neural network for preliminary SOC estimation and uses a particle filter to adaptively fuse the outputs of the neural network and the ampere-hour counting method for the final estimation results. The algorithm also provides a 95% confidence interval for the estimate., facilitating uncertainty assessment. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm exhibits good performance for different temperatures and different cells within a battery pack., with a mean absolute error of less than 0.9% across the entire SOC range. Two extreme test cases demonstrate the algorithm's strong robustness to unknown initial SOC., sensor anomalies., and noise.

articleTitle: Perturbation Observer-Based Frequency Support Control Strategy of VSC- HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the voltage source converter based high voltage direct current (VSC- HVDC) transmission system cannot respond to frequency change of the receiving-end AC grid under traditional control strategy, this paper proposes a perturbation observer-based frequency support control strategy (POFSCS) to improve the active and rapid support capability of the VSC-HVDC system for grid frequency regulation. Firstly, a two-region VSC-HVDC system model is constructed. Then, the frequency-supported control strategy is designed using perturbation observer and feedback linearization control method. The strategy utilizes the maximum available energy of the DC capacitor to regulate grid frequency deviation, thereby improving the response speed and output depth of the frequency regulation controller. Finally, the effectiveness of POF-SCS is verified in MATLAB/Simulink platform. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of POFSCS in effectively suppressing significant frequency deviations and contributing to the enhancement of frequency stability in the receiving-end grid.

articleTitle: Modification of Mathematical Model for Electromagnetic Calculation of Cable with Single-Ended Grounded System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this paper, the corrected mathematical model for electromagnetic calculation of cable grounding system with single-ended grounding is investigated in order to solve the errors caused by the existence of complex ground network and unknown conductors and other factors on the calculation results in practical applications. Combined with the actual measurement data, the superposition theorem and chi-square theorem are used for mathematical modeling and correction. The corrected model can output the expected results when the input excitation changes. The corrected model in this study can more accurately invert the electromagnetic induction results of the cable grounding system, and provide theoretical support for the calculation of actual induced electric parameters in cable engineering.

articleTitle: Capacity Optimization for a Photovaltaic-Integrated Hydrogen Refueling Station System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To promote the widespread adoption of hydrogen fuel cell vehicles, reducing the cost of hydrogen refueling stations (HRS) is impatiently anticipated. This paper proposes a Photovoltaic-Integrated Hydrogen Refueling Station (PI-HRS) and establishes a capacity planning model to configure the PI-HRS to optimize its economic feasibility. Furthermore, a rule-based operating strategy is introduced, and the economic capacity planning model is solved using the improved Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm based on the proposed operating strategy. The optimization results demonstrate that the proposed PI-HRS, compared to traditional HRS, reduces the unit cost of hydrogen energy by 24.62%, which indicates that the optimized configuration of the PI-HRS achieves both economic and environmental benefits effectively. Finally, a sensitivity analysis is conducted to study the influence of electricity prices and hydrogen distribution on the capacity planning results.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Assessment of Hybrid Off Grid AC-DC Microgrid: A Desert Area Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper conducts the techno-economic assessment of an AC/DC off grid hybrid microgrid arrangement mainly designed for the desert location of Quseir, Egypt. This system integrates wind turbines, diesel generators, batteries, photovoltaic, and converters to fulfill the power demand of 257.1 kWh/day in the selected site. Using the HOMER Pro simulation, the designed scheme evaluates according to the cost of electricity, renewable fraction, and loss of power system probability. The simulation results show that the combination of diesel generators, wind turbines, photovoltaic, converter, and batteries effectively satisfies the load demand. In the Quseir area, the most optimal arrangement includes diesel generators of 15 kW, wind turbines of 20 kW, 20 kW solar PV, 40 kW converters, and 80 kW batteries. This configuration has the lowest net present cost of 169,800 $ and an energy cost of 0.140 $/kWh, with a renewable fraction of 82.4%.

articleTitle: An Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm-Based MPPT Method for Distributed Photovoltaic Hydrogen Production Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to cope with the increase in carbon emissions caused by the excessive use of fossil energy, the world's energy structure needs to be adjusted. Distributed photovoltaic (PV) hydrogen production system, as an integrated energy system, is an important pathway to the zero-carbon goal. But distributed PV is prone to face the shading situation, while the PV module power output curve will show the phenomenon of multiple peaks. The traditional maximum power tracking methods are prone to fall into the local optimal situation, and the intelligent tracking methods are inherently more complex. The hydrogen production electrolyzer puts forward the requirement of stability on the output power of the PV power supply. Existing research focuses on the maximum power tracking of PV system, or the control of electrolyzer, lacking the coupled modeling control research of distributed PV hydrogen production system. In order to fill the gap of the existing research, this paper proposes a composite algorithm which combines the Improved Particle Swarm Algorithm (IPSO) with the Improved Perturbation Observation (IP&O) method. The initial population and termination conditions of the particle swarm search method (PSO) are improved to enhance the convergence speed of the algorithm and reduce the oscillations during the convergence process of the algorithm, and the IP&O method is utilized to provide stable inputs for the electrolytic tanks. The performance of the algorithm is verified through the comparative experiments with other algorithms.

articleTitle: Towards Loss Sentivity-based Energy Storage Contol Method for Loss Reduction in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the high proportion of photovoltaic (PV) power generation access, the line loss problem of the distribution network has become one of the focuses of grid enterprises. Increased progress in advanced energy storage systems makes energy storage control a promising tool to improve the operation of the distribution system with PV s since energy storage can be applied for load leveling and reducing system losses. Currently, most methods for power loss reduction are based on the analysis of power flow calculation, which may lack efficiency and flexibility. Therefore, a novel energy storage control method based on the sensitivity of power losses is proposed in this paper. The proposed method has the advantage of low complexity to compute the value of energy storage control for reducing system losses in the distribution system. The performance of the proposed energy storage control approach is evaluated on the IEEE 33 distribution system, demonstrating that the proposed method is effective in reducing power losses without the computational complexity of power flow calculation.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Considering the Safety of Energy Storage Power Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a battery energy storage operation model that comprehensively considers temperature, and safety of state (SOS). Additionally, we present an optimal scheduling method that takes into account the safety of energy storage stations, aiming to address the issues of rapid life decay and poor safety of battery energy storage in wind-photovoltaic-storage system at high temperatures. Through the electrothermal coupling model, an analytical battery electrothermal coupling model suitable for day-ahead scheduling is proposed, and an operation model of the energy storage plant with temperature-power characteristics, considering SOC and SOS, is constructed. Additionally, with the goal of maximizing the total revenue of wind and solar energy storage, while considering temperature and safety limitations of energy storage, the day-ahead optimization scheduling model is linearized, and scheduling strategies that consider the safety of energy storage power stations are developed. Finally, a simulation model was constructed to compare different scheduling schemes. The results showed that the scheduling strategy proposed in this paper, which considers the safety of energy storage stations, can effectively improve the service life, safety, and utilization of battery energy storage operation.

articleTitle: Distributed Primal-Dual Method for Current Sharing and Voltage Regulation in DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Due to the strong coupling between power injection and bus voltage in the DC microgrid, it is challenging to achieve both economic dispatch and restoration of nominal voltages for all buses simultaneously. To address this problem, this paper first proposes a control model based on bi-objective optimization to balances economic efficiency and voltage distribution quality. Furthermore, a distributed weighted gradient primal-dual method is introduced, as even short-term mismatches between generation and demand in the system can lead to voltage collapse. Specifically, this method obtains the gradient information with aggregated variables in a fully distributed manner by the collaborative transmission of weighted information between agents. Compared to existed methods, this method not only maintains supply-demand balance at all times, but also dynamically tracks the optimal operating point, thus achieving online distributed optimization. Finally, the stability and convergence of this method are theoretically analysed and its effectiveness in real-time energy management is validated by simulation studies.

articleTitle: Analysis of Trading Opportunities for Source-Load-Storage Resources in the Main-Auxiliary Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Currently, research on the source-load-storage (SLS) integrated main-auxiliary joint market primarily focuses on modeling and clearing methods, while actual trading opportunities of the various resources in the various markets under the current cost levels are rarely examined. In the light of this, this paper, after constructing a clearing model for the SLS integrated energy-frequency regulation-reserve joint market, presents case studies towards two provincial markets with different SLS cost ratios, analyzing the trading opportunities for various resources in different areas. Results of the case study show that adjustable aggregate loads have trading opportunities in the reserve market in both areas due to their low interruptible costs; electric vehicle aggregators (EVAs) may find trading opportunities in downward frequency regulation market in the area with low coal-fired generation cost; however, in provinces with high coal-fired generation costs, independent energy storage stations may find more opportunities in downward frequency regulation than EVAs. These research findings provide valuable insights for the timely development of load-storage resources across different regions.

articleTitle: Diagnosis Method for Partial Discharge Faults in Power Cables Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming at the current problem of low accuracy of partial discharge fault diagnosis of power cables, this paper proposes a deep learning-based partial discharge fault diagnosis method for power cables. Firstly, the causes and types of partial discharges in high-voltage transmission cables are analyzed, and an experimental platform for partial discharges in high-voltage transmission cables is constructed to collect the original signals. Then the improved complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (ICEEMDAN) is used to decompose the signal to obtain the reconstructed signal, and the fuzzy entropy value is introduced to construct the partial discharge fault feature vector. Finally, a Lévy flight and dynamic weights are used to improve golden sine algorithm (GSA), so IGSA is proposed for realizing the hyper-parameter optimization of convolutional neural network-bi-directional gated recurrent unit (CNN-BiGRU), so as to obtain the partial discharge fault diagnosis model of power cable based on IGAS-CNN-BiGRU. The experimental results prove that the diagnosis accuracy of the method proposed in this paper reaches 98.3333% and the diagnostic efficiency is high, which realizes the accurate diagnosis of partial discharge faults in power cables, and can give full play to the engineering efficiency in power cable operation and maintenance work.

articleTitle: Adjustable Capacity of Hydropower Stations with Hydrological Model in the Watershed
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Hydropower is affected by geographical location, hydrology and meteorology, seasons, etc., making it difficult to predict the output and adjustable capacity of hydropower stations, which restricts the difficulty of local power grid management of hydropower stations. It is urgent to study and consider the distributed adjustable capacity of hydropower in the same basin to ensure the economic operation of hydropower -photovoltaic power generation systems in county power grids. Therefore, a hydropower station runoff prediction model considering multiple factors such as geographical location, hydro meteorology, and season is proposed. Advanced hydro meteorological monitoring technology is adopted to study the regulation characteristics of distributed hydropower stations in the basin. Based on hydrological forecasting in the basin, a quantitative model for the adjustable capacity of distributed hydropower in the basin considering hydro meteorology and demand side flexible resources is proposed. The result can provide a foundation for hydropower-photovoltaic joint power generation and also provide effective guarantees for the economic operation of hydropower-photovoltaic power generation systems in county power grids.

articleTitle: Prediction and Preventive Control Scheme for Wind and PV Power Ramp Events
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: As the large scale integration of photovoltaic and wind power into the grid increases, renewable energy ramp events have become a potential threat to the secure operation of the power grid. To effectively address renewable energy power ramp events, this paper proposes a prediction and preventive control scheme. First, a rolling warning approach is achieved by the long short-term memory network and fuzzy logic, which provides warning levels and guides decision-making for preventive control. Second, a two-stage optimization scheduling model is proposed, including a day-ahead and an intra-day sub-model. The two-stage scheduling model comprehensively considers power support from interconnectors and preventive control costs. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can provide adaptive preventive control strategies for power ramp events with varying risk levels, thereby enhancing the utilization of renewable energy and improving the security of power system.

articleTitle: Research on Economic Emission Dispatch in Power Systems Based on Multi-Objective Membrane Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To solve the non-convex, nonlinear, and discontinuous multi-objective optimization problem of the power system economic emission dispatch, which is very challenging, this article proposes a new multi-objective optimization algorithm based on membrane search to solve the power system dispatch considering the considering the prohibited operation zone of the unit. Taking the power system containing 14 units and 40 units as research cases, equation and inequality constraint processing rules were designed, and the constructed multi-objective membrane search was used for dispatch research of the case system. The Pareto Front of emissions and fuel costs for the 14-unit and 40-unit power systems were presented, and the published research results were used for comparison. The results show that the compromise solution recommended in this article produces less emissions at the same fuel cost, which is of great significance to cost reduction and emission reduction in the power sector, and also further verifies the effectiveness of the proposed multi-objective optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: Power System Transient Stability Analysis Based on Transformer and Supervised Contrastive Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Transient stability analysis (TSA) is crucial for maintaining the stability of power systems. Compared to traditional dynamic simulations, neural network-based power system TSA models have been widely applied in recent years due to their strong nonlinear mapping capability and fast prediction speed. In this paper, a new TSA approach is proposed based on the Transformer neural network, which combines the encoder-decoder architecture and the attention mechanism. A multi-channel feature extraction structure and a supervised contrastive learning algorithm are utilized to mitigate the overfitting phenomenon and enhance the generalization capability of the proposed model, resulting in competitive performance. The efficacy of the proposed TSA method is validated by the superior performance in the standard IEEE 39-bus test case.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Strategy and Capacity Optimization Configuration of Thermal Power-Energy Storage Joint System Based on FESS in Primary Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With high instantaneous power, short response time, and long life cycle, flywheel energy storage has been widely noticed and applied in the field of auxiliary participation of energy storage systems in grid frequency regulation. The participation of flywheel energy storage in primary frequency regulation can effectively share the frequency regulation pressure of thermal power units, improve the frequency safety of the power grid, and is of great significance for improving the frequency regulation performance of the system. Firstly, virtual droop inertia coordinated control strategy based on low-pass filtering for automatic allocation of fire storage power and considering the state of charge of energy storage for fire storage joint primary frequency regulation was designed to achieve power coordinated allocation in the fire storage joint system; Secondly, considering the system's frequency regulation performance, operational costs, and frequency regulation benefits, a collaborative optimization model for primary frequency regulation based on the PSA algorithm was established to achieve capacity configuration and control parameter optimization of flywheel energy storage under coordinated control strategy. Finally, simulation verification was conducted, and the results showed that the proposed coordinated control strategy and capacity configuration collaborative optimization method could effectively reduce system frequency deviation, improve the frequency regulation performance of the fire storage joint primary frequency regulation system, reduce the action amplitude of thermal power units, effectively alleviate the pressure of unit frequency regulation, and improve system economy, promoting the safe and economic operation of the system.

articleTitle: Enhancing Solar Radiation Conversion in Floating Photovoltaic Systems Through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Overreliance on traditional energy sources leads to resource depletion and environmental pollution, posing serious challenges to global energy security. In response, Floating Photovoltaic (FPV) technology has emerged as a promising solution, offering an alternative to traditional ground-mounted Photovoltaic (PV) systems. This study utilizes data collected from Brookhall Estate between September 2022 and January 2023, employing six machine learning algorithms and the interpretable SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) technique to analyze solar radiation convertibility. Random Forest is identified as the most reliable model for FPV prediction. The results highlight the nonlinear impact of factors such as temperature, conductivity, seasonal variations, water depth, and wind direction on solar radiation collection efficiency. Targeted strategies for FPV design and placement are proposed, contributing to overall FPV optimization in alignment with sustainable energy development goals and the pursuit of net-zero emissions.

articleTitle: A Fast Power Control Strategy of Wind Farms Oriented to Power System Transient Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: As wind power is increasingly integrated into power systems, the uncertainty and variability of power systems are rising, resulting in the challenge for the safe and stable operation of power systems. Thus, the fast power control capability of wind farms is significant for power system transient stability. The purpose of this paper is to propose a fast power control strategy for wind farms considering the quantification of wind turbine fast power control capability and the wind turbine classification. Case studies utilize a wind farm comprising 22 wind turbines to validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Fault Location Algorithm for Distribution Network Cables Based on Power Frequency Additional Impedance Angle
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the complex urban power grid environment, traditional fault location methods struggle to quickly and accurately pinpoint fault points, leading to extended repair times and increased risks and costs for grid operation. This paper explores a rapid fault location technique based on cable fault characteristics. It analyzes the composite sequence network characteristics of faults and establishes the relationship between local measurement quantities, fault points, and electrical quantities on the opposite side. Based on the study of composite sequence network characteristics, it investigates the variation law of sequence components after a fault occurs and identifies fault characteristic electrical quantities through sequence components. Consequently, it provides the calculation formula for measuring impedance for single-ended distance protection under different fault types. Furthermore, it proposes a method for solving the impedance of the opposite end system. The paper introduces a fault location algorithm for distribution network cables based on the power frequency additional impedance angle. This fault location method, based on the additional impedance angle, constructs the impedance equation by introducing the equivalent impedance of the line's opposite end and the additional impedance angle, fundamentally overcoming the impact of transition resistance and the equivalent impedance of the line's opposite end on the location accuracy.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Open-Circuit Fault Diagnosis in VSC-MTDC Transmission Systems Based on Passive Sliding-Mode State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper proposes a passive sliding-mode state estimator (PSMSE)-based hierarchical open-circuit fault diagnosis scheme for identifying the open-circuit fault and locating the faulty power semiconductor device in voltage source converter-based multi-terminal direct current (VSC-MTDC) transmission systems. Fault detection and isolation (FDI) is one of the most crucial processes in the VSC-MTDC operation. The energy storage function in passivity theory is constructed for analyzing the system stability and preserving the system passivity property. Then the additional inputs are designed to reshape energy and guarantee the global asymptotic convergence to the sliding surface. Four layers are established in the proposed hierarchical fault diagnosis scheme for precise fault identification and localization. The enhanced observation dynamics are provided compared with the conventional sliding-mode method because of the extra damping injections. Meanwhile, the fault detection time is also reduced with enhanced immunity. Simulation cases on healthy transient conditions and faulty conditions are executed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed PSMSE-based hierarchical open-circuit fault diagnosis scheme.

articleTitle: Analyses of Factors Affecting Transient Synchronous Stability of Grid-connected Systems with Full-power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Photovoltaic and wind turbines connected to weak grids may trigger transient synchronous stability problems under severe fault conditions due to the coupling effect between the converter output current, grid impedance and phase-locked loop (PLL), leading to out-of-step and off-grid of new energy equipment. In this paper, a nonlinear model suitable for transient synchronous stability analysis is established for the grid-connected system with full-power converter to describe the swinging process of the converter's virtual power angle; and the transient synchronous instability mechanism of the converter is analyzed with reference to the equal-area criterion (EAC), as well as the influences of the fault conditions, grid parameters, the converter's PLL parameters and output reactive current. Results show that the higher the voltage amplitude of fault point, or the larger the system short-circuit ratio (SCR), or the further the distance from the converter to the fault point, then the better the transient synchronous stability. Also, reducing the integration coefficient of the PLL, and inductive reactive power output by the converter in the initial state or during the fault period can help to increase the transient stability margin. In addition, the phase-angle jumping at the fault point is unfavorable to the transient synchronous stability in general.

articleTitle: Fault Location Method of Distribution Network Based on Improved Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Distribution network fault location is the key technology to ensure the stable operation of power system, and it is very important for the reliability and security of the system. In this paper, a fault location method of distribution network based on improved graph neural network GraphSAGE-GAT is proposed, inspired by the advantage of graph neural network to capture topological features. In this method, the topology of distribution network was transformed into an adjacency matrix, and the electrical features of fault lines were superimposed into the model. The representation of graph nodes was learned through sampling and aggregating of neighbor node information by GraphSAGE, and the multi-head attention mechanism in GAT was introduced to improve the feature characterization, and then the fault location problem was transformed into a node classification problem. Finally, the method was verified in the IEEE09 node distribution network model. The experimental results showed that GraphSAGE-GAT model has better accuracy and timeliness of fault location compared with common graph neural network models.

articleTitle: Threat Hunting Architecture for Electric Internet of Things: Redundancy, Diversity, Dynamism and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The Electric Internet of Things (E-IoT) system, as a critical information infrastructure, has become a primary target for cyber attackers, resulting in significant consequences upon compromise. Consequently, threat hunting within the E-IoT system plays a crucial role in detecting cyber threats and preventing cyber attacks. In recent decades, machine learning (ML)-based threat hunting methods have proliferated, aiming to achieve better performance and enhance security. These methods focus on analyzing the features of E-IoT equipment and predicting whether they are under attack. However, they often fall short when dealing with attacks that manipulate the output of equipment and compromise other connected devices without altering their configuration information or internal data. This paper first classifies cyber attacks into two categories: the destructive attack and the latent attack, illustrating that traditional ML-based threat hunting methods are primarily effective against the former. Subsequently, we propose the Redundancy Diversity Dynamism Machine Learning (RDD&ML) threat hunting architecture for the E-IoT system and prove that the RDD&ML architecture enhances the system's reliability. Moreover, the proposed architecture exhibits superiority over traditional ML-based methods when confronting unknown threats or attacks, as it does not rely on prior knowledge of the adversary. Experimental results on real dataset demonstrate that the RDD&ML architecture enhances the threat hunting performance of the E-IoT system.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment and Protection Methods for Overload Transmission Lines Considering Dynamic Temperature Rise Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Recently, the increasing focus on investigating the influence of transmission line temperature on power system operation has propelled the study of line temperature rise modeling into the spotlight in theoretical research areas like line equivalent parameter adjustment, safety risk assessment for line operation, and electrical-thermal coordination scheduling. The traditional temperature rise model still faces challenges in accurately describing the temperature changes along the entire line. Consequently, novel approaches such as finite element models have emerged in recent years. This article examines the two prevalent temperature rise models, scrutinizes the causes and repercussions of transmission line overloads, and outlines the risk assessment and protective strategies for mitigating line overload issues. The exploration in this domain encompasses both theoretical significance and practical engineering applicability.

articleTitle: Research on IoT Application of Power Consumption Information Collection Based on Short Message of BDS
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: To achieve the construction goal of “full coverage, full collection, and full cost control” of electricity information, addressing the challenges of power data collection and transmission in remote areas is crucial. This paper analyzes the functions and applications of the Beidou Navigation Satellite System (BDS), comparing its advantages with other remote communication methods. It proposes targeted solutions to overcome the difficulties associated with remote communication. The paper details the design of an energy data acquisition and transmission system based on Beidou communication, including a comprehensive overview of the system architecture and protocol format. It also establishes the acquisition terminal transmission system and the master terminal access system, and verifies the system's data acquisition and transmission capabilities. This work provides innovative approaches to resolving various data collection and transmission issues in remote areas.

articleTitle: Stochastic Optimization Method for the Operation of Integrated Energy Systems Under High Renewable Energy Penetration
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Integrated energy system with high renewable en-ergy penetration is an effective way to reduce carbon emissions and improve energy efficiency. However, the increase in system complexity, as well as the randomness and intermittency of wind power, have brought difficulties to the optimal scheduling of system. In order to address this challenge, this paper proposes a stochastic optimization method for integrated electricity and heat system (IEHS) based on hierarchical optimization strategy. Firstly, thermoelectric decoupling is performed for the integrated energy system, and then establish thermal network balance model and optimal power flow model of power system. Considering the randomness of wind power output, the quasi-Monte Carlo method is introduced to solve economic and stable operating parameters; Subsequently, the bacterial foraging optimization algorithm (BFOA) with better global search ability is used as the solution algorithm of the model; Numerical simulations show that the proposed method can significantly improve the system's ability to resist random interference and operate economically.

articleTitle: Visualization Analysis of Substation Ventilation Research Based on Bibliometrics
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the continuous growth of electricity demand and the expansion of grid scale, the safety and reliability of substations, as an important part of the power system, have received increasing attention. This study employs bibliometric analysis, using CiteSpace and VOSviewer tools, to systematically analyze the research status, hotspots, and trends in the field of substation ventilation. Through quantitative analysis of 130 papers from the Web of Science core collection from 2001 to 2024, the study reveals the research dynamics and main research directions in this field. The findings indicate that research interest and activities in the field of substation ventilation have shown a growing trend year by year, especially after 2016, with a significant increase in annual publications. Additionally, China holds a significant position in this field, although the average citation rate of papers is low, suggesting that the quality of publications needs improvement. Research hotspots mainly focus on numerical simulation technology, ventilation and noise control, as well as intelligent ventilation cooling and energy saving. This study provides a reference for understanding the research progress, hotspots, and trends in the field of substation ventilation.

articleTitle: Research and Energy-Saving Analysis of Hybrid Power System Retrofit for Marine Engineering Vessels
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Since the Copenhagen Climate Change Conference, global concern over carbon emissions has been steadily increasing. In response to this goal, the vessel “Marine Petroleum 257” underwent an electric system hybrid power retrofit to enhance fuel efficiency and reduce carbon emissions. This paper first introduces the structure and operation mode of the target vessel before the retrofit, followed by a detailed explanation of the hybrid power retrofit plan, including the installation and debugging of intelligent energy efficiency data acquisition systems and hybrid power equipment based on lithium iron phosphate battery packs. A hybrid power system energy management strategy is proposed based on charging and discharging tests of on-board energy storage batteries. Using maximum fuel savings from a single charge-discharge cycle as the evaluation criterion, with the main diesel engine shaft power and shaft-driven generator active power as decision variables, considerations include ship power supply balance, main diesel engine power output constraints, and the reliability of the power system. In the MATLAB environment, energy allocation is optimized using an improved Hippo optimization algorithm. The results indicate that this strategy can effectively save fuel and holds promising practical applications.

articleTitle: WPMamba: Enhanced Wind Power Forecasting Model Based on Mamba with Weather Forecast Data
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: As global warming intensifies, the development of wind energy becomes increasingly important. Given the inherent unpredictability of wind, there is a growing demand for sophisticated forecasting techniques to better incorporate wind energy into the existing power grid. Previous studies mostly relied on historical data to predict power generation without considering future climate conditions. These methods were only effective for short-term predictions, not for long-term predictions. To address the aforementioned issues, future weather forecast information is incorporated into the traditional framework within the paper. According to the new framework, a novel network model named WPMamba is proposed for predicting the output power of wind farm based on the Mamba model. Concurrently, a data preprocessing method, specifically tailored for wind power forecasting (WPF), is also introduced in this paper. Experiments show that the proposed WPMamba model demonstrates convincing performance in short-term, medium-term and long-term WPF tasks, achieving significant performance advantages over existing models. The ablation experiments also demonstrate that the introduction of future weather forecast information and our proposed data processing method can both enhance the model's forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: Day-Ahead Optimal Scheduling Study of a Combined Water-Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to cope with the future large-scale renewable energy with stochasticity, volatility and intermittency, the joint operation of flexible energy storage and renewable energy needs to be promoted on the basis of taking into account the operation of existing hydropower units, so as to realise the safe and economic integration of renewable energy into the grid. Aiming at the above problems, this paper constructs a day-ahead optimal scheduling model for the joint operation system of water-wind-photovoltaic-storage, using the fast regulating ability of battery storage and the regulating ability of pumped storage power plant to form a complementa-ry system, and solves the problem with the Yalmip optimisation toolbox to obtain the day-ahead optimal scheduling results of the joint system under various operating scenarios. The results show that the fast regulation capability of the storage battery can effectively complement the regulation capability of the pumped storage power station, improve the operating economy of the combined system, reduce the cost of pollution control in the system, and improve the stability of power output.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Fast DC Fault Current Limiter Prototype
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the rapid development of the DC distribution network, the method of limiting the rapid rise of current after a short-circuit fault on the DC side has become a research hotspot. This paper proposes a new DC fault current limiter (FCL) topology and its prototype design scheme. The topology converts DC into AC through the IGBT bridge during fault and uses the characteristics of low-frequency resistance and high frequency of reactor to limit current. Secondly, this paper optimizes the main equipment parameters of the proposed FCL prototype, selects the current limiting reactance, Hall sensor, drive plate and arrester, and uses AutoCAD to design the appearance and overall layout of the current limiting prototype. At the same time, the hardware and software of the control and protection system are designed. Based on the RS232 serial port, the software program communicates with the host computer to analyze the operating state of the current limiter under normal operation and fault period. Finally, the reliability and superiority of the FCL control system and current limiting characteristics proposed in this paper are verified by comparing the experiment with the RT-LAB semi-physical simulation data.

articleTitle: Design and Application of the Coordinated Regulation System for Distributed Hydro-PV Complementation Combined with Load Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous increase of the installed capacity of distributed PV systems, the issue of county-level power grids lacking of technical management and control methods of distributed energy sources has been acquired more and more attentions. It has also been noticed that a large number of scattered small hydro-power stations do not play an important role during peaking operation. Aiming at the coordinated management and control of distributed small hydro-power stations, PV systems, demand-side flexible resources, a coordinated regulation system for distributed hydro-PV complementation combined with load resources has been developed. The system includes three major functional modules: a resources aggregation module, an output forecast module, and a coordinated optimization regulation module. Therefore the system has capability of coordinated optimizing and making full, efficient utilization of various resources, inclusive of small hydro-power stations, PV systems, energy storage systems, and user-side flexible loads. The system was demonstrated in Hunan Province, and the demonstration results showed that the system can effectively improve the peaking capability of the power grid, promote the consumption level of clean energy, and lower the energy cost for users, and also provide a new resolution to enhance the grid's flexibility and reliability.

articleTitle: A Review of Emerging Trends in Wind Power Forecasting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The global demand for renewable energy is growing gradually, with wind energy accounting for 25-30% of the renewable energy sector by 2023, and accurate wind power prediction technology plays a key role in the process of grid-connecting wind power. This paper provides a comprehensive review of recent advancements in wind power forecasting, focusing on the usage scenarios and performance comparisons of different prediction models. Starting from physical and statistical models, the main prediction methods were analyzed, and their advantages and limitations in practical applications were discussed. And introduced a combination model based on data preprocessing, model optimization, and error compensation, discussing the complementary advantages and high prediction accuracy between different models. Afterwards, based on the needs of wind power forecasting research, suggestions for improving the accuracy of wind power forecasting were proposed from three aspects: enhancing the accuracy of NWP data, optimizing combined pre-test models, and improving the prediction accuracy for wind power ramping events. This review provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners to advance the development of wind power forecasting technologies.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Storage Capacity and System Economic Operation of Thermal Power Units Considering Electricity-Carbon Coupling Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: As the global energy transition accelerates, thermal power units, as representatives of traditional energy, face the dual challenges of reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency. This study aims to explore optimization of energy storage capacity and system economic operation of thermal power units considering electricity-carbon coupling constraints. The impact of the electricity-carbon coupling mechanism on the operation of thermal power units is analyzed. Then, a multi- objective optimization model that comprehensively considers economic and environmental benefits is constructed. The non- dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) is employed to solve the above model. Based on the obtained pareto front, the potential impact of the battery energy storage systems (BESS) on the operational efficiency and carbon emissions of thermal power units is evaluated. The results show that a 14.27% BESS capacity ratio of the thermal power units can significantly improve the operational flexibility of thermal power units, reduce operating costs, and decrease carbon emissions. The rise in carbon prices corresponds to the increase in power generation costs for thermal power units, which may weaken their competitiveness and profitability. A series of operation strategies for thermal power units based on the electricity-carbon coupling mechanism is proposed, providing practical guidance for achieving low-carbon and efficient operation of thermal power units.

articleTitle: Dynamic Aggregation Strategy of Virtual Power Plants Considering the Adjustable Ability Recovery Process and Dependencies of Distributed Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: For the aggregation process of distributed resources into a Virtual Power Plant (VPP) to respond to grid dispatching, this paper proposes a dynamic aggregation strategy considering the adjustable ability recovery process and dependencies of distributed resources (DRs). By analyzing the benefits of the recovery process of DRs and the dependencies of adjustable abilities among DRs, the economic efficiency and reliability of flexible resource aggregation are effectively improved. Firstly, an economic optimization-based aggregation strategy considering the recovery process is proposed. Predictive control is used to solve the economic benefits of each DR during the power response recovery process under optimal operation. Aggregation is then performed using the optimal benefits of each DR. After that, a dependency-based predictive screening strategy is proposed. The Gaussian copula function is used to establish the dependencies among DRs, predict the adjustable power of each DR under different dispatch states, and screen the optimal economic aggregation results, effectively improving the reliability of the response. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified using actual data from 247 charging stations in Shenzhen.

articleTitle: Energy Block Pool-Based Two-Stage Clearing Model for Electricity Spot Market
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to satisfy the diverse transaction demands of multiple energy resources and players, and to improve the operational efficiency of the temporal bidding-based electricity spot market, it is urgent to design clearing mechanisms for the electricity spot market that take into account diversification, standardization and flexibility. To solve this problem, in this paper, the clearing models for energy block pool-based electricity spot market are established. First, four types of energy blocks are introduced, and their mathematical models are established according to their physical-economic characteristics. Next, the concept of energy block pool is proposed, and the day-ahead and real-time clearing model of energy block pool-based electricity spot market is established. Moreover, the cost-benefit settlement methods of different energy blocks are given. Finally, the numerical simulations are carried out in the IEEE-9 bus system with fourteen energy blocks. It shows that the established two-stage clearing model is effective. The differentiated characteristics and transaction demands of the four types of energy blocks can be satisfied.

articleTitle: An Overview and Prospect of Artificial Intelligence Applied in Electricity Spot Market
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Under the “double carbon” strategic goal, the development of distributed energy facilities aims to drive further reform in China's electricity spot market. However, electricity spot market participants face increasingly complex and challenging issues in power trading. At the same time, AI has shown its broad prospects in the field of new energy power system operation and control, but also in the electricity spot market transactions to show its strong vitality. This paper generally reviews the research of AI in the field of electricity spot market trading and gives its broad prospects. This paper focuses on analysing more than a dozen literatures in this field in the last two years and draws timelines and tables to illustrate the research progress. Firstly, this paper summarises the electricity spot market structure and its current problems. Secondly, this paper summarizes and compares the applications of three key technologies in electricity spot market trading: traditional machine learning and AI semantic large models, reinforcement learning-assisted decision-making, and meteorological large models. Finally, this paper envisions the application of AI in electricity spot market trading through the development of AI large model electricity platforms, offering a cutting-edge research direction in future. In summary, this paper helps relevant researchers to carry out work on AI applications in the area of electricity spot market.

articleTitle: Research on Heat Load Prediction Model of Secondary Network Based on Improved Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In this note, a new ICEEMDAN-KPCA-LSTM heat load prediction model is proposed to address the current problem that heat supply enterprises adopt the regulation of crude heat supply, which leads to the mismatch between the heat supply and the heat required by users. The model utilizes ICEEMDAN to decompose the sequence of environmental factors and reduce its non-stationarity; KPCA is used to extract the main influencing variables of the feature sequence and reduce the input dimension. Meanwhile, in order to accurately forecast the heating load of the heating system, the LSTM network is used for dynamic modeling of the multiple characteristic sequences. Experiments indicate that this model has better forecasting precision than conventional methods, and it is possible to optimize system adjustment strategy and energy saving operation. In this paper, a new heat load forecasting model is put forward, which can be used as a reference for the management and operation of thermal power plants.

Author Keywords: long- and short-term memory neural networks

articleTitle: A Cycle Consistent Dual-Domain Transformer Framework for Detection of Partial Discharge
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Over the past decade, scholarly inquiries have delved into the critical issue of insulation failure attributed to partial discharge (PD) phenomena in overhead transmission lines with insulated conductors, as well as in electrical apparatus such as generators and motors across various sectors. The development of a proficient PD detection framework could result in considerable maintenance savings and avert electricity supply interruptions. Conventional techniques depend on manually curated features and sector-specific knowledge for the identification of PD patterns within electrical currents. Recent advancements have seen a surge in the proposition of data-driven, deep learning methodologies aimed at obviating the need for these bespoke feature extractions. Nonetheless, these innovative approaches predominantly analyze data either in the time or frequency domain. A significant body of research has been dedicated to producing phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) patterns from unprocessed PD sensor data, extracting pivotal attributes of these patterns to furnish a visual diagnostic tool for exhaustive defect analysis. PRPD diagrams infer a linkage between PD events within the positive and negative half-cycles of an alternating electrical waveform. This inter-cycle correlation, however, has not been thoroughly investigated in deep learning strategies. The present study introduces an innovative feature fusion model, termed Dual-Trans Net, designed to harness time, frequency, and phase domain features for unified learning within a singular framework. An empirical evaluation of our framework, employing a publicly available dataset from high-frequency voltage sensors for the identification of compromised power lines, has culminated in a leading-edge Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) score of 0.7830.

articleTitle: EVCS Optimal Planning Based on Dynamic Traffic Network Charging Demand Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of mismatch between charging demand and supply caused by the rapid growth of electric vehicles (EV), and alleviate the problem of charging difficulty during peak travel hours, it is urgent to accelerate the reasonable construction of electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) and form a perfect EVCS network. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-objective EVCS optimal planning model considering the spatio-temporal distribution prediction of charging demand. The model takes the comprehensive cost, user dissatisfaction and voltage fluctuation as the objective function, and realizes the tripartite benefit trade-off between investors, EV users and grid company. Finally, the model is applied to the second ring road area of Kunming, Yunnan province, and fast convergence multi-objective equilibrium optimizer equipped with archive evolution path mechanism (FC-MOEO/AEP) algorithm is used to optimize the solution to verify the effectiveness and feasibility of the model.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Threshold of Current-Carrying Capacity Considering the Efficiency and Reliability of Overhead Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The capacity of overhead transmission lines to carry current is a crucial parameter for evaluating their load-bearing capability, directly impacting the need for dynamic capacity expansion, which is essential for the stable operation of the power system. In addition to the inherent characteristics of the conductors, the current carrying capacity of overhead lines is closely linked to local meteorological conditions. This research utilizes a K-means algorithm-based approach to assess the current carrying capacity of overhead transmission lines. Initially, historical data undergo statistical analysis, and monthly meteorological data similarities are used to partition time periods using the K-Means algorithm with appropriate boundary conditions. Subsequent simulation calculations employing the Morgan formula aim to maximize line transmission capacity while ensuring stable and secure operation, assessing operational stability to enhance the safety of overhead transmission lines.

articleTitle: Bi-Level Capacity Optimization of Microgrid Considering Orderly Charging and Discharging Strategies for Electric Vehicles in a Power-Carbon Market Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With the increased penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) in communities, the negative impacts of vehicle charging on the power system have gradually increased. To enlarge the EV charging carrying capacity of the community grid, this paper proposes a bi-level capacity configuration strategy for community microgrid (MG) in a Power-Carbon market environment. The upper-level model allocates capacity with the objectives of highest MG reliability, minimum comprehensive operating cost and minimum carbon emission, while the lower-level model optimizes the scheduling strategy with the objectives of minimum weighted operating cost and minimum charging cost for EV users. First, the real-time price is used to guide the residents' electricity consumption behavior to be more adaptive to the uncertainty of renewable energy sources and to ensure that the community MG has sufficient resilient capacity. Second, based on the alternative storage effect of EVs, EVs are integrated with storage batteries and participate in ancillary services. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a simulation case.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Power System Energy Storage Operation Configuration Based on Multi-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: In the context of the “carbon neutrality” goal, future power systems will inevitably rely on a high percentage of renewable energy. However, since the output power of renewable energy systems is highly stochastically volatile, this will have a big impact on the real-time balance of the system. To ensure the real-time balance of power system output power with a high percentage of renewable energy sources, optimize the power distribution plan, and increase economic efficiency, we first propose a control method to enhance the operational stability of wind turbines by controlling the system power, frequency regulation, and optimal load shedding operation under random wind conditions. Second, the Robust Multiple Reserve Scheduling (RMRS) model is established to optimize the energy storage configuration. This model enables decision-makers to make optimization decisions from a multi-objective perspective by simultaneously optimizing multiple subsystems. The Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Decomposition (MOEA/D) algorithm is then employed to achieve an optimal balance among the different objectives, providing decision-makers with a range of feasible trade-off solutions. Finally, a case study conducted on IEEE30 nodes validates the effectiveness and practical application value of the proposed model in efficiently optimizing power system configurations.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Non-Zero Crossing Switching of AC Filters on Controllable Line Commutated Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) technology based on Line Commutated Converter (LCC) is widely used in long-distance power transmission due to high efficiency and low power loss. AC filters are equipped in HVDC project to eliminate the harmonics and support reactive power for converter units, but the non-zero cross switching of the filters may lead fluctuations and distortions in the AC bus voltage, causing HVDC power disturbances, and even commutation failure. To address this issue, phase-selective breaker controller, commutation failure prevention, Gamma-kick control, and low voltage current limiting (VDCOL) strategies are applied, while those methods can only reduce the risk and cannot completely avoid commutation failure. The literature proposes a Controllable Line Commutated Converter (CLCC) based on fully controlled IGBT and semi-controlled thyristor hybrid connection, which avoids commutation failure through topological innovation. The related research mainly focus on the commutation failure caused by AC faults, while lack of corresponding research on the impact of the AC filter switching on CLCC. This paper analyzes the structure and working principle of CLCC, and discusses the system impact of LCC and CLCC when the AC filter is switching at the non-zero point. The performance of CLCC in resisting filter switching disturbances is verified by PSCAD, revealing the influence mechanism of non-zero point closure on the commutation process, and proposing optimization strategies, providing guidance for the safe and stable operation of high voltage transmission systems.

articleTitle: Natural Ice-Melting Mechanism of Wind Turbine Blades in Hilly and Mountainous Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Wind energy resources are abundant in cold mountainous areas, where wind farms are predominantly situated in hilly terrains characterized by high altitude and low temperatures, leading to significant atmospheric liquid water content (LWC) and heightened susceptibility of wind turbine blades to icing. This study aims to analyze the ice-melting mechanism of wind turbine blades under natural conditions, leveraging winter meteorological observations from the Hubei Jieshan Wind Farm. A mathematical model of blade ice-melting is developed based on heat transfer theory, incorporating considerations of ice-water phase transitions and the effects of elevation-induced air pressure variations in hilly regions. The influence of wind speed and ambient temperature on ice melting is studied through finite element simulation by calculating the temperature distribution of the blade. Comparison and validation with experimental results further establish the relationship between blade temperature distribution and environmental conditions during ice-melting. Findings indicate that the leading edge of the blade exhibits the highest temperature, while the middle section experiences the lowest. Ice-melting dynamics are significantly influenced by wind speed, with varying effects across different temperature ranges: Between temperatures of -3°C to 0°C, increased wind speeds correspond to greater ice thickness and accelerated ice accumulation rates. Conversely, within the range of 0°C to 4°C, higher wind speeds result in reduced ice thickness and heightened ice melting rates. For wind farms situated in boundary mountainous regions as described, complete ice-melting occurs at a blade temperature of 3°C, reducing surface ice thickness to zero.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Electricity Price Prediction: LDS-GRU Algorithm for Long-Tail Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: As China's electricity spot trading market evolves, accurate electricity price forecasting has become crucial for optimizing power system operations and reducing costs and risks for market participants. Traditional forecasting methods struggle with the nonlinear and volatile nature of electricity prices, particularly with extreme values or long-tail effects. This paper proposes an advanced forecasting method that integrates the Label Distribution Smoothing (LDS) algorithm with the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model, termed LDS-GRU, to enhance prediction accuracy by addressing long-tail effects. We conduct an empirical analysis of intraday electricity prices in the Guangdong power market for 2023, revealing significant time-domain characteristics and variability in price distributions. By segmenting the data into 24 hourly models and applying LDS for preprocessing, our approach demonstrates substantial improvements in forecasting performance compared to traditional GRU models. The findings underscore the importance of accounting for extreme price values and provide a more accurate solution for electricity price forecasting, with clear guidance for market traders.

articleTitle: MG-MetaDETR: Marrying Muti-Scale and Grouping Strategy With DETR for Few-Shot Insulator Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Insulator defects pose a significant risk to the safe operation of transmission lines and can potentially lead to serious hazards within the power system. While UAV inspection technology has gradually replaced manual inspection of transmission lines due to its cost-effectiveness and efficiency, the limited number of samples for detecting insulator anomalies necessitates the development of a few-shot object detection algorithm with robust generalization capabilities, accuracy, and efficiency for effective power grid operation and maintenance. This paper presents the construction of a few-shot private dataset of insulator defects, based on insulator defect images obtained from a provincial power grid company during the period of 2020–2023. Secondly, the paper introduces a few-shot learning model, MG-MetaDETR, which is based on a multi-scale and grouping strategy for insulator defect detection. The proposed model leverages the end-to-end Transformer architecture DETR to streamline the object detection process. Additionally, it introduces the use of the multi-scale backbone network Res2Net-101 to enhance the detection of small target insulators. Finally, the paper employs a label grouping strategy to expedite the convergence of the model. The precision and recall rates of this method are reported as 72.4% and 75.4%, respectively, based on 50 training samples of each type.

articleTitle: Distributed Optimal Voltage Control in Large-Scale PV Power Stations Considering Q-V Droop Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: For large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power stations, the voltage drop in the internal collecting power lines is significant. The fluctuation in PV power outputs might lead to system-wide voltage violations, necessitating voltage optimal control. Considering that traditional centralized control faces significant communication burdens, a distributed optimal voltage control strategy is proposed. In terms of constructing the optimization model, the influences of Q-V droop characteristics from PV generation units are considered. Accordingly, the segmented linearized Q-V droop curve is formulated as a set of mixed integer linear constraints, embedded into the optimal voltage control model. The alternating direction multiplier method (ADMM) is employed to provide a distributed-solving approach. Particularly, asynchronous updating is taken to enhance the ADMM performances when encountering communication delays. Numerical analysis in case studies is conducted to validate the applicability of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Optimization Scheduling Strategy For Active Distribution Network With Multiple Microgrids Using Energy Router
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Distribution networks (DNs) with the multiple microgrids (MGs) are becoming increasingly common. However, the transmission of MGs is relatively complex and expensive. As a multi-port device, the energy router (ER) can control power transmission. Thus, this paper proposes a hierarchical optimization strategy for the management of ER-controlled multiple MGs in the DN. On the one hand, a structure of multiple MGs in the DN is established, based on the structure and functions of the ER, laying the structural foundation for the following. On the other hand, a hierarchical operation optimization strategy is proposed to minimize power losses and maximize economic benefits. In the energy optimization of the ER, the Alternative Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is used to determine the optimal operating state of each MG at the port in a distributed manner. Finally, an improved IEEE-33 system is utilized for numerical simulation. The results demonstrate that this strategy can improve the performance in the DN, reduce the total operating costs of multiple MGs, and fully capitalize on the benefits of multiple MGs resources.

articleTitle: Research on Modular Inverter Control Technology of Dual Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Using medium-voltage DC transmission instead of traditional three-phase AC transmission can significantly reduce cable losses. However, high DC bus voltages pose challenges for voltage equalization across inverter modules. This paper proposes a topology for a modular dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) inverter, and studies its dual closed-loop vector control and modular inverter voltage equalization control strategies. By using a series connection of inverters and three-phase decoupled PWM technology for individual control of inverter modules, a modular inverter series bus voltage equalization control strategy is established. Compared to parallel modular inverter, it can further reduce voltage fluctuations and enhance the dynamic performance of the motor. Simulation has verified the performance of the motor operation based on this control strategy, demonstrating that this method can achieve effective voltage equalization.

Author Keywords: Dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Spline Global MPPT with PID Controller Based on Levy Invasive Weed Technique for Renewable Energy Resources of Smart Homes
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Renewable energy systems, particularly photovoltaic (PV) systems, have been played important role in the reducing carbon emissions. A primary concern in the field of photovoltaics (PV) based on the design of the maximum power point tracking (MPPT) is the capacity to accurately monitor power across many parameters in addition to ascertain the power production of solar cells or wind turbines and adjust the load to maximise power efficiency under varying weather conditions. On another hands, the hybrid smart system uses a wind catcher to reduce the amount of energy consumed by buildings from the grid, which is a historically significant architectural component for cross ventilation and passive cooling. This paper presents an updating of model that proposes improvements to the regulation of Spline MPPT with tuning PID controller by using Levy Invasive Weed optimization (LIWO)technique. A rapid, accurate, and straightforward approach for determining the (MPPT) of PV systems under consistent irradiation and partial shade, as well as wind turbines, is presented using the Spline- MPPT technique. The model of this paper employs LIWO in conjunction with a PID controller to improve the selection of PID gains. Moreover, is applied to generate the optimal values of duty cycle of the model. The comprehensive system design depicted has been simulated using MATLAB Simulink to verify the functionality of the system. The model has attained an accuracy of 93%. The outcomes of this model contribute greatly to our understanding of the suitability and efficacy of both AI and traditional MPPT controllers. This modeling will be beneficial to the renewable energy industry.

articleTitle: Extraction of Parasitic Inductance of Laminated Bus Bar of High Frequency Inverter Arc Welding Power Supply Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Inverter arc welding power supplies use higher switching frequency, which puts more stringent requirements on the design of the parasitic parameters of the commutation circuit. In inverter arc welding power supplies, stray inductance can cause various problems such as surge voltage and switching losses. These problems lead to improper operation and increased levels of electromagnetic interference (EMI) in inverter arc welding power supplies. Laminated bus bars can achieve mutual inductance cancellation and are considered a good way to minimize stray inductance. Current research on laminated bus bar mainly focuses on the effect of current path on parasitic inductance, and there is little research on the combination of genetic algorithm to extract its parasitic inductance and the effect of electromagnetic field on its parasitic inductance. In this paper, for the 50 kHz/20 kW inverter arc welding power supply, a laminated bus bar with integrated DC capacitor, soft-start circuit, IGBT module, and three-phase rectifier module is designed, and the numerical calculation of quasi-static electromagnetic field is carried out by using ANSYS Q3D to extract the parasitic parameter matrix, and the multi-port circuit model of the laminated bus bar is established.
