The impedance frequency characteristics and switching characteristics of the laminated bus bar are measured and simulated by impedance resonance method and genetic algorithm, and the parasitic inductance of the laminated bus bar is extracted, which confirms the accuracy of the laminated bus bar modeling.

articleTitle: Optimization of Multi-scenario Distributed Generation Considering Voltage Sag
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Considering the fluctuation and uncertainty of distributed generation (DG) output and its impact on the distribution network, how to reasonably plan the access scheme of DG is one of the current research focuses. The combination of K-means clustering algorithm (K-mean) and Adaptive and Fast Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (AF -DBSCAN) is employed to realize more efficient scenario reduction. The voltage sag economic loss evaluation index of sensitive loads considering multi-scenario is proposed to further reflect the impact of DG output uncertainty on voltage sag of sensitive loads. A mathematical model for capacity optimal configuration of DG is established by taking voltage stability, active power loss, and voltage sag economic loss of sensitive loads as the optimization objectives. The sparrow search algorithm is used to solve the mathematical model, and the fuzzy matter-element evaluation method is adopted to evaluate the Pareto optimal set and finally obtain the optimal access scheme. The simulation results of the IEEE 33-bus distribution system show that the reasonable access of DG helps to improve the overall system voltage stability as well as reduce the system network loss and economic loss, which verifies the rationality and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration Method of High-Rate Characteristic Energy Storage Battery Based on Wind Level Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Aiming at the application scenario of energy storage to stabilize wind power fluctuations, a method for optimal configuration of energy storage batteries is proposed in consideration of high rate characteristics. Use the net present value method to construct an economic model that considers life cycle costs and operating process benefits. Analyze the impact of the energy storage battery rate characteristics on the available capacity, consider the life weight factor, and establish a method for calculating the operating life of the energy storage under high-rate charge/discharge based on the throughput energy. With the goal of optimal energy storage battery economy, the optimal rate configuration is found, so as to form an energy storage configuration plan that meets the technical and economic characteristics. The simulation analysis of a wind farm energy storage capacity configuration example verifies the effectiveness and economic value of the configuration method.

articleTitle: Non-characteristic Harmonic Analysis of CLCC-HVDC System
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: State Grid Shanghai Municipal Electric Power Company proposes a new type of controllable grid phase shifting converter CLCC, which adopts a hybrid design of converter valves to improve the stability of high-voltage direct current transmission system operation. Aiming at the problem of non-characteristic harmonic currents generated by controllable grid phase-change converter, firstly, we theoretically introduce the principle of CLCC model, analyze the reasons for the generation of non-characteristic harmonic currents in the system, and put forward the scheme of filtering by improving the existing STATCOM device. PSCAD software is used as a platform to establish a simulation model and design cases to calculate and analyze the non-characteristic harmonic currents. The simulation results show that when the converter trigger angle is unbalanced, it has the greatest influence on the system net-side non-characteristic harmonic current, and the proposed STATCOM improvement measures have better non-characteristic harmonic suppression effect.

articleTitle: Research on Power Transmission Line Fault Diagnosis Based on Transformer-BiGRU
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Efficient and accurate identification and diagnosis are of paramount importance to the development of modern power systems. This paper proposes a fault diagnosis method that integrates Transformer and BiGRU models. The Transformer model processes input sequences in parallel, employing self-attention mechanisms to prioritize the identification of critical features. Bidirectional GRU (BiGRU) processes the data sequentially from both the past to the future and future to the past, comprehensively capturing bidirectional temporal dependencies within the fault data. It addresses a limitation of the Transformer in this context, thereby compensating for its deficiency. By means of feature engineering, this paper successfully extracts 11-dimensional time-domain features, which are consequently fed into the Transformer-BiGRU model for the purposes of fault identification and classification. Experimental verification indicates that this model possesses accurate fault detection and classification abilities. The overall fault recognition accuracy amounts to 98.84%, and the recognition accuracy for five types of faults reaches 100%. In comparison with three traditional machine learning methods, namely CNN, LSTM, and SVM, it exhibits more superior performance.

articleTitle: Temperature Field Analysis and Optimal Design of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Motor Based on Fluid-Solid Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: With its compact spatial structure and high power density, the axial flux permanent magnet motor is suitable for specialized applications but also imposes higher cooling requirements. It necessitates a well-designed rotor cooling structure to ensure reliable motor operation. This paper uses a 7kW dual-stator single-rotor axial flux permanent magnet motor as an example. Based on the principle of fluid-solid coupling, the motor's three-dimensional fluid field and temperature field models are established to study the impact of different rotor structures on the motor's heat dissipation capability. The research results indicate that the permanent magnets exhibit the highest temperature rise in a dual-stator single-rotor axial flux permanent magnet motor. By more effectively agitating the air around the permanent magnets and increasing the heat dissipation area of the permanent magnets, the motor's cooling capacity can be improved. Specifically, thinning the rotor support structure can effectively suppress the temperature rise of the permanent magnets.

articleTitle: Review of Live Measurement for Power Frequency Parameters of Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The live measurement of line parameters (LMLPs) has great application prospects. However, up to now, the application of LMLPs in engineering is very rare. In view of this problem, the paper analyzes the influencing factors of the accuracy of LMLPs, and puts forward that the error of measuring small signal by VT and CT should be paid attention to. The signal increment method and non-power frequency method are the two main methods for LMLPs. Combined with the non-power frequency method, signal increment method can further resist strong electromagnetic interference and improve the measurement accuracy. It is feasible to generate large zero sequence signals by operatng the single-phase circuit breaker on line, and there is no overvoltage and safety risk. Finally, the problems to be solved in the popularization and application of LMLPs are summarized: improving the power of the test power supply, miniaturization and light weight; clarifying the small signal measurement accuracy of VT and CT, and quantifying the system error of LMLPs. The corresponding suggestions are given, which provides a technical reference for the popularization and application of live line parameter measurement.

articleTitle: The Equivalent Method for Wind Power Units Considering the Power Characteristic Differences of Units Under Low-Voltage Ride-Through
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: Considering the increasing penetration of doubly-fed wind farms, a simplification method is proposed for clustering the DFIG units in the stability analysis of the power system. Moreover, the low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) process is taken into account and the power characteristics of the units are considered as a basis for the clustering. First, the control strategy during LVRT is analyzed to achieve a mathematical representation of the output power characteristics of the DFIG units. Then, by examining the differences in dynamic power characteristics among the units, the ability to restore steady-state active power to pre-fault levels is used as the criterion for initial clustering. After that, the units are clustered for equivalence based on an improved D-K clustering method. Finally, power curves and error levels are compared between the proposed and alternative methods using five measured wind speed scenarios. Simulation and calculation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively improve the accuracy of the equivalent model.

articleTitle: Numeric Study of Conventional Generators Strategic Bidding With Reliability Pricing Model Demand Curve in a Renewable-Integrated Capacity Market
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The growth of renewable energy has disrupted energy markets, reducing profitability for conventional generators by lowering prices. Capacity markets have emerged to address this, offering stable revenue streams. This paper presents a numeric study for a capacity market that integrates RES and conventional generators, analysing how costs and bidding strategies affect market outcomes. A case study using the IEEE 6-bus system highlights the impact of cost variations and the role of zero-bid strategies in securing capacity market participation. The results emphasize cost efficiency and strategic bidding as critical for conventional generators' profitability in competitive, RES-driven markets.

articleTitle: Improved Three-Region Moisture Migration Model for Calculating the Ampacity of 220 kV Submarine Cables Buried in Tidal Flats
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: The accurate calculation of current-carrying capability (ampacity) in submarine cables is essential for ensuring their safe operation. This paper proposes an improved three-region finite element (FEM) model to accurately calculate the ampacity of 220 kV three-core AC submarine cables buried in tidal flats, with a specific focus on moisture migration effects. First, the impact of different soil thermal resistivity coefficients on the critical temperature location was thoroughly investigated. Based on the observed characteristics of critical temperature changes, a novel three-region submarine cable ampacity calculation model that incorporates moisture migration was developed. The study further examines the influence of varying external soil thermal resistivity, burial depth, and air temperature on the ampacity. The results reveal that soil thermal resistivity significantly influences the position of the critical temperature point, which shifts farther from the cable center as the thermal resistivity increases. The proposed improved three-region model more accurately simulates the impact of actual soil moisture migration on the cable temperature field by finely dividing the thermal domain around the cable. This model demonstrates superior accuracy and applicability compared to the IEC 60287 standard calculation methods. This research provides a robust theoretical foundation for accurately calculating the ampacity of submarine cables in tidal flat environments, which is crucial for ensuring their safe operation and extending their service life.

articleTitle: A Defense Strategy Against False Data Injection Attack in Smart Grid Based on Multi-Stage Game*
publicationTitle: 2024 The 9th International Conference on Power and Renewable Energy (ICPRE)
abstract: This paper addresses the critical issue of false data injection attacks (FDIA) in smart grids by proposing a novel multi-stage dynamic attack and defense game model. This model not only accounts for the possibility of multiple attacks occurring in a short time frame but also enables the derivation of optimal defense strategies by solving the Nash equilibrium point. The significance of this research lies in its ability to enhance the reliability and security of smart grids against increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks. Through simulations on the IEEE 14 bus system, the effectiveness of the proposed multi-stage game model is demonstrated, showing superior performance over single-stage models in mitigating the impact of FDIAs.
